effect_claim_quote: All were able to independently identify the objects at 1-month follow-up.
replication_target_quote: The aims were to support the findings of Muldoon and Gray (2023) by significantly increasing the number of vocabulary targets
outcome_quote: Receptive object identification improved significantly for both participants.
review_note: Clinic-based, individualized follow-up of the preschool procedure; two children versus three in the original.

original_title: The BIAS map: Behaviors from intergroup affect and stereotypes.
replication_title: Emotions as mediators of the stereotype–discrimination relationship: A BIAS map replication
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
effect_name: BIAS-map emotion mediation
effect_claim: Warmth and competence stereotypes relate to behavioral tendencies toward groups partly through intergroup emotions.
effect_claim_quote: Emotions predict behavioral tendencies more strongly than stereotypes do and usually mediate stereotype-to-behavioral-tendency links.
replication_target_quote: none have tested them by replicating the original study (Cuddy, Fiske, & Glick, 2007, Study 1).
outcome_quote: However, for each of the four behavior outcomes the effect of stereotype content was mediated through one emotion rather than two as predicted by the BIAS map.
review_note: Norwegian Study 1 replication supports emotion mediation but finds one mediator per outcome, rather than the original two-mediator pattern.

original_title: On the Dual Nature of Extraversion
replication_title: The dual nature of extraversion: A replication
original_journal: British Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology
effect_name: Sociability and impulsiveness components of extraversion
effect_claim: Extraversion questionnaire items form related sociability and impulsiveness components under factor analysis.
effect_claim_quote: sociability and impulsiveness do emerge as separate traits, correlating about 0–5 with each other in two independent samples.
replication_target_quote: A replication of a study by Eysenck & Eysenck confirms their finding that Extraversion items from the M.P.I, and elsewhere produce two clusters when factor analysed.
outcome_quote: The common characteristics of the clusters are sociability and impulsiveness respectively.
review_note: Factor structure finding only; the original also discussed unitary extraversion and independence from adjustment.

original_title: Machiavellianism and Dating: Deception and Intimacy
replication_title: Digging in the Dark Triad: A Replication of ``Machiavellianism and Dating: Deception and Intimacy''
original_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
effect_name: Machiavellianism and dating deception
effect_claim: Higher Machiavellianism scores are associated with greater self-reported use of deceptive tactics to attract dating partners.
effect_claim_quote: Higher scores on Machiavellianism were associated with greater likelihood of using deceptive tactics and lower levels of relationship intimacy.
replication_target_quote: The present study is a replication and an extension of Dussault, Hojjat, and Boone (2013).
outcome_quote: The results support the positive association between Machiavellianism and the use of deceptive dating strategies
review_note: The deceptive-tactics association held; the separate original intimacy association was not detected.

original_title: Improving social norms interventions: Rank-framing increases excessive alcohol drinkers’ information-seeking.
replication_title: Replication of a Rank-Framed Social Norms Experiment
effect_name: Rank-framed alcohol norms and information seeking
effect_claim: Showing excessive drinkers their drinking rank among peers increases requests for alcohol-related health information relative to other norm messages.
effect_claim_quote: Participants informed of how their consumption ranked were more likely to request information (p < .01, odds ratio = 6.0)
replication_target_quote: rank-framing messages (Taylor, Vlaev, Maltby, Brown, & Wood, 2015).
outcome_quote: Rank-framed messages did decrease drinking behaviors but did not increase information seeking.
review_note: Information seeking is the original target outcome; the new paper reported reduced drinking, a separate endpoint. Attrition reduced both studies' analyzed samples.

original_title: Sensory curation: theorizing media use for sensory regulation and implications for family media conflict
replication_title: Media sensory curation and family media conflict: replication and validation of short-form measures
effect_name: Child media sensory curation and family conflict
effect_claim: Greater child media sensory curation is associated with more adult-child conflict about media use, accounting for use time.
effect_claim_quote: Controlling usage time, child media sensory curation strongly predicted problematic child media use and moderately predicted adult–child media conflict
replication_target_quote: This paper replicates an initial survey of caregivers of children ages 3 to 14 with an independent replication survey of N = 754.
outcome_quote: As in the original study, media sensory curation was higher among children with sensory diagnoses (e.g., autism, ADHD) than without and was a moderate to strong predictor of problematic child media use and adult-child media conflict for all children.
review_note: Independent caregiver survey by the same lead author; cross-sectional self-report association, not a causal effect.

original_title: The Bergen 4-Day Treatment for Panic Disorder: A Pilot Study
replication_title: The Bergen 4-day treatment for panic disorder: replication and implementation in a new clinic
effect_name: Bergen four-day panic treatment improvement
effect_claim: In an open pilot, patients receiving four-day exposure-based treatment for panic disorder showed reduced panic severity and high three-month remission.
effect_claim_quote: The remission rate was 72% at both assessments.
replication_target_quote: This is the first replication study for B4DT on panic disorder.
outcome_quote: The results showed a significant reduction in symptom severity from pre-treatment to post-treatment (d = 4.32), and at 3-month follow-up (d = 4.91).
review_note: Both cohorts are small open trials without randomized controls; the new clinic used the same treatment with overlapping authors.

original_title: Gene-environment interaction of the dopamine D4 receptor (DRD4) and observed maternal insensitivity predicting externalizing behavior in preschoolers
replication_title: Dopamine Receptor Gene DRD4 7-Repeat Allele X Maternal Sensitivity Interaction on Child Externalizing Behavior Problems: Independent Replication of Effects at 18 Months
effect_name: DRD4 sensitivity to maternal insensitivity
effect_claim: Maternal insensitivity is associated with more externalizing behavior in young children carrying the DRD4 7-repeat allele than in noncarriers.
effect_claim_quote: maternal insensitivity was associated with externalizing (oppositional, aggressive) behaviors, but only in the presence of the DRD4 7-repeat polymorphism.
replication_target_quote: we detected similar significant interaction of the same direction as the initial study of (Bakermans-Kranenburg & van Ijzendoorn, 2006)
outcome_quote: Infants carrying the DRD4 7R allele showed greater effects of maternal insensitivity than non-carriers for behavioral problems at 18-months.
review_note: Independent small sample (63 families; 42 European ancestry); original preschoolers, replication toddlers at 18 months. Observational genotype-by-parenting association.

original_title: Clinically significant improved fitness and weight loss among overweight persons with serious mental illness
replication_title: Pragmatic Replication Trial of Health Promotion Coaching for Obesity in Serious Mental Illness and Maintenance of Outcomes
effect_name: In SHAPE one-year fitness-or-weight response
effect_claim: About half of overweight adults with serious mental illness assigned to In SHAPE achieve a clinically significant fitness gain or at least five percent weight loss after one year.
effect_claim_quote: Among In SHAPE participants, 49% achieved either clinically significant increased fitness or weight loss (5% or greater)
replication_target_quote: This pragmatic clinical trial aims to replicate positive health outcomes demonstrated in a prior randomized effectiveness study of the In SHAPE program
outcome_quote: Approximately half of In SHAPE participants (51% at 12-month program completion and 46% at 18-month follow-up) achieved clinically significant cardiovascular risk reduction
review_note: Same team and program, new urban community clinics. Claim is the combined responder rate; weight loss alone did not improve over control in the original.

original_title: The Inventory of Problems–29 is a Cross-Culturally Valid Symptom Validity Test: Initial Validation in a Turkish Community Sample
replication_title: The Cross-Cultural Ability of the Inventory of Problems-29-M (IOP-29-M) to Detect Feigned Symptom Presentations: A Replication of Akca et al. (2023) on a Romanian-Speaking Sample
replication_journal: Journal of Forensic Psychology Research and Practice
effect_name: IOP-29 cutoff detects simulated symptom feigning
effect_claim: In an online simulation sample, the IOP-29 False Disorder Probability cutoff distinguishes honest responses from feigned psychiatric presentations.
effect_claim_quote: the Turkish IOP–29 is effective in discriminating between credible and noncredible presentations
replication_target_quote: This study replicated research on the ability of the Inventory of Problems-29 (IOP-29) to detect honest, feigning, and random responding
outcome_quote: The standard cutoff of >=.50 on the IOP-29 False Disorders Probability Scale accurately discriminated honest from feigned protocols.
review_note: Romanian translation and IOP-29-M memory-module extension; repeated claim concerns the IOP-29 cutoff in simulated responding, not clinical malingering diagnosis.

original_title: A Field Study of the Relation between Leaders' Anticipation of Targets' Resistance and Targets' Reports of Influence Tactics Used by Leaders in Dyadic Relations
replication_title: Correlations for Leaders' Anticipation of Targets' Resistance and Targets' Ratings of Leaders' Influence Tactics: A Replication
effect_name: Anticipated resistance and leaders’ influence tactics
effect_claim: Leaders’ anticipated resistance among followers was moderately related to the influence tactics leaders used.
effect_claim_quote: Results from 83 leader-member dyads imply moderate relationships between perceptions of followers' resistance and influence tactics used by leaders.
original_authors: John E. Barbuto Jr., Richard W. Scholl, Charles F. Hickox III, and John Boulmetis
replication_authors: John E. Barbuto Jr., Brent J. Goertzen, and Susan M. Fritz
replication_target_quote: A sample of 553 leader-target dyads was used to replicate the 2001 work of Barbuto, Scholl, Hickox, and Boulmetis.
outcome_quote: Present results show no relation between leaders' anticipation of targets' anticipated resistance and the influence tactics used.
review_note: Original associations varied across tactics in 83 dyads; the larger 553-dyad follow-up reports no relation. Association, not causation.

original_title: Telling Things Apart
replication_title: Things Can Be Told Apart
replication_journal: Experimental Psychology (formerly Zeitschrift für Experimentelle Psychologie)
effect_name: Response-key distance reduces Stroop interference
effect_claim: Larger distance between response keys facilitated incongruent Stroop responses and reduced the Stroop effect.
effect_claim_quote: responses on incongruent Stroop trials were significantly facilitated when participants performed the Stroop task with response keys located far apart
original_authors: Daniël Lakens, Iris K. Schneider, Nils B. Jostmann, and Thomas W. Schubert
replication_target_quote: We conceptually replicated the results previously observed without these confounds
outcome_quote: Stroop effects were significantly smaller if the distance between the response keys increased.
review_note: Conceptual replication removed two confounds. Online 2013; journal issue 2014.

original_title: Confabulating reasons for behaving bad: The psychological consequences of unconsciously activated behaviour that violates one's standards
replication_title: Explaining unexplainable food choices
effect_name: Confabulated explanations after unconsciously primed eating
effect_claim: When priming steered eating against a participant’s personal standard, participants were more likely to confabulate reasons for their behavior.
effect_claim_quote: Study 2 replicated these findings in the domain of eating and provided evidence for the moderating role of personal standards
original_authors: Marieke A. Adriaanse, Jonas Weijers, Denise T. D. De Ridder, Jessica C. De Witt Huberts, and Catharine Evers
replication_authors: Marieke A. Adriaanse, Floor M. Kroese, Jonas Weijers, Peter M. Gollwitzer, and Gabriele Oettingen
replication_target_quote: Study 1 addresses this question by replicating Study 2 of Adriaanse, Weijers, De Ridder, De Witt Huberts, and Evers
outcome_quote: only those participants with high dieting standards who did not receive an explanation for their increased chocolate consumption scored higher on the confabulation questionnaire.
review_note: Confabulation in Study 1 was supported; the negative-affect mediation component was not reproduced.

original_title: Religious People Endorse Different Standards of Evidence When Evaluating Religious Versus Scientific Claims
replication_title: Religiosity Predicts Evidentiary Standards
effect_name: Religiosity lowers evidence threshold for religious claims
effect_claim: Religious participants required fewer successful repetitions to believe a prayer-related effect than a scientifically attributed effect.
effect_claim_quote: fewer repetitions when an effect was attributed to prayer compared to scientific methodology.
replication_authors: Emilio J. C. Lobato, Shadab Tabatabaeian, Morgan Fleming, Sven Sulzmann, and Colin Holbrook
replication_target_quote: a preregistered replication and extension of McPhetres and Zuckerman
outcome_quote: religious individuals exhibited a bias for believing religious claims relative to scientific claims
review_note: Only the threshold for confirming a claim is assessed here. The follow-up separately studied thresholds for rejection. Online 2019, issue 2020.

original_title: Improving memory in old age through implicit self-stereotyping.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: The Effects of Age-Stereotype Priming on the Memory Performance of Older Adults
effect_name: Positive age-stereotype priming and older adults’ memory
effect_claim: Unaware exposure to positive age stereotypes tended to improve older adults’ memory performance.
effect_claim_quote: activated positive stereotypes of aging without the participants' awareness tended to improve memory performance
replication_authors: Renee Stein, Fredda Blanchard-Fields, and Christopher Hertzog
replication_target_quote: a conceptual replication and extension of Levy's (1996
outcome_quote: priming a positive age stereotype did not increase older adults' memory performance.
review_note: Only positive primes and memory performance assessed. Negative primes impaired memory in a small unaware subset; the broader theory had mixed support.

original_title: Gradual behaviour change towards meat reduction: Development and validation of a novel decisional balance scale
replication_title: Gradual behaviour change towards meat reduction revisited: Applying the decisional balance scale in a Dutch study
effect_name: Decisional balance shifts across meat-reduction stages
effect_claim: Perceived barriers outweighed benefits for consumers without intent to reduce meat, while benefits outweighed barriers among those intending reduction.
effect_claim_quote: the cons outweighed the pros for consumers who did not intend to reduce meat consumption, while the pros outweighed the cons for consumers who intended
replication_authors: Muriel C. D. Verain, Machiel J. Reinders, Emily P. Bouwman, and Hans Dagevos
replication_target_quote: The current study sets out to replicate their German study in the Dutch context.
outcome_quote: the further in the meat reduction process, the more the pros outweigh the cons.
review_note: Dutch survey versus original German samples. The original corrigendum 10.1016/j.appet.2024.107545 concerns barrier rankings and a table typo, not this stage pattern.

original_title: The impact of recent and long-term experience on access to word meanings: Evidence from large-scale internet-based experiments
replication_title: Retuning of lexical-semantic representations: Repetition and spacing effects in word-meaning priming.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition
effect_name: Recent exposure biases later ambiguous-word meaning
effect_claim: A disambiguated encounter with an ambiguous word increased later retrieval of the exposed meaning.
effect_claim_quote: they then retrieve this primed meaning more often (compared with an unprimed control condition).
original_authors: Jennifer M. Rodd, Zhenguang G. Cai, Hannah N. Betts, Betsy Hanby, Catherine Hutchinson, and Aviva Adler
replication_authors: Hannah N. Betts, Rebecca A. Gilbert, Zhenguang G. Cai, Zainab B. Okedara, and Jennifer M. Rodd
replication_target_quote: recently encountered word-meanings become more readily available (Rodd et al., 2016, 2013).
outcome_quote: 1 encounter with an ambiguous word biased the later interpretation of this word towards the primed meaning
review_note: Single-exposure word-meaning priming only. Original issue 2016 though DOI metadata lists 2015; follow-up online 2017 and issue 2018.

original_title: Vagus nerve stimulation boosts the drive to work for rewards
replication_title: Non‐invasive vagus nerve stimulation and the motivation to work for rewards: A replication of Neuser et al. (2020, Nature Communications )
effect_name: Auricular vagus stimulation increases reward-effort invigoration
effect_claim: Left-ear transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation increased effort invigoration for rewards, particularly food.
effect_claim_quote: acute taVNS enhances invigoration of effort, and stimulation on the left side primarily facilitates invigoration for food rewards.
replication_target_quote: positive effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) on the invigoration of reward‐seeking behaviors, especially for food rewards.
outcome_quote: taVNS did not increase the strength of invigoration ( p = .62)
review_note: Direct replication used left-ear stimulation; it did not test the original right-ear contrast.

original_title: Accusations by Adults of Childhood Sexual Abuse: a Survey of the Members of the British False Memory Society (BFMS)
replication_title: Characteristics of recovered memories: a Dutch replication of Gudjonsson's (1997) British survey
effect_name: Recovered-memory accusations chiefly name biological fathers in member surveys
effect_claim: In a British false-memory society member survey, adult women made most accusations and biological fathers were most often named.
effect_claim_quote: The great majority (87%) of the accusers were female and most of the accusations were directed against the biological father.
replication_target_quote: results of this survey parallel those of the Gudjonsson (1997) survey among members of the BFMS.
outcome_quote: most accusations were made by adult daughters about their biological fathers and arose in the context of psychotherapeutic treatment.
review_note: Both are selected society-member surveys, not population prevalence estimates.

original_title: Processing collocations in a second language: A case of first language activation?
replication_title: Explaining the Effect of Congruency on Processing Collocations: A Modified Replication of Wolter and Yamashita (2015)
replication_journal: The Journal of Second Language Acquisition and Teaching (JSLAT)
effect_name: No first-language collocation advantage in second-language lexical decisions
effect_claim: First-language-only collocations did not gain a speed advantage during second-language lexical decisions.
effect_claim_quote: The results revealed no such activation.
replication_target_quote: collocations that exist only in L1 but not in L2 were not processed faster than collocations that only exist in L2 but not in L1
outcome_quote: there was no L1 activation effect by L2 (L1 Korean) learners
review_note: Outcome is restricted to the online lexical-decision task; the replication's offline recall test pointed to L1 reliance. Neither null result establishes equivalence.

original_title: Group as a social microcosm: The reciprocal relationship between intersession intimate behaviors and in-session intimate behaviors.
replication_title: The social microcosm revisited: A replication of Kivlighan et al. (2021) on the reciprocal relationship between in-session and intersession intimate behaviors.
effect_name: In-session and everyday intimate behaviors reciprocate in therapy groups
effect_claim: Group members' in-session and outside-session intimate behaviors showed reciprocal associations.
effect_claim_quote: predicting following week intersession intimate behaviors from in-session intimate behaviors, showed significant between-member and between-groups effects.
replication_target_quote: The present study represents a replication and extension of Kivlighan et al.'s (2021) study, focusing on the social microcosm hypothesis
outcome_quote: there was a reciprocal relationship for partners' but not for actors' intimate behaviors.
review_note: Replication hypotheses were not confirmed, but partner-level reciprocity supported part of the broader social-microcosm pattern; modeling and sample differed.

original_title: Sentence processing deficits: Theory and therapy
replication_title: Sentence processing deficits: A replication of therapy
replication_journal: International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders
effect_name: Sentence-mapping therapy improves chronic aphasia language performance
effect_claim: Therapy targeting thematic-role mapping improved sentence comprehension and production in people with chronic aphasia.
effect_claim_quote: improvements were measured in sentence comprehension and production for both patients
replication_target_quote: replication of a therapeutic programme originally used by one of the authors, Byng
outcome_quote: Sentence comprehension and production both improved as a result of therapy.
review_note: Replication concerned one patient with a similar, not identical, impairment.

original_title: The Price of Expertise: Effects of Experience on the Water-Level Task
replication_title: Experience and the Water-Level Task Revisited: Does Expertise Exact a Price?
effect_name: Liquid-handling occupational experience reduces water-level-task accuracy
effect_claim: Waitstaff and bartenders with daily liquid-handling experience performed less accurately on the water-level task than control occupations.
effect_claim_quote: liquid surfaces that waitresses and bartenders considered natural deviated even more from horizontal than was the case for comparison groups
replication_target_quote: whose occupations involved considerable experience with liquids in containers were less accurate on Piaget's water-level task
outcome_quote: bartenders, waiters and waitresses) are, in fact, more accurate on two versions of the water-level task
review_note: North American replication used tighter controls than the original Munich experiment.

original_title: The Effects of Feedback Equivocality on Escalation of Commitment: An Empirical Investigation of Decision Dilemma Theory1
replication_title: Equivocality and Escalation: A Replication and Preliminary Examination of Frustration1
effect_name: Equivocal feedback increases escalation of commitment
effect_claim: High versus low equivocality feedback increased investment escalation after subsequent negative feedback in a simulated marketing decision.
effect_claim_quote: subjects who received high equivocal feedback escalated allocations.
replication_target_quote: a replication and extension of Hantula and DeNicolis Bragger (1999).
outcome_quote: participants receiving highly equivocal feedback invested a greater relative amount of money during failure than did those who received feedback low in equivocality.
review_note: The original's separate goal-or-standard attenuation result is outside this claim.

original_title: Conservation without conversation? An alternative, non‐verbal paradigm for assessing conservation of liquid quantity
replication_title: Conservation without Conversation Revisited: a replication and elaboration of the Wheldall‐Poborca findings on the nonverbal assessment of conservation of liquid quantity
effect_name: Nonverbal liquid-conservation tests reveal verbal-task bias
effect_claim: Some young children who failed a standard verbal conservation test demonstrated liquid-volume conservation with nonverbal assessment.
effect_claim_quote: young children who could not conserve within the traditional verbal procedure were more likely to demonstrate*** conservation within the non‐verbal paradigm
replication_target_quote: more young children can conserve liquid volume when tested using a novel, nonverbal paradigm than when tested by conventional verbal assessment procedures.
outcome_quote: the original Wheldall and Poborca findings were replicated
review_note: The original abstract contains a publisher extraction artifact after 'demonstrate'; the quote is preserved verbatim.

original_title: ASSESSING AND TREATING VOCAL STEREOTYPY IN CHILDREN WITH AUTISM
replication_title: A replication of the RIRD strategy to decrease vocal stereotypy in a student with autism
effect_name: Response interruption and redirection reduces vocal stereotypy
effect_claim: Response interruption and redirection reduced noncommunicative vocal stereotypy in children with autism.
effect_claim_quote: For each child, RIRD produced levels of vocal stereotypy substantially lower than those observed in baseline.
replication_target_quote: We used the Response Interruption and Redirection (RIRD; Ahearn, Clark, & McDonald, 2007 ) strategy
outcome_quote: the RIRD intervention successfully reduced the target behavior.
review_note: Replication was an ABAB single-student intervention, compared with four children in the original.

original_title: Dissociation as a Function of Child Abuse and Fantasy Proneness in a Substance Abuse Population
replication_title: The importance of fantasy‐proneness in dissociation: a replication
effect_name: Fantasy proneness predicts dissociation in substance-abuse patients
effect_claim: Fantasy proneness predicted dissociation at least as strongly as reported childhood abuse among male substance-abuse patients.
effect_claim_quote: Regression analyses suggested that fantasy proneness is as important as sexual abuse in predicting dissociation.
replication_target_quote: Previous research (Pekala, Kumar, Ainslie, Elliott, Mullen, Salinger and Masten, 1999/2000) found that dissociation, as measured by the ‘Dissociative Experiences Scale’ (DES) (Bernstein and Putnam, 1986), was predicted as much by fantasy‐proneness (Wilson and Barber, 1983a) as by child abuse
outcome_quote: These results replicate the findings of the previous study (Pekala et al., 1999/2000)
review_note: Both studies are observational male substance-abuse samples; no causal effect is inferred.

original_title: Processing advantages for consonance: A comparison between rats (Rattus norvegicus) and humans (Homo sapiens).
replication_title: Reexamining the Effects of Ratio Simplicity and Familiarity on Abstract Pattern Learning in Dyad Sequences
effect_name: Consonant dyads improve abstract auditory-pattern learning
effect_claim: Human participants learned abstract auditory patterns better over consonant than dissonant intervals.
effect_claim_quote: Humans, on the contrary, learn an abstract rule better when it is implemented over consonant (Experiment 4) than over dissonant intervals (Experiment 5).
replication_target_quote: conceptually replicated two experiments by Crespo-Bojorque and Toro (2016; Experiments 4a & 5a)
outcome_quote: Neither conventionally consonant nor unconventionally tuned small integer-ratio dyads conferred any advantage in pattern learning or generalization.
review_note: Conceptual replication; a post hoc untrained-musician subsample suggested a familiarity effect, outside the preregistered primary comparison.

original_title: Response-Style Effects, Response-Shift Bias and a Bogus-Pipeline
replication_title: Response-Style Effects, Response-Shift Bias, and a Bogus-Pipeline: A Replication
effect_name: Bogus-pipeline instruction lowers self-reported preratings
effect_claim: A bogus-pipeline induction lowered self-reported pretest ratings and eliminated response-shift bias in a psychology-student training experiment.
effect_claim_quote: The bogus-pipeline induction in the pretesting did lower self-reported preratings and consequently eliminated response-shift bias
replication_target_quote: a bogus-pipeline induction did remove response-style effects in the self-reported pretest.
outcome_quote: Contrary to expectation, a bogus-pipeline induction did not lower self-reported preratings.
review_note: Changed educational-training context; response shift occurred in neither replication arm, so this only fails the claimed decrease in preratings.

original_title: THE USE OF RESPONSE PREVENTION TO ELIMINATE NOCTURNAL THUMBSUCKING
replication_title: A Systematic Replication of Response Prevention to Eliminate Nocturnal Thumbsucking
effect_name: Response-prevention fading suppresses nocturnal thumbsucking
effect_claim: A fading response-prevention package suppressed nocturnal thumbsucking behavior in children.
effect_claim_quote: The response prevention package completely eliminated thumbsucking behavior in both boys.
replication_target_quote: A systematic replication of Van Houten and Rolider's (1984) response prevention study to eliminate nocturnal thumbsucking behavior was performed.
outcome_quote: Response prevention procedures led to the suppression of thumbsucking behavior
review_note: Replication involved one child, shorter treatment and modified fading steps; follow-up was one year.

original_title: Health Teaching Needs of Clients With Serious and Persistent Mental Illness: Client and Provider Perspectives
original_journal: Journal of Psychosocial Nursing and Mental Health Services
replication_title: Educational Needs of Inpatients with Severe & Persistent Mental Illnesses: A Partial Replication
replication_journal: Journal of Psychosocial Nursing and Mental Health Services
effect_name: Patients and staff disagree on mental-health education needs
effect_claim: Mental-health clients' perceived education needs differed from staff ratings in an outpatient clinical setting.
effect_claim_quote: Contrasts between staff and client ratings suggest that results support the practice of assessing clients' own perceptions of their needs
replication_target_quote: differences may exist between the perceived health education needs of outpatients and their health care providers.
outcome_quote: As in the original study, we found discrepancies between patients' actual needs and nurses' perceptions of those needs
review_note: Partial replication shifted from outpatients to inpatients and modified the survey instrument.

original_title: The modified WAIS: An alternative to short forms
replication_title: Replication of a Modified Procedure for Administering the WAIS
effect_name: Modified WAIS scores correlate highly with standard WAIS scores
effect_claim: An abbreviated Modified WAIS administration produced IQ scores highly correlated with standard WAIS scores.
effect_claim_quote: The Modified WAIS was shown to correlate quite highly with the Standard WAIS: .999 for Verbal, Performance, and Full Scale IQ (N = 200).
replication_target_quote: The modified WAIS, an abbreviated scoring procedure presented by Vincent in 1979, was evaluated in a replication study of 45 subjects.
outcome_quote: Modified WAIS and WAIS IQs correlated highly for Verbal (.996) and Performance (.999) scales, and Full Scale (.998).
review_note: High correlation is the reviewed claim; it alone does not establish interchangeability of the two tests.

effect_name: Spatial-frequency memory after 24 hours
effect_claim: Visual spatial-frequency information remains precise in perceptual memory after 24 hours.
effect_claim_quote: stable across time intervals of 24 hr, confirming previous findings of high-fidelity storage in the long-term memory range.
original_title: High-Fidelity Perceptual Long-Term Memory Revisited—and Confirmed
replication_title: Long-term memory for spatial frequency: a non-replication
replication_target_quote: We report an attempted replication of Magnussen et al. (Psychol Sci 14:74-76, 2003)
outcome_quote: Group thresholds after 24 h were significantly higher than after 5 s, therefore failing to support long-term storage of spatial frequency.
review_note: Spatial-frequency discrimination at 5 seconds versus 24 hours; the original studied high-fidelity storage across visual attributes.

effect_name: Camera angle and confession coercion judgments
effect_claim: Viewers judge a videotaped confession as less coerced when the camera focuses on the suspect rather than the detective.
effect_claim_quote: Subjects in the suspect‐focus condition subsequently judged that the confession was elicited by means of a small degree of coercion; subjects in the equal‐focus condition judged that it was elicited by means of a moderate degree of coercion; and subjects in the detective‐focus condition judged that it was elicited by means of a large degree of coercion.
original_title: Videotaped Confessions: The Impact of Camera Point of View on Judgments of Coercion1
replication_title: Replicating Camera Perspective Bias in the Japanese Justice System
replication_target_quote: originally reported by Lassiter and Irvine (1986)
outcome_quote: we did not find any evidence supporting the presence of CPB
review_note: Replication tested Japanese video-recording style, including an experiment intended to recreate the original camera-perspective bias under that style.

effect_name: Husband emotional maturity and marital adjustment
effect_claim: Husbands who rate themselves as more emotionally mature report better marital adjustment.
effect_claim_quote: emotional maturity (self-rated) correlated .28 with his marital adjustment score
original_title: Emotional Maturity and Marital Adjustment
original_journal: Journal of Marriage and the Family
replication_title: Emotional Maturity and Marital Adjustment: A Decade Replication
replication_journal: Journal of Marriage and the Family
replication_target_quote: a randomn sample of 143 husband-wife pairs in the same community in which Dean (1966) did his original study
outcome_quote: correlated .33 with his and .28 with his
review_note: Exact self-rated husband maturity association; replication used the same community but a different marital-adjustment scale.

effect_name: Rhythmic timing improves pitch judgments
effect_claim: Listeners judge pitch more accurately when a comparison tone arrives at an expected beat than at an unexpected time.
effect_claim_quote: Listeners were most accurate judging the pitch of rhythmically expected tones and least accurate with very unexpected ones.
original_title: Temporal Aspects of Stimulus-Driven Attending in Dynamic Arrays
replication_title: The auditory dynamic attending theory revisited: A closer look at the pitch comparison task
replication_target_quote: Here we aimed to replicate and complement the most prominent experimental implementation of dynamic attending (Jones et al., 2002. Psychol. Sci. 13(4), 313-319).
outcome_quote: the group average effects did not replicate the pattern reported by Jones et al., 2002. Psychol. Sci. 13(4), 313-319 in any of the five experiments.
review_note: Four conceptual variants and one exact pitch-comparison attempt; the failure is specific to this task, not all dynamic-attending effects.

effect_name: Even a penny increases donation frequency
effect_claim: Adding Even a penny will help to a charity request increases the proportion of people who donate.
effect_claim_quote: increase significantly the frequency of donations while leaving unaffected the size of the donations by adding the sentence, Even a penny will help
original_title: Increasing compliance by legitimizing paltry contributions: When even a penny helps.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Teaching replication through replication to solve the replication “crisis”
replication_target_quote: students replicated Cialdini and Schroeder’s “even a penny will help” (EPH) donation solicitation experiment.
outcome_quote: a larger percentage donated in the EPH condition.
review_note: Verdict applies only to donation frequency. The replication found larger donation amounts for the standard request, unlike the original no-difference result for amount.

effect_name: Personality shifts with memory disorders
effect_claim: Caregivers rate people with memory disorders as more neurotic and less extraverted, open, and conscientious than before impairment.
effect_claim_quote: There were significant changes in four of the five domains of normal personality functioning toward less conscientiousness, lower extraversion, higher neuroticism, and lower openness.
original_title: Ratings of Personality Change in Patients Being Evaluated for Memory Disorders
replication_title: Caregiver ratings of personality change in Alzheimer's disease patients: A replication.
replication_target_quote: Results replicated previous findings on the degree of change reported in a previous group of patients with mixed memory disorder diagnoses.
outcome_quote: After a diagnosis of AD, the patients were rated as significantly more neurotic, less extraverted, less open, and less conscientious.
review_note: Original sample had mixed memory disorders; replication narrowed to Alzheimer disease. Both used caregiver ratings of current versus premorbid personality.

effect_name: Female excess in somatic depression
effect_claim: Women have higher prevalence of depression with somatic symptoms than men, without a higher prevalence of depression lacking those symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: Female subjects exhibited a higher prevalence than male subjects of somatic depression but not a higher prevalence of pure depression.
original_title: Gender Difference in the Prevalence of Clinical Depression: The Role Played by Depression Associated With Somatic Symptoms
replication_title: Gender Differences in the Prevalence of Somatic Versus Pure Depression: A Replication
replication_target_quote: attempted to replicate the finding of the National Comorbidity Survey that the prevalence of depression associated with somatic symptoms was much higher among women than men.
outcome_quote: the prevalence of somatic depression but not pure depression was much higher among women than men.
review_note: Replication reanalyzed the Epidemiologic Catchment Area survey, rather than the original National Comorbidity Survey.

effect_name: Actuarial prediction of violent reoffending
effect_claim: A 12-variable actuarial risk score predicts violent reoffending among male forensic patients.
effect_claim_quote: The actuarial instrument consisted of 12 variables and significantly predicted violent outcome in each of five subgroups.
original_title: Violent Recidivism of Mentally Disordered Offenders
replication_title: Prospective replication of the Violence Risk Appraisal Guide in predicting violent recidivism among forensic patients.
replication_target_quote: prospective replication of the predictive accuracy of the Violence Risk Appraisal Guide (VRAG).
outcome_quote: The VRAG yielded a large effect size in predicting violent recidivism (ROC area = .80) over a constant 5-year follow-up
review_note: The original derivation and validation sample was male. Replication overall supported prediction but reports no positive association in a small low-risk female subsample.

effect_name: Foster-child reading gains with paired reading
effect_claim: Foster children improve their reading age during a 16-week paired-reading program with their carers.
effect_claim_quote: The results revealed an average improvement in reading age of 12 months during this time
original_title: Paired Reading as a Literacy Intervention for Foster Children
replication_title: Paired Reading for foster children: results from a Swedish replication of an English literacy intervention
replication_target_quote: A UK literacy intervention – Paired Reading – was replicated in seven Swedish local authorities
outcome_quote: average improvement in reading age was 11 months, basically the same as in the UK
review_note: Both studies report pre-to-post reading gains with carer-supported paired reading; neither abstract establishes a randomized control contrast.

effect_name: Power need predicts competitive victimhood
effect_claim: A stronger need for power predicted greater competitive victimhood among advantaged and disadvantaged groups.
effect_claim_quote: Focusing on the structural inequality between Jewish and Arab citizens of Israel (Study 1) and Israeli women and men (Study 2), we found that across all groups and contexts, power needs predicted competitive victimhood.
original_title: Power matters: The role of power and morality needs in competitive victimhood among advantaged and disadvantaged groups
replication_title: Replicating What Motivates Conflicting Groups to Engage in Competitive Victimhood: The Roles of Need for Power and Need for Morality
replication_target_quote: The main objective of the present research was to replicate Kahalon et al.'s Study 1 findings, testing the robustness of their results by conducting it in the context of a unique threat (i.e., COVID‐19).
outcome_quote: Our results, involving a well‐powered sample of Jews (N = 205) and Arabs (N = 152) living in Israel, demonstrated that while need for morality and need for power individually related to competitive victimhood, when included simultaneously in a regression need for power but not need morality predicted competitive victimhood among members of both a disadvantaged group (Arabs living in Israel) and an advantaged group (Jews living in Israel).
review_note: The follow-up tested the original Study 1 in the COVID-19 context.

effect_name: Ideal-type leader prototypicality advantage
effect_claim: Leader group prototypicality defined as an ideal group member had a stronger relationship with leadership effectiveness than prototypicality defined as an average member.
effect_claim_quote: The effect is stronger (a) when prototypicality is conceptualized as the ideal-type rather than the average group member, (b) for stronger prototypes (indexed by group longevity), and (c) for group members in formal rather than nonformal leadership roles.
original_title: Advancing the social identity theory of leadership: A meta-analytic review of leader group prototypicality
replication_title: Leader Group Prototypicality: A Replication of Average Member Versus Ideal-Type Operationalization Effects
replication_target_quote: Steffens, Munt, van Knippenberg, Platow, and Haslam’s meta-analysis showed that LGP operationalized as embodying the ideal-type of the group (ideal-type prototypicality, ITP) is more strongly related to indicators of leadership effectiveness than LGP operationalized as embodying the average group member (average member prototypicality, AMP).
outcome_quote: Replicating Steffens et al.'s finding, both studies showed that LGP is more strongly related to trust when it is operationalized as ITP rather than AMP.
review_note: Within-study follow-ups use trust in the leader as the outcome; this is a conceptual replication of the meta-analytic moderator.

effect_name: Heavy traffic raises driver stress
effect_claim: Drivers in heavy traffic reported greater state stress than drivers in light traffic.
effect_claim_quote: Both state driver stress and aggression were greater in high- than in low-congestion conditions.
original_title: Traffic congestion, driver stress, and driver aggression
replication_title: In Situ Methodology for Studying State Driver Stress: A Between‐Subjects Design Replication
replication_target_quote: The current study replicated the findings of the in situ methodology using a between‐subjects research design.
outcome_quote: State stress was greater in heavy traffic.
review_note: Follow-up used a between-subjects design; the named claim concerns state driver stress only.

effect_name: Spaced practice improves explicit L2 vocabulary
effect_claim: Spaced practice produced better explicit second-language vocabulary recall and meaning matching than massed practice.
effect_claim_quote: Results showed an advantage of spaced over massed learning on the meaning recall and meaning–form matching posttests.
original_title: Effects of spacing on contextual vocabulary learning: Spacing facilitates the acquisition of explicit, but not tacit, vocabulary knowledge
replication_title: Effects of spacing on the acquisition of explicit and implicit vocabulary knowledge: An approximate replication of Nakata and Elgort (2021)
replication_journal: Studies in Second Language Learning and Teaching
replication_target_quote: The present study replicated Nakata and Elgort’s (2021) study to investigate how massing and spacing impact the acquisition of explicit and implicit vocabulary knowledge in L2.
outcome_quote: Posttest results showed that spaced learning led to better explicit vocabulary acquisition compared to massed learning.
review_note: Only the explicit-vocabulary contrast is counted. The replication abstract reports no spacing advantage on implicit knowledge.

effect_name: Suicide attempts and implicit death-self association
effect_claim: Among psychiatric emergency patients, those with a suicide-attempt history showed a stronger implicit death-or-suicide association with self than those without an attempt history.
effect_claim_quote: Results confirmed that people who have attempted suicide hold a significantly stronger implicit association between death/suicide and self than do psychiatrically distressed individuals who have not attempted suicide.
original_title: Measuring the Suicidal Mind
replication_title: Suicide and self-injury-related implicit cognition: A large-scale examination and replication.
replication_target_quote: We recruited a large sample of participants (N = 7,015) via a public web-based platform called Project Implicit Mental Health (PIMH) to test several hypotheses about self-harm-related implicit associations using the Implicit Association Test (IAT).
outcome_quote: Results replicated prior studies demonstrating that self-harm-related implicit associations were stronger among individuals with (vs. without) a history of suicide attempt and NSSI.
review_note: Only the suicide-attempt-history group contrast is counted; the follow-up also tested nonsuicidal self-injury.

effect_name: Consciousness inventory predicts hypnotic susceptibility
effect_claim: Self-reported experiences during hypnosis predicted scores on a hypnotic susceptibility scale.
effect_claim_quote: Regression analyses that held up under cross-validation during HI suggest that the PCI may be an appropriate instrument for predicting susceptibility.
original_title: Predicting Hypnotic Susceptibility by a Self-Report Phenomenological State Instrument
replication_title: Predicting Hypnotic Susceptibility via a Self-Report Instrument: A Replication
replication_target_quote: In an attempt to replicate the previous results, 434 subjects were given the Harvard Scale and the self-report inventory in reference to a baseline condition and a hypnotic induction.
outcome_quote: A validity coefficient of .57 (n = 342) was obtained between the actual Harvard scores of the present study and the predicted Harvard scores (using the coefficients of the previous study).
review_note: Same-author replication; predictor coefficients from the earlier sample predicted the later sample.

effect_name: Mere existence raises favorable evaluations
effect_claim: People evaluated an existing state more favorably than an alternative because it already existed.
effect_claim_quote: Studies 1 and 2 demonstrate that an existing state is evaluated more favorably than an alternative.
original_title: The existence bias.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: The existence bias: a systematic replication
replication_target_quote: Four experiments were conducted to re-examine the recently proposed “existence bias,” according to which people think that the status quo is good simply because it exists.
outcome_quote: The existence bias was confirmed, but the effect size was small.
review_note: One follow-up experiment favored the alternative, while three showed a status-quo preference; count as mixed.

original_title: Gender differences in sexual behaviors and fantasies in a college population
replication_title: Gender differences in sexual fantasy and behavior in a college population: A ten-year replication
effect_name: Men report more sexual fantasies than women in college samples
effect_claim: Male university students reported more frequent sexual fantasies than female university students.
effect_claim_quote: Males fantasized about sex more
replication_target_quote: replication of a study conducted 10 years ago by Person et al., investigating gender differences in sexual behaviors and fantasies in a college population.
outcome_quote: men continue to fantasize more than women, but the gender differences have narrowed.
review_note: The directional frequency difference replicated but narrowed; this claim excludes aggressive or sadistic fantasy stereotypes, which neither study supported.

original_title: Buying Books Online: Follow-up
replication_title: Buying Books Online: A Replication
effect_name: Computer and Internet skills predict online book purchasing
effect_claim: Among college students, stronger computer and Internet skills predicted buying books online.
effect_claim_quote: purchasing books online was predicted by their computer/Internet skills.
replication_target_quote: In a replication study, purchasing books online by 137 state college students
outcome_quote: purchasing books online by 137 state college students was predicted by computer/Internet skills.
review_note: Original sample 72 undergraduates; replication 137 state-college students.

original_title: Retrieval Practice Produces More Learning than Elaborative Studying with Concept Mapping
replication_title: Re-examining the testing effect as a learning strategy: the advantage of retrieval practice over concept mapping as a methodological artifact
effect_name: Retrieval practice beats concept mapping on meaningful learning
effect_claim: Retrieval practice produced greater meaningful learning gains than concept mapping in the original study conditions.
effect_claim_quote: practicing retrieval produces greater gains in meaningful learning than elaborative studying with concept mapping.
replication_target_quote: The present preregistered study examined whether the advantage observed in the retrieval practice condition over the concept mapping condition in previous studies was actually driven by additional memorization rather than by retrieval practice.
outcome_quote: While we replicated the previous finding that retrieval practice in combination with additional memorizing produces more learning than concept mapping without additional memorizing, this advantage of retrieval practice over concept mapping vanished when participants in the concept mapping condition, too, memorized the learning material
review_note: Original-condition advantage replicated; equalizing subsequent memorization removed it. The replication authors attribute the original contrast to a memorization-time confound.

original_title: MMPI Personality Characteristics of Physical and Social Science Students
replication_title: Psychology of Scientist: XXXIV. MMPI Characteristics of Physical and Social Science Students: Replication and Reanalysis
effect_name: Physical-science graduates score higher on MMPI social introversion
effect_claim: Physics and zoology graduates scored higher on MMPI social introversion than sociology and history graduates.
effect_claim_quote: the physics and zoology majors are higher on Si than the sociology and history majors
replication_target_quote: Only one of the four hypotheses was supported: physics and zoology students were higher on Social Introversion than sociology and history students.
outcome_quote: the physics and zoology majors are higher on Social Introversion ( p < .001)
review_note: Review is restricted to the shared social-introversion comparison; the papers disagree on the count of other hypotheses.

original_title: Sequential and parallel letter processing in letter-by-letter dyslexia
replication_title: Parallel processing blocked by letter similarity in letter by letter dyslexia: A replication
effect_name: Letter similarity blocks orthographic-neighborhood facilitation in dyslexia
effect_claim: In letter-by-letter dyslexia, high letter confusability prevented the word-recognition benefit of many orthographic neighbors.
effect_claim_quote: the facilitatory effect of N size is prevented with high letter-confusability targets.
replication_target_quote: An investigation of the joint effects of orthographic neighbourhood size (N size) and of letter confusability
outcome_quote: All three patients showed a facilitatory effect of increased N size with low letter-confusability words, but no N size effect with high confusability words.
review_note: Replication tested three new patients against the original single-patient result.

original_title: The effect of distance on the moral judgment of environmental wrongdoings
replication_title: The Effect of Spatial Distance on the Moral Judgment of Environmental Wrongdoings
effect_name: Spatially distant environmental decisions draw harsher moral judgments
effect_claim: Third parties judged an otherwise identical environmental wrongdoing more severely when the decision was made farther away.
effect_claim_quote: An increase in spatial distance leads to a more severe judgment of an otherwise identical decision.
replication_target_quote: higher spatial distance between a decision-maker and the environmental wrongdoing led to harsher moral judgments by third parties.
outcome_quote: we found minimal support for the original findings, with effect sizes substantially smaller than the original study.
review_note: Direct German-speaking replication of the France experiment; original DOI metadata says 2022 though the replication cites its 2023 issue year.

original_title: Experimental Philosophy and the Incentivisation Challenge: a Proposed Application of the Bayesian Truth Serum
replication_title: Taking a Closer Look at the Bayesian Truth Serum
replication_journal: Experimental Psychology (formerly Zeitschrift für Experimentelle Psychologie)
effect_name: Bayesian Truth Serum changes Likert response distributions
effect_claim: Introducing Bayesian Truth Serum incentives altered answers to experimental-philosophy Likert items.
effect_claim_quote: demonstrating its qualified impact on the distribution of answers
replication_target_quote: finding that the introduction of this mechanism significantly altered response behavior.
outcome_quote: We fail to find significant differences in response behavior between participants who were simply paid for completing the study and participants who were incentivized with the BTS.
review_note: Registered report provides evidence against effects of V greater than .1; smaller effects remain possible.

original_title: Confirming the latent structure and base rate of schizotypy: A taxometric analysis.
replication_title: The taxonicity of schizotypy: A replication.
effect_name: Perceptual Aberration Scale schizotypy has a taxonic structure
effect_claim: Schizotypy measured with the Perceptual Aberration Scale had a discrete latent taxon with roughly ten-percent base rate.
effect_claim_quote: schizotypy, as assessed by the PAS, is taxonic at the latent level with a general population taxon base rate of approximately .10.
replication_target_quote: sought to replicate earlier findings concerning the taxonic latent structure and general population base rate of schizotypy
outcome_quote: the data strongly suggest that schizotypy, as assessed by the PAS, is taxonic at the latent level with a low general population taxon base rate (i.e., < .10).
review_note: Both studies used MAXCOV-HITMAX on PAS items in new nonclinical university samples.

original_title: Children With a History of SLI Show Reduced Sensitivity to Audiovisual Temporal Asynchrony: An ERP Study
original_journal: Journal of Speech Language and Hearing Research
replication_title: Sensitivity to Audiovisual Temporal Asynchrony in Children With a History of Specific Language Impairment and Their Peers With Typical Development: A Replication and Follow-Up Study
replication_journal: Journal of Speech Language and Hearing Research
effect_name: Children with prior language impairment detect audiovisual asynchrony less well
effect_claim: Children with a history of specific language impairment detected sound-image temporal separation less accurately than typically developing peers.
effect_claim_quote: H-SLI children were profoundly less sensitive to temporal separations between auditory and visual modalities compared with their TD peers.
replication_target_quote: Earlier, my colleagues and I showed that children with a history of specific language impairment (H-SLI) are significantly less able to detect audiovisual asynchrony compared with children with typical development
outcome_quote: children with H-SLI perceived asynchrony significantly less frequently than children with TD at SOAs of 400-500 ms.
review_note: New children, same tone-and-flash task; claim is behavioral discrimination, not a neurological mechanism.

original_title: Objecting to experiments even while approving of the policies or treatments they compare
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Experiment aversion does not appear to generalize
replication_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
effect_name: People disapprove randomized trials despite approving tested policies
effect_claim: People sometimes rated randomized policy experiments less appropriate even while approving either tested policy if applied universally.
effect_claim_quote: people often disapprove of experiments involving randomization despite approving of the policies or treatments to be tested.
replication_target_quote: people often rate randomized experiments as less appropriate than the policies they contain even when approving the implementation of either policy untested
outcome_quote: our triangulation reveals insufficient evidence to conclude that people exhibit a common pattern of behavior that would be consistent with relative experiment aversion
review_note: One direct and six conceptual preregistered replications tested generalizability; the source describes failure to generalize rather than universal absence.

original_title: Detecting the Snake in the Grass
replication_title: The effect of spatial frequency information and visual similarity in threat detection
effect_name: Threatening animals are detected faster in visual search
effect_claim: Participants detected threat-relevant animals more rapidly than nonthreatening animals in visual search arrays.
effect_claim_quote: Both the children and the adults detected snakes more rapidly than three types of nonthreatening stimuli
replication_target_quote: sought to examine the role of spatial frequency on the detection of threat using a speeded visual search paradigm.
outcome_quote: The results replicate previous work demonstrating more rapid detection of threatening versus non-threatening stimuli
review_note: Replication tested snakes or spiders with image filtering and different distractors; it does not independently establish the original young-child subgroup result.

original_title: Experience and Latency to Achieve Stereopsis
replication_title: Experience and Latency to Achieve Stereopsis: A Replication
effect_name: Repeated stereogram viewing shortens time to perceive depth
effect_claim: Repeated exposure to a complex random-dot stereogram reduced latency to achieve stereoscopic depth within a session.
effect_claim_quote: Latency to achieve stereopsis decreases over trials each day
replication_target_quote: This study replicated and extended the findings of MacCracken and Hayes (1976).
outcome_quote: Latencies decreased across 5 trials in the first session
review_note: Replication used two nonconsecutive days versus four consecutive days and also found incomplete carryover.

original_title: Producing meaningful improvements in problem behavior of children with autism via synthesized analyses and treatments
replication_title: Use of synthesized analysis and informed treatment to promote school reintegration
effect_name: Synthesized behavior treatment reduces severe autism-related problem behavior
effect_claim: An interview-informed synthesized contingency assessment and treatment reduced severe problem behavior in children with autism.
effect_claim_quote: no problem behavior was observed at the clinic and in the home.
replication_target_quote: sought to replicate the interview‐informed synthesized contingency analysis and treatment procedures developed by Hanley and colleagues
outcome_quote: Treatment resulted in meaningful reductions in problem behavior, sustained improvements in compliance
review_note: School replication involved one child, increased treatment intensity after a burst, and broad classroom implementation; original involved three children in clinic and home.

original_title: Unskilled and unaware of it: How difficulties in recognizing one's own incompetence lead to inflated self-assessments.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Unskilled, unaware, or both? The better-than-average heuristic and statistical regression predict errors in estimates of own performance.
replication_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
effect_name: Metacognitive deficits explain low-performer overconfidence
effect_claim: The original authors attributed low performers' inflated self-assessments partly to deficits in distinguishing correct from incorrect answers.
effect_claim_quote: Several analyses linked this miscalibration to deficits in metacognitive skill
replication_target_quote: J. Kruger and D. Dunning (1999) attributed these asymmetric errors to differences in metacognitive skill.
outcome_quote: A replication study showed no evidence for mediation effects for any of several candidate variables.
review_note: The low-performer overestimation pattern itself recurred; this failed result concerns the proposed metacognitive explanation, with regression and better-than-average effects offered as alternatives.

original_title: Age-related differences in the motoric aspects of transcription typing skill.
replication_title: Age and skill differences in typing related and unrelated reaction time tasks
effect_name: Older typists show skill-dependent translation and execution deficits
effect_claim: Older low-skill typists showed deficits in both keystroke translation and execution, while older high-skill typists showed a translation deficit only.
effect_claim_quote: low-skill, older typists exhibited a deficit in both the translation and the execution components of motor performance, whereas high-skill, older typists exhibited a deficit in translation only.
replication_target_quote: replicated results reported by Bosman (1993) suggesting that low skill older typists exhibit a deficit in both the translation and execution components
outcome_quote: low skill older typists exhibit a deficit in both the translation and execution components of motor performance, whereas high skill older typists exhibit a deficit in translation only.
review_note: Replication used digraph typing and choice reaction time with 65 typists versus 80 in the original.

effect_name: Negative affect and visual memory precision
effect_claim: Negative affect increases the precision of representations stored in visual working memory.
effect_claim_quote: However, in both memory systems, this decrease in capacity was accompanied by an increase in precision.
original_title: Negative affect improves the quality of memories: Trading capacity for precision in sensory and working memory.
replication_title: No evidence that self-rated negative emotion boosts visual working memory precision.
replication_target_quote: Two recent studies (Spachtholz et al., 2014; Xie & Zhang, 2016) reported that self-reported negative emotion boosted the precision with which information was stored in visual working memory.
outcome_quote: six experiments showed substantial evidence against changes in visual working memory precision (and quantity) under negative (and positive) emotion in comparison with neutral, whereas one condition, in one study, showed increased precision under both negative and positive emotion compared with neutral.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
review_note: Six experiments did not reproduce the precision gain, but one condition in one study did; classified mixed.

effect_name: Group Knobe effect
effect_claim: The positive or negative character of a group action’s side effect changes whether people attribute intention to the group.
effect_claim_quote: Building upon this research, we found evidence that the positiveness or negativeness of side-effects of group actions influences people’s willingness to attribute intentions to groups (Experiment 1a)
original_title: “The Group Knobe Effect”: evidence that people intuitively attribute agency and responsibility to groups
replication_title: The Group Knobe Effect revisited: epistemic and doxastic side-effect effects in intuitive judgments concerning group agents
replication_target_quote: In this paper, we investigate the effect described in the literature as the Group Knobe Effect, which is an asymmetry in ascription of intentionality of negative and positive side-effects of an action performed by a group agent.
outcome_quote: We successfully replicate two studies originally conducted by Michael and Szigeti (Philos Explor 22:44–61, 2019), who observed this effect
review_note: The original abstract reports a group intention attribution effect of side effect valence; the later abstract explicitly says its Group Knobe experiments replicated.

effect_name: Neuroticism before dementia diagnosis
effect_claim: People who later receive a dementia diagnosis show rising neuroticism before diagnosis.
effect_claim_quote: Individuals who were eventually diagnosed with dementia showed a significant increase in neuroticism preceding diagnosis of dementia.
original_title: Trajectories of Personality Traits Preceding Dementia Diagnosis
replication_title: Increases in Neuroticism May Be an Early Indicator of Dementia: A Coordinated Analysis
replication_target_quote: One prospective study found increases in neuroticism preceding dementia diagnosis (Yoneda, T., Rush, J., Berg, A. I., Johansson, B., & Piccinin, A. M. (2017). Trajectories of personality traits preceding dementia diagnosis. The Journals of Gerontology. Series B, Psychological Sciences and Social Sciences, 72, 922-931. doi:10.1093/geronb/gbw006).
outcome_quote: growth curve analyses consistently revealed significant linear increases in neuroticism preceding dementia diagnosis in both datasets and in individuals with mild cognitive impairment.
original_journal: The Journals of Gerontology Series B
replication_journal: The Journals of Gerontology Series B

effect_name: Averaged music performance preference
effect_claim: A mathematically averaged music performance is rated more highly than most individual performances.
effect_claim_quote: The average performance was rated second highest in quality, even though it was judged second lowest in individuality.
original_title: The Aesthetic Quality of a Quantitatively Average Music Performance: Two Preliminary Experiments
replication_title: Tendency Towards the Average? The Aesthetic Evaluation of a Quantitatively Average Music Performance
replication_target_quote: The present study has investigated the minimal-distance hypothesis in music (Langlois & Roggman, 1990; Repp, 1997) by replicating Repp's original study (1997) on the aesthetic quality of an averaged performance—compared to individual interpretations—of Robert Schumann's Träumerei (Op. 15, No. 7).
outcome_quote: The average performance was rated better than the individual performances, and the lowest rated performance from the original study was rated lowest in this replication as well (large effect size).
review_note: Original average ranked second of eleven, so the claim is higher than most individual performances rather than all.

effect_name: Positive psychology exercise benefits
effect_claim: Some positive psychology exercises increase happiness and decrease depressive symptoms relative to a control exercise.
effect_claim_quote: They found that 3 of the interventions lastingly increased happiness and decreased depressive symptoms.
original_title: Positive Psychology Progress: Empirical Validation of Interventions.
replication_title: A replication and conceptual evaluation of commonly used positive psychology interventions
replication_target_quote: The findings of the original study were not fully replicated. Specifically, although all groups showed an increase in happiness levels and a decrease in depression levels over time, there was no differential effect between the PPEs and the control exercise.
outcome_quote: there was no differential effect between the PPEs and the control exercise
review_note: The later thesis tests three of the original five positive exercises in an Australian sample; no advantage over control.

effect_name: Object word spatial interference
effect_claim: Words for objects usually located high or low hinder detection of targets in the corresponding visual location.
effect_claim_quote: words denoting objects that typically occur high in the visual field hindered identification of targets appearing at the top of the display, whereas words denoting low objects hindered target identification at the bottom of the display
original_title: Head Up, Foot Down
replication_title: Foot or X down? Response compatibility but no effects of the object's typical location. Several failures to replicate Estes, Verges & Barsalou (2008)
replication_target_quote: Estes, Verges, Barsalou (2008) reported that centrally presented words denoting objects usually appearing in the upper/lower portion of the visual field interfere with the identification of unrelated targets appearing up/down on the display, respectively.
outcome_quote: In a series of 6 experiments, run in different laboratories, we tried to replicate this pattern of results, without success.

effect_name: Predatory helpfulness relational shift
effect_claim: Survivors of sex trafficking report a shift from apparently helpful grooming to sexual exploitation.
effect_claim_quote: 17 of the 19 participants were able to identify a distinct relational shift between this grooming stage and the recruitment stage, where CSE began.
original_title: Predatory Helpfulness: An Empirical Framework to Identify Fraudulent Tactics Used by Pimps to Recruit and Commercially Sexually Exploit Young Girls and Women
replication_title: Predatory Helpfulness: A Replication (and Expansion) Study Examining Grooming and Recruitment Tactics in Sex Trafficking
replication_target_quote: Focusing on the fraud and coercion, Basra et al. proposed a new framework, Predatory Helpfulness, which consists of a two-prong process of both a grooming stage priming the victim for seduction, and a recruitment stage which activates the victim into exploitative commercial sex.
outcome_quote: 50 of the 59 participants also spontaneously identified a relational shift that occurred between the grooming and recruitment stages.
review_note: Independent qualitative sample of 59 survivors versus 19 in the original; the relational shift is the paired finding.

effect_name: Parent art therapy group helpfulness
effect_claim: Parents of children with chronic pain find group art therapy helpful and supportive.
effect_claim_quote: Parents enjoyed participating in the group, agreed that they would try art therapy again, and found it to be a helpful, supportive, and validating experience.
original_title: Connecting Parents of Children With Chronic Pain Through Art Therapy
replication_title: Replicating a Therapeutic Art Group Protocol for Parents of Youth With Chronic Pain
replication_target_quote: This study measured the feasibility of implementing a published, parent-only group-based therapeutic art intervention in an IIPT program
outcome_quote: Parents attended 69% of sessions, reported little difficulty attending, and reported a high degree of satisfaction, helpfulness, and support.
replication_journal: The Journal of Child Life Psychosocial Theory and Practice
review_note: The repeated outcome is parent reported satisfaction and helpfulness, not pain relief or a treatment efficacy claim.

effect_name: Unconscious sentence meaning processing
effect_claim: The meaning of masked word sequences is processed without awareness, causing more negative expressions to break into awareness sooner.
effect_claim_quote: the more negative a verbal expression is, the more quickly it becomes conscious
original_title: Reading and doing arithmetic nonconsciously
replication_title: The importance of awareness for understanding language.
replication_target_quote: Sklar et al. (2012) found that sentences, masked from consciousness using the technique of continuous flash suppression (CFS), broke into awareness more rapidly when their meanings were more unusual or more emotionally negative
outcome_quote: we found no evidence that the meaning of a phrase or word could be understood without awareness
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

effect_name: Test anxiety desensitization and grades
effect_claim: Desensitization for test anxiety improves community college students’ grade point averages.
effect_claim_quote: The experimental group showed a significant increase in grade point average from 1.73, term before, to 2.39 at the end of the treatment term.
original_title: DESENSITIZATION OF TEST‐ANXIOUS URBAN COMMUNITY COLLEGE STUDENTS AND RESULTING CHANGES IN GRADE POINT AVERAGE
replication_title: Desensitization of test anxious urban community-college students and resulting changes in grade point average: A replication
replication_target_quote: These results support those reported by Hudesman and Wiesner (1979) on a similar sample.
outcome_quote: At the end of the treatment semester, results indicated that students who participated in the program had improved their academic averages more than the control group, as measured by Mann-Whitney U test.
review_note: The replication used a larger self referred community college sample and compared GPA improvement with controls.

effect_name: Instructor sexual orientation credibility bias
effect_claim: Students rate a male instructor as less credible when he identifies as gay than when he identifies as straight.
effect_claim_quote: Findings indicate that students perceive a gay teacher as significantly less credible than a straight teacher.
original_title: Coming Out in the Classroom... An Occupational Hazard?: The Influence of Sexual Orientation on Teacher Credibility and Perceived Student Learning
replication_title: Is Coming Out in the Community College Classroom an “Occupational Hazard?”
replication_target_quote: This study is a replication of Russ et al.’s (2002) work, which showed that students’ credibility beliefs about and perceived learning from a male university instructor were negatively affected when he identified as gay.
outcome_quote: Participants as a collective did not provide significantly different ratings for any dimension of credibility nor for perceptions of learning in either condition.
review_note: Replication uses community college students rather than the university students in the original.

effect_name: Context driven Stroop control
effect_claim: Context cues modulate the Stroop effect even for items without frequency bias.
effect_claim_quote: In particular, we demonstrate that context-driven processes can modulate the size of the Stroop effect for frequency-unbiased item types.
original_title: Short article: The flexibility of context-specific control: Evidence for context-driven generalization of item-specific control settings
replication_title: Limits on the generalizability of context-driven control
replication_target_quote: In the current paper, we attempt to replicate and extend one such finding [Crump, M. J. C., & Milliken, B. (2009). The flexibility of context-specific control: Evidence for context-driven generalization of item-specific control settings. The Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 62, 1523-1532].
outcome_quote: Across three experiments we fail to find evidence for context-driven control in the absence of stimulus frequency confounds.

effect_name: Fast mapping of novel constructions
effect_claim: Children learn a novel sentence construction from examples and apply it to new appearance scenes.
effect_claim_quote: Children who watched the videos and heard the accompanying description were able to match new descriptions that used the novel construction with new scenes of appearance.
original_title: Fast mapping between a phrasal form and meaning
replication_title: Can children use similarity between actions to learn grammar?
replication_target_quote: The present study was a replication and extension of Casenhiser and Goldberg (2005).
outcome_quote: The children in both conditions performed significantly worse on the appearance items than the causative trials, which fails to replicate the original study.
review_note: Later thesis varies training conditions but explicitly reports failure of the original novel construction result.

effect_name: Social class and income estimates
effect_claim: Middle class children estimate occupational incomes higher than working class children do.
effect_claim_quote: Middle‐class children, as compared to working‐class children, not only made higher overall estimates of income for all the occupations considered but also perceived a greater spread in incomes and a clearer division between manual and non‐manual occupations.
original_title: Children's representation of economic inequalities: The effects of social class
replication_title: Children's representations of economic inequality: A replication
