replication_target_quote: In a study of children's estimates of occupational incomes Emler & Dickinson (1985) found substantial social class but no age differences in a Scottish sample, a result they interpreted as supporting Moscovici's theory of social representation. The main part of that study was replicated with West German children of the age range 8–12, whose parents were also interviewed.
outcome_quote: Significant age but no social class differences were found, estimates of both types progressively converging upon true values.
review_note: Replication is in West German children rather than the original Scottish sample.

original_title: THE EFFECTS OF A SELF‐INSTRUCTIONAL PACKAGE ON OVERACTIVE PRESCHOOL BOYS
replication_title: EFFECTS OF SELF‐INSTRUCTIONAL TRAINING ON SECOND‐ AND THIRD‐GRADE HYPERACTIVE CHILDREN: A FAILURE TO REPUCATE
effect_name: Self-instructional training increases classroom on-task behavior
effect_claim: A brief self-instructional package increased classroom on-task behavior among overactive preschool boys.
effect_claim_quote: On-task behaviors increased dramatically concomitant with the introduction of the self-instructional package
replication_target_quote: Bornstein and Quevillon (1976) demonstrated generalization from a 2-hour self-instructional training session to on-task behavior in the classroom
outcome_quote: The results of Bornstein and Quevillon's (1976) study were not replicated
review_note: Replication tested 7- and 8-year-old children rather than preschoolers; a later token program increased on-task behavior, but self-instruction alone did not.

original_title: Inter- vs Intra-Modal Performance of College Men and Women
replication_title: Inter- vs Intramodal Performance of College Men and Women: A Replication
effect_name: Women outperform men on an auditory-visual matching task
effect_claim: Female college students made more correct responses than male college students on temporal auditory-visual matching tasks.
effect_claim_quote: Women made significantly more correct responses than men.
replication_target_quote: Results are consistent with an earlier report by Gould (1977).
outcome_quote: women made significantly more correct responses than men.
review_note: The unexpected sex difference replicated; the absence of an intermodal versus intramodal performance difference also recurred but is outside this claim.

original_title: Why people are reluctant to tempt fate.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Magical thinking in predictions of negative events: Evidence for tempting fate but not for a protection effect
effect_name: Tempting-fate actions raise perceived chance of negative outcomes
effect_claim: People judged a negative outcome as more likely after an action perceived as tempting fate.
effect_claim_quote: actions that tempt fate increase the likelihood of negative outcomes.
replication_target_quote: two replications of a tempting fate experiment reported in Risen and Gilovich (2008)
outcome_quote: did replicate the tempting fate effect.
review_note: The separate protection-effect experiments targeted Tykocinski (2008) and failed; that failure does not apply to this original pair.

original_title: Implicit and explicit learning: Individual differences and IQ.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition
replication_title: COGNITIVE ABILITIES, CHUNK-STRENGTH, AND FREQUENCY EFFECTS IN IMPLICIT ARTIFICIAL GRAMMAR AND INCIDENTAL L2 LEARNING: REPLICATIONS OF REBER, WALKENFELD, AND HERNSTADT (1991) AND KNOWLTON AND SQUIRE (1996) AND THEIR RELEVANCE FOR SLA
effect_name: Explicit learning shows more individual variation than implicit grammar learning
effect_claim: Individual performance varied more in explicit series-completion learning than in implicit artificial-grammar learning.
effect_claim_quote: Substantial individual differences were found between subjects on the explicit task; relatively small individual differences were found on the implicit task.
replication_target_quote: replications of studies of implicit artificial grammar (AG) learning and explicit series-solution learning
outcome_quote: there was significantly greater variance in explicit compared to implicit learning.
review_note: The variance result replicated; the replication found an IQ relation to implicit learning that differed from the original.

original_title: Incidental Learning and Long‐Term Retention of New Word Meanings From Stories: The Effect of Number of Exposures
replication_title: Contextual Learning of New Meanings for Familiar Word Forms from Reading and Listening to Stories
effect_name: More story exposures improve recall of new word meanings
effect_claim: Repeated story encounters with new meanings of familiar words incrementally improved later recall of those meanings.
effect_claim_quote: Accuracy in cued recall of novel meanings showed a linear, incremental increase with more exposures.
replication_target_quote: Study 1 was a conceptual replication and extension of Hulme et al. (2018).
outcome_quote: more explicit knowledge of the meaning was produced with more exposures.
review_note: Study 1 of a university-repository thesis supplies the replication; its immediate recall supports the exposure gradient, but does not test the original one-week retention claim.

original_title: Gifted Adolescents' Attitudes Toward Their Giftedness
replication_title: Gifted Adolescents' Attitudes Toward Their Giftedness: A Partial Replication
effect_name: Gifted adolescents hold multifaceted views of giftedness
effect_claim: Gifted adolescents held mixed, multidimensional views of their own giftedness.
effect_claim_quote: Gifted adolescents have strongly mixed attitudes about their giftedness.
replication_target_quote: Kerr, Colangelo, and Gaeth (1988) assessed gifted adolescents' perceptions of their own and others' views
outcome_quote: views of the gifted label and its effects are multifaceted
review_note: Specific positive and negative facets differed from the original, so only the multidimensional pattern is coded as replicated.

original_title: Perceived Parental Acceptance-Rejection and Artistic Preference
replication_title: Perceived Parental Acceptance-Rejection and Artistic Preference: Replication Thirty Years Later
effect_name: Perceived parental acceptance predicts preference for complex art
effect_claim: Adults recalling more parental warmth and acceptance tended to prefer more complex graphic art.
effect_claim_quote: preference for complex works of art is associated with parental warmth and acceptance.
replication_target_quote: The purpose of our study was to replicate Rohner and Frampton’s (1982) work
outcome_quote: perceived maternal acceptance in childhood was associated with a preference for more complex art forms [similar to Rohner and Frampton’s (1982) findings]. However, our participants’ perceived paternal acceptance in childhood had no association with artistic preference.
review_note: Maternal association replicated, paternal association did not; recalled acceptance and art preference are observational.

original_title: The Conceptualisation of Dreams by People with Intellectual Disabilities
original_journal: Journal of Applied Research in Intellectual Disabilities
replication_title: The conceptualisation of dreams by adults with intellectual disabilities: relationship with theory of mind abilities and verbal ability
effect_name: Some adults with intellectual disabilities see dreams as public physical events
effect_claim: A substantial share of adults with intellectual disabilities misunderstood dreams as perceptually public or physical.
effect_claim_quote: 40% of their replies in answer to questions regarding the non‐physical, private nature of dreams were incorrect
replication_target_quote: aim of the current study was to replicate the results found by Stenfert Kroese et al.
outcome_quote: many adults with ID tend to think that dreams take place around them, can be witnessed by others, can be touched and manipulated, can be shared by others
review_note: Replication confirms the qualitative pattern, not the original 40-percent estimate for each question.

original_title: The IAT shows no evidence for Kandinsky's color-shape associations
replication_title: Color-Shape Associations Revealed with Implicit Association Tests
effect_name: Kandinsky color-shape pairs show little implicit-association evidence
effect_claim: Implicit Association Tests gave little support for Kandinsky's proposed yellow-triangle, red-square, and blue-circle pairings.
effect_claim_quote: there is no implicit association between the original color-form combinations.
replication_target_quote: Makin and Wuerger tested the theory using the Implicit Association Test (IAT) and did not find clear evidence for Kandinsky's color-shape associations
outcome_quote: found similar results to those of Makin and Wuerger, showing little support for Kandinsky's theory.
review_note: British null pattern recurred in a Japanese sample; a different Japanese color-shape mapping did show positive IAT evidence.

original_title: Improving the interview skills of college students using behavioral skills training
replication_title: Using Web-Based Behavioral Skills Training to Teach Online Interview Skills to College Students
effect_name: Behavioral-skills training improves college interview skills
effect_claim: Behavioral skills training improved college students' targeted job-interview skills.
effect_claim_quote: All participants acquired targeted skills
replication_target_quote: replicated previous research on teaching interview skills with BST by using this procedure to teach interview skills to college students
outcome_quote: All participant performance improved from baseline to post-training across all targeted dependent variables.
review_note: Replication moved from simulated in-person interview practice to synchronous web-based video; it is a procedural extension.

original_title: A hard to read font reduces the causality bias
replication_title: Does perceptual disfluency affect the illusion of causality?
effect_name: Hard-to-read fonts reduce illusory causal judgments
effect_claim: Presenting a noncontingent causal-learning task in a hard-to-read font reduced the illusion of causality.
effect_claim_quote: This effect was reduced when the same task was presented in a hard-to-read font.
replication_target_quote: a hard-to-read font led to a decrease in the magnitude of the illusion
outcome_quote: we found no discernible effect of font type on the magnitude of the illusion
review_note: The direct font manipulation was Experiment 2; a separate contrast manipulation was also null but is outside this pair's coded target.

original_title: Perseverance in self-perception and social perception: Biased attributional processes in the debriefing paradigm.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Persistence of Impressions of Personal Persuasiveness
effect_name: Discredited performance feedback leaves persistent ability impressions
effect_claim: Initial impressions of a person's ability persisted after the evidence on which they were based was discredited.
effect_claim_quote: Both actors and observers showed substantial perseverance of initial impressions
replication_target_quote: These results replicate previous impression-perseverance findings obtained by Ross, Lepper, and Hubbard (1975)
outcome_quote: initial assessments of their persuasive ability persisted after the evidential value of apparent success or failure upon which these impressions were based was fully discredited.
review_note: Conceptual replication used persuasive ability rather than the original discrimination task and a different discrediting procedure.

original_title: Semantic effects in single-word naming.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition
replication_title: What exactly interacts with spelling--sound consistency in word naming?
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition
effect_name: Imageability benefits naming low-frequency exception words
effect_claim: Low-frequency exception words with concrete, imageable meanings were named more accurately and quickly than abstract exceptions.
effect_claim_quote: Participants were slower and more error prone when naming exception words with abstract meanings
replication_target_quote: Experiment 4 replicated Experiment 2 of E. Strain, K. E. Patterson, and M. S. Seidenberg's (1995) study
outcome_quote: obtained the same apparent effect of imageability on naming. That effect disappeared when AoA was entered as a covariate.
review_note: Unadjusted pattern replicated, but age-of-acquisition adjustment removed it; the original abstract did not address this covariate.

original_title: Volitional facilitation of difficult intentions: Joint activation of intention memory and positive affect removes Stroop interference.
replication_title: Intention memory and achievement motivation: Volitional facilitation and inhibition as a function of affective contents of need-related stimuli.
replication_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
effect_name: Positive-affect primes reduce Stroop interference
effect_claim: Brief exposure to positive-affect words reduced or removed Stroop interference in difficult-intention tasks.
effect_claim_quote: Removal of Stroop interference was obtained after exposure to words eliciting positive affect.
replication_target_quote: Replicating findings of J. Kuhl and M. Kazén (1999)
outcome_quote: reduction or removal of Stroop interference was achieved after short exposure to primes eliciting positive affect.
review_note: Replication narrowed the effect to achievement-related positive primes across five studies.

original_title: False fame prevented: Avoiding fluency effects without judgmental correction.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: On the (elusive) role of oral motor-movements in fluency-based memory illusions.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition
effect_name: Oral-motor interference blocks the false-fame effect
effect_claim: A secondary oral-motor task reduced the false-fame effect from repeated person-name exposure.
effect_claim_quote: blocking such pronunciation simulations through a secondary oral motor task decreased the false-fame effect
replication_target_quote: fluency effects are eliminated if such judgments are made while these muscles are otherwise engaged
outcome_quote: We were also unable to replicate the finding that an oral-motor task blocks the false fame effect (Topolinski & Strack, 2010).
review_note: Replicators compared gum chewing with a manual-motor task; fluency illusions remained.

effect_name: Toddlers trust accurate speakers
effect_claim: Toddlers learn new words more reliably from speakers who previously labeled familiar objects correctly.
effect_claim_quote: children performed less systematically in response to an inaccurate than to an accurate source.
original_title: Sensitivity of 24-month-olds to the prior inaccuracy of the source: Possible mechanisms.
replication_title: Knowing How You Know: Toddlers Reevaluate Words Learned From an Unreliable Speaker
replication_target_quote: Experiment 1 replicated previous research (Koenig & Woodward, 2010)
outcome_quote: children displayed better performance in a word learning test when they learned words from a speaker who has previously revealed themself as reliable
review_note: Original toddlers were 24 months old; replication toddlers averaged 30 months. Verdict concerns the initial word-learning contrast, not the later reevaluation experiment.

effect_name: Motor errors disrupt working memory
effect_claim: Making a motor response error while holding information in mind worsens subsequent working-memory performance.
effect_claim_quote: Motor error commission during the delay period consistently reduced accuracy on the WM probe
original_title: Action errors impair active working memory maintenance.
replication_title: Impact of motor error processing on performance on a working memory task: effect of modulating cognitive load in high and low span groups
replication_target_quote: The presented study replicates the ERIAM protocol of Wessel et al. (2022)
outcome_quote: Results show a replication of ERIAM effect in our sample.
review_note: Replication changed the working-memory probe to recall and varied cognitive load. The error-related impairment appeared under load conditions that differed by memory-span group.

effect_name: Switching toward memory has larger attention cost
effect_claim: Switching attention from something seen to something held in memory is slower than switching from memory to perception.
effect_claim_quote: this switch cost was asymmetric, being substantially larger when switching from (external) perception to (internal) memory than the other way around.
original_title: Attentional flexibility is imbalanced: Asymmetric cost for switches between external and internal attention.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
replication_title: More efficient shielding for internal than external attention? Evidence from asymmetrical switch costs.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
replication_target_quote: The authors observed an asymmetrical switch cost, which was larger when switching toward internal than external material
outcome_quote: After replicating the original asymmetry (Experiment 1)
review_note: The source abstracts compare directional switch costs, not overall speed on internal versus external trials.

effect_name: Fractions draw more negative math attitudes
effect_claim: People report more negative attitudes toward fractions than toward whole numbers.
effect_claim_quote: The vast majority of children and adults reported negative attitudes toward fractions despite having positive attitudes toward whole numbers.
original_title: Children’s and Adults’ Math Attitudes Are Differentiated by Number Type
replication_title: Perceptions of ease and difficulty, but not growth mindset, relate to specific math attitudes
replication_target_quote: Replicating prior work (Sidney, Thompson, Fitzsimmons, & Taber, 2021)
outcome_quote: college students endorsed more negative attitudes about fractions than WNs and percentages.
review_note: Original covered children and adults; replication sampled college students and also compared percentages.

effect_name: False certainty in low-risk HIV counseling
effect_claim: Many counselors tell low-risk clients that a positive HIV test means infection is certain, despite possible false positives.
effect_claim_quote: half of the counsellors told the client that if he tests positive, it is 100% certain that he is infected with the virus.
original_title: AIDS counselling for low-risk clients
replication_title: What Counselors Tell Low-Risk Clients About HIV Test Performance
replication_target_quote: Sixteen years later we assessed whether HIV counseling in Germany has improved by replicating the original study
outcome_quote: About half of professional counselors communicated the illusion of certainty for sensitivity (15 of 30), specificity (16 of 30), and the PPV (18 of 30).
review_note: The paper describes failure to improve counseling. For this original finding, continued false certainty is a successful replication. Test performance itself improved between studies.

effect_name: Survival processing increases directed forgetting
effect_claim: Processing words for survival relevance increases intentional forgetting compared with processing them for moving relevance.
effect_claim_quote: survival encoding brought about greater remembering (after the remember cue) and forgetting (after the forget cue).
original_title: Effects of survival processing on list method directed forgetting
replication_title: Survival processing and directed forgetting: enhanced memory for both to-be-remembered and to-be-forgotten information
replication_target_quote: In Experiment 1, we did not replicate the findings of (Parker, A., Parkin, A., & Dagnall, N. (2021)
outcome_quote: making survival ratings and moving ratings yielded a similar cost of directed forgetting for List 1 items.
review_note: Verdict concerns the relative cost of list-method directed forgetting; the follow-up also tested an item method and found other memory benefits.

effect_name: Regular ordinals precede irregular forms
effect_claim: Dutch-speaking children learn regular ordinal words before irregular ordinal words.
effect_claim_quote: Not only is the tiered pattern absent in regular low ordinals, we also see that it takes time for children to link drie ‘three’ to irregular derde ‘third.’
original_title: Ordinals are not as easy as one, two, three: The acquisition of cardinals and ordinals in Dutch
replication_title: Many systems, one strategy: Acquiring ordinals in Dutch and English
replication_journal: Glossa a journal of general linguistics
replication_target_quote: offer a replication of the core findings in Meyer et al. (2018)
outcome_quote: Dutch-speaking children acquire irregular forms (such as derde ‘third’) after they acquire regular synthetic forms (such as vierde ‘fourth’)
review_note: Replication added English learners; verdict is the Dutch regular-versus-irregular acquisition order.

effect_name: Visual change detection without awareness
effect_claim: People can detect visual changes even when they are unaware that a change occurred.
effect_claim_quote: sensitivity to change does occur in the absence of awareness
original_title: Change Detection Without Awareness: Do Explicit Reports Underestimate the Representation of Change in the Visual System?
replication_title: Implicit detection of change: Can we do without awareness?
replication_target_quote: D. Fernandez-Duque and I. M. Thornton (2000) seemingly demonstrated “unconscious detection of change”
outcome_quote: both experiments failed to replicate D. Fernandez-Duque and I. M. Thornton’s finding of an increase in change detection for unaware trials.
review_note: Follow-up found above-chance detection when adding a control condition, but argues a conscious strategy can explain that result; the original unaware-trial increase did not recur.

effect_name: Thirteen-month-olds comprehend familiar words
effect_claim: Thirteen-month-old infants look longer at the named object when hearing a familiar word than when hearing a nonsense word.
effect_claim_quote: 13-month-olds directed their looking time significantly longer at the referent of the known word when that word was uttered than when the nonsense word was uttered.
original_title: Semantic Comprehension in Infancy: A Signal Detection Analysis
replication_title: Overextensions in early language comprehension: evidence from a signal detection approach
replication_target_quote: Experiment 1 replicated the original findings of Thomas et al.
outcome_quote: 13-month-olds understand a word that a parent reported they would understand and did not understand a word that a parent reported they would not.
review_note: Verdict is for Experiment 1 using parent-reported known versus unknown words; Experiment 2 examined overextension.

effect_name: Message interpretation and false-belief tasks
effect_claim: Young children find a false-belief message task easier than a classic false-belief prediction task.
effect_claim_quote: children performed better on the message-desire discrepant task than on a false belief task.
original_title: Children's Interpretation of Messages from a Speaker with a False Belief
replication_title: Young children's false-belief reasoning: Interpretation of messages is no easier than the classic task.
replication_target_quote: In Study 3 we followed the Robinson and Mitchell procedure precisely
outcome_quote: failed to replicate the contrast reported previously.
review_note: The original advantage appeared in one of five investigations; follow-up found no advantage in matched tasks or in a close procedural replication.

effect_name: Direct speech activates voice-selective cortex
effect_claim: Silent reading of direct speech activates voice-selective auditory cortex more than reading equivalent indirect speech.
effect_claim_quote: silent reading of direct versus indirect speech engenders differential brain activation in voice-selective areas of the auditory cortex.
original_title: Silent Reading of Direct versus Indirect Speech Activates Voice-selective Areas in the Auditory Cortex
replication_title: Processing Speech and Thoughts during Silent Reading: Direct Reference Effects for Speech by Fictional Characters in Voice-Selective Auditory Cortex and a Theory-of-Mind Network
replication_target_quote: Previous research has shown that direct reference to speech in stories
outcome_quote: Evidence of elevated auditory cortex responses to direct speech over indirect speech was observed, replicating previously reported effects
review_note: Replication used short fictional stories and contrasted direct speech with indirect speech and direct thoughts.

effect_name: Heavy TV viewing and accessible social estimates
effect_claim: Heavier television viewers give higher frequency estimates about social phenomena and answer those questions faster.
effect_claim_quote: those subjects who watch comparatively more television not only overestimate frequency or probability but also give faster responses to various types of cultivation questions.
original_title: Processes and Effects in the Construction of Social Reality
replication_title: Psychological Processes Underlying Cultivation Effects Further Tests of Construct Accessibility
replication_target_quote: replicating the findings of Shrum and O'Gunn (1993)
outcome_quote: Heavy viewers gave significantly higher frequency estimates (cultivation effect) and responded significantly faster (accessibility effect) than did light viewers
review_note: Replication focused on soap-opera viewing and tested several social topics; mediation held for some but not all.

effect_name: Infant attachment distress and serotonin allele
effect_claim: Infants carrying the short 5-HTTLPR allele show greater distress in attachment assessments.
effect_claim_quote: The short allele for 5-HTTLPR was associated with attachment classifications characterized by higher emotional distress.
original_title: Genetic and Caregiving-Based Contributions to Infant Attachment
replication_title: Molecular-genetic correlates of infant attachment: A cautionary tale
replication_target_quote: this paper attempts, but fails, to replicate a recent finding by Raby et al. (2012)
outcome_quote: this paper attempts, but fails, to replicate a recent finding by Raby et al. (2012)
review_note: Verdict is for short-allele variation in distress during the Strange Situation, not the broader caregiver-responsiveness finding.

effect_name: Foreign language reduces illusory causality
effect_claim: Using a foreign language reduces mistaken judgments that unrelated events are causally connected.
effect_claim_quote: those performing the task in their foreign language were more accurate in detecting that the two events were causally unrelated.
original_title: Thinking in a Foreign language reduces the causality bias
replication_title: The foreign language effect in the illusion of causality: Evidence of absence
replication_target_quote: We conducted a replication study with a large sample ( N = 220)
outcome_quote: our results did not support the original findings.
review_note: Replication tested the same proposed foreign-language debiasing effect in a larger sample.

effect_name: Team-task ratings distinguish interdependent work
effect_claim: Ratings of team relatedness and workflow distinguish interdependent tasks from individual tasks.
effect_claim_quote: the scales differentiated between tasks that were predetermined to be individual versus team based.
original_title: Team Task Analysis: Identifying Tasks and Jobs That Are Team Based
original_journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
replication_title: Team Task Analysis
replication_journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
replication_target_quote: constructive replication and extension of Arthur, Edwards, Bell, Villado, and Bennett (2005)
outcome_quote: team relatedness and team workflow effectively differentiated between tasks with varying levels of interdependency
review_note: Original used student teams in a combat simulation; follow-up used F-16 pilot teams and expert-rated task interdependency.

effect_name: Distinct coercive-sexuality subtype of psychopathy
effect_claim: Early and coercive sexual behavior forms a distinct category among male sex offenders assessed for psychopathy.
effect_claim_quote: Taxometric analyses gave evidence of a natural discontinuity underlying coercive and precocious sexuality.
original_title: Coercive and Precocious Sexuality as a Fundamental Aspect of Psychopathy
replication_title: In search of the psychopathic sexuality taxon: Indicator size does matter
replication_target_quote: attempted to replicate the hypothesized psychopathic sexuality taxon
outcome_quote: Clearly dimensional results, however, were obtained when higher correlating and more valid quasi-continuous indicators were analyzed
review_note: Original taxon was found with weaker dichotomized indicators; follow-up found dimensional results with stronger indicators and several methods.

effect_name: Expected testing enhances sleep consolidation
effect_claim: Sleep strengthens learned material more when people expect to be tested on it later.
effect_claim_quote: the mere expectancy that a memory will be used in a future test determines whether or not sleep significantly benefits consolidation of this memory.
original_title: Sleep Selectively Enhances Memory Expected to Be of Future Relevance
replication_title: Future-relevant memories are not selectively strengthened during sleep
replication_target_quote: sought to replicate the seminal finding that the memory benefits of sleep are enhanced when people expect a future test [Wilhelm et al., 2011].
outcome_quote: knowledge of an upcoming test had no impact on sleep-associated consolidation in either experiment
review_note: Follow-up observed a general sleep benefit but no additional benefit from expecting a test; verdict is limited to the interaction.

effect_name: Dissociative PTSD subtype
effect_claim: A distinct subgroup of people with PTSD shows especially pronounced dissociative symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: a small but distinctly dissociative subgroup that composed 12% of individuals with a current diagnosis of PTSD.
original_title: A Latent Class Analysis of Dissociation and Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
replication_title: The dissociative post‐traumatic stress disorder ( PTSD ) subtype: A treatment outcome cohort study in veterans with PTSD
replication_target_quote: This study aimed to replicate findings of a dissociative PTSD subtype
outcome_quote: a subsample of severely dissociative veterans was identified
review_note: Original latent analysis produced three classes including a dissociative subtype; follow-up found four classes including a dissociative subtype in treatment-seeking veterans.

effect_name: Childhood trauma and cannabis psychosis interaction
effect_claim: Childhood trauma and cannabis use interact beyond their separate effects to raise psychotic symptom risk.
effect_claim_quote: However, the presence of both childhood trauma and early cannabis use significantly increased the risk for psychotic symptoms beyond the risk posed by either risk factor alone, indicating that there was a greater than additive interaction between childhood trauma and cannabis use.
original_title: Cannabis use and childhood trauma interact additively to increase the risk of psychotic symptoms in adolescence
replication_title: Replication in two independent population-based samples that childhood maltreatment and cannabis use synergistically impact on psychosis risk
replication_target_quote: To replicate and further investigate this issue, prospective data from two independent population-based studies, the Greek National Perinatal Study (n=1636) and The Netherlands Mental Health Survey and Incidence Study (NEMESIS) (n=4842), were analyzed.
outcome_quote: A significant adjusted interaction between childhood maltreatment and later cannabis use was evident in both samples, indicating that the psychosis-inducing effects of cannabis were stronger in individuals exposed to earlier sexual or physical mistreatment [Greek National Perinatal Study: test for interaction F(2, 1627)=4.18, p=0.02; NEMESIS: test for interaction χ2(3)=8.08, p=0.04].
review_note: The later study uses two independent cohorts and tests the trauma by cannabis interaction on psychotic symptoms.

effect_name: Mortality salience and worldview defence
effect_claim: Mortality reminders increase positive reactions to worldview supporters and negative reactions to worldview critics.
effect_claim_quote: mortality salience led to especially positive reactions to someone who directly praised subjects ' cultural worldviews and especially negative reactions to someone who criticized them
original_title: Evidence for terror management theory II: The effects of mortality salience on reactions to those who threaten or bolster the cultural worldview
replication_title: Mild Depression, Mortality Salience and Defense of the Worldview Evidence of Intensified Terror Management in the Mildly Depressed
replication_target_quote: Two studies were conducted in which mildly depressed and nondepressed American college students contemplated their own mortality or a neutral topic and then evaluated targets who supported or threatened aspects of their worldviews.
outcome_quote: Replicating previous research, subjects who contemplated their own mortality engaged in more defense of the worldview (more positive reactions to worldview supporters and more negative reactions to worldview threateners).
review_note: The later study adds depression as a moderator but reports the original mortality salience worldview defence effect.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

effect_name: Older target overaccommodation
effect_claim: People endorse unnecessary helping behaviour more toward older than younger adults.
effect_claim_quote: In the older conditions, hypotheses were confirmed that participants approved overaccommodative behaviors, endorsed higher warmth and lower competence, and attitudes were modified when the older women contradicted the paternalistic stereotype by declining assistance.
original_title: Benevolent ageism: Attitudes of overaccommodative behavior toward older women
replication_title: Expanding Benevolent Ageism: Replicating Attitudes of Overaccommodation to Older Men
replication_target_quote: In prior work, a female target was offered unnecessary assistance, which is replicated in the current study with a male target.
outcome_quote: Our findings replicated earlier work in that overaccommodative behaviors were endorsed more so for the older target than the younger target, which corroborates support for the Stereotype Content Model in that older adults are viewed paternalistically.
review_note: The original vignette used a female target; the replication includes male and female targets.

effect_name: Behavioral sunk cost choices
effect_claim: Prior investments of effort or time can lead people to continue a choice despite its sunk cost.
effect_claim_quote: we argue that, through an effort-justification mechanism, people account for the amount of behavioral resources invested when selecting an alternative, in which case they may fall prey to purely behavioral sunk-cost effects. The results of two experiments support this prediction.
original_title: Sunk‐Cost Effects on Purely Behavioral Investments
replication_title: Behavioral Investments in the Short Term Fail to Produce a Sunk Cost Effect
replication_target_quote: In Studies 1 and 2, we attempted to observe whether this effect occurs for short-term behavioral investments.
outcome_quote: In both studies, a reverse, or no sunk cost effect was found.
review_note: The later study tests short term behavioral investments; its primary studies find reverse or no sunk cost effect, while a different hypothetical scenario showed an effect.

effect_name: WAIS Block Design versus Digit Symbol in alcoholism
effect_claim: Alcohol dependent adults score lower on WAIS Block Design than on WAIS Digit Symbol.
effect_claim_quote: A clear asymmetry was found between the tests, the Block Design being poorer than the Digit Symbol.
original_title: AN ASYMMETRY BETWEEN THE WAIS DIGIT SYMBOL AND BLOCK DESIGN SCORES IN ABSTINENT ALCOHOLICS
replication_title: WAIS Digit Symbol and Block Design Scores in Abstinent Alcoholics: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Previous work has indicated that alcoholics perform more poorly on the Finnish WAIS Block Design than on the Digit Symbol. The purpose of the present study was to replicate that result.
outcome_quote: The same kind of asymmetry was found between the tests, scores on the Block Design being poorer than those on Digit Symbol.
review_note: Original and replication abstracts identify the same measured effect and result.

effect_name: Awareness and emotional attentional blink
effect_claim: Masked fearful faces reduce the attentional blink, whereas visible fearful faces increase it, compared with neutral faces.
effect_claim_quote: We found that, in comparison with neutral faces, masked fearful faces significantly decreased the AB magnitude (Experiment 1), whereas unmasked fearful faces significantly increased the AB magnitude (Experiment 2).
original_title: Emotional Modulation of the Attentional Blink Is Awareness-Dependent
replication_title: No Evidence for an Awareness-Dependent Emotional Modulation of the Attentional Blink
replication_target_quote: Pictures of faces with emotional expressions presented before a temporal attention task have been reported to affect temporal attention in an awareness-dependent manner: Awareness of a fearful face was linked to an increased deficit in the temporal attention task, while preventing the face from reaching awareness was linked to a decreased deficit, both relative to neutral faces.
outcome_quote: In both experiments the finding of an awareness-dependent emotional modulation of temporal attention through fearful faces could not be replicated, even when data were pooled across experiments.
review_note: Original and replication abstracts identify the same measured effect and result.

effect_name: Salience network connectivity and self control
effect_claim: Higher salience network interaction scores are associated with better real life self control.
effect_claim_quote: Logistic multilevel regression analysis showed that higher NII scores were associated with increased real-life self-control.
original_title: Functional connectivity in a triple-network saliency model is associated with real-life self-control
replication_title: Salience network resting-state functional connectivity predicts self-controlled decision-making
replication_target_quote: Here, we attempted to replicate this result using data from our own study where 121 participants completed an fMRI self-control task comprising real-life scenarios and data from a second study (N = 79) retrieved from OpenNeuro (dataset ID: ds002643) where participants completed an fMRI food choice task.
outcome_quote: We could not replicate the proposed role of salience network resting-state functional connectivity in self-controlled decision-making in either of those data sets.
review_note: The later studies use task decisions rather than daily self control and report the opposite direction of the original network association.

effect_name: Traumatic brain injury and emotional feedback
effect_claim: Adults with severe traumatic brain injury have weaker subjective responses to posed emotional expressions than controls.
effect_claim_quote: TBI participants were globally less responsive to the effects of body and facial feedback than control participants, F(1,50) = 5.89, p = .02, η(2) = .11.
original_title: Emotional Regulation Impairments Following Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: An Investigation of the Body and Facial Feedback Effects
replication_title: Subjective emotional experience and physiological responsivity to posed emotions in people with traumatic brain injury.
replication_target_quote: We failed to replicate past research that demonstrated an impairment in the feedback effect in people with TBI.
outcome_quote: Participants with TBI did not differ from controls in their subjective ratings in response to posed emotional expressions.
review_note: The comparison is the subjective response to posed emotions; later physiological results are a separate outcome.
original_journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society

effect_name: Numeracy moderation of natural frequency benefit
effect_claim: Natural frequency formats improve Bayesian reasoning mainly among people with high numeracy.
effect_claim_quote: the performance-boosting benefits of the natural frequency presentation occurred primarily for participants who scored high in numeracy
original_title: Numeracy, frequency, and Bayesian reasoning
replication_title: When and for whom do frequencies facilitate performance? On the role of numerical literacy
replication_target_quote: This interaction, either that frequencies improve performance only for those of low numeracy or that frequencies work only for those of high numeracy, would suggest that better performance using frequencies could be due to (nonevolutionary) numeracy effects.
outcome_quote: Results from these experiments consistently failed to replicate previous findings of interactions
review_note: The later paper tests several reasoning tasks; the exact paired result is the numeracy by format interaction.

original_title: Resetting capacity limitations revealed by long-lasting elimination of attentional blink through training
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Training-induced Changes in the Dynamics of Attention as Reflected in Pupil Dilation
effect_name: Brief attentional training eliminates the attentional blink
effect_claim: One hour of color-salient target training eliminated the attentional blink in the original behavioral task.
effect_claim_quote: just 1 h of specific attentional training can completely eliminate AB
replication_target_quote: the AB can be eliminated after a 1-hr training with a color-salient T2.
outcome_quote: Behaviorally, we replicated the original training effect with a color-salient T2.
review_note: Behavioral target replicated; the pupil-dilation study proposed a different temporal-expectation mechanism.

original_title: The effect of leg-to-body ratio on male attractiveness depends on the ecological validity of the figures
replication_title: The influence of leg-to-body ratio, arm-to-body ratio and intra-limb ratio on male human attractiveness
effect_name: Slightly longer male legs are rated most attractive
effect_claim: For detailed male-body figures, heterosexual women rated leg-to-body ratios about half a standard deviation above average as most attractive.
effect_claim_quote: optima for more detailed computer-generated images was approximately 0.5 s.d. above the baseline
replication_target_quote: Previous work has focused on leg-to-body ratio (LBR) as a determinant of male attractiveness
outcome_quote: the optimally attractive LBR is approximately 0.5 standard deviations above the baseline.
review_note: The claim is restricted to detailed body figures; the original silhouette condition had a different optimum.

original_title: Happy Now, Tired Later? Extraverted and Conscientious Behavior Are Related to Immediate Mood Gains, but to Later Fatigue
replication_title: Sociable behavior is related to later fatigue: moment-to-moment patterns of behavior and tiredness
effect_name: Extraverted behavior predicts fatigue hours later
effect_claim: Momentary extraverted behavior predicted increased fatigue two to three hours later.
effect_claim_quote: Extraverted and conscientious behavior were concurrently related to positive mood and lower fatigue, but to higher fatigue after a 3-hour delay.
replication_target_quote: The present research attempted to replicate this finding and rule out some alternative explanations.
outcome_quote: extraverted behavior was indeed related to feeling tired 2–3 h later.
review_note: The replication tested extraversion-related delayed fatigue, not the original conscientiousness result.

original_title: Musician advantage for speech-on-speech perception
original_journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
replication_title: Musician Advantage for Segregation of Competing Speech in Native Tonal Language Speakers
effect_name: Musicians outperform nonmusicians on speech-on-speech perception
effect_claim: Musicians performed better than nonmusicians when recognizing speech against competing speech.
effect_claim_quote: there was a strong musician benefit for speech perception in a speech masker.
replication_target_quote: replicate previous English-language musician advantage studies in Mandarin-speaking musicians and nonmusicians.
outcome_quote: For all tests, performance was significantly better for musicians than for nonmusicians.
review_note: Cross-language conceptual replication used Mandarin speech; masker-sex interaction differed from the replicators' prediction.

original_title: Emotion-Regulation Choice
replication_title: Choosing an emotion regulation strategy - The importance of emotional category
effect_name: High emotional intensity shifts regulation choice toward distraction
effect_claim: People preferred reappraisal for low-intensity negative stimuli and distraction for high-intensity negative stimuli.
effect_claim_quote: in low-intensity negative situations, people would show a relative preference to choose to regulate emotions by engagement reappraisal
replication_target_quote: We used the emotion regulation choice task designed by Sheppes et al., (2011)
outcome_quote: when the emotion evoked by stimuli was fear or sadness, participants preferred reappraisal in low intensity and distraction in high intensity conditions.
review_note: Replicated for fear and sadness; disgust elicited distraction regardless of intensity. Reappraisal-affordance result concerned another prior study.

original_title: The Precautionary Principle and Risk Perception: Experimental Studies in the EMF Area
replication_title: Improving Precautionary Communication in the EMF Field? Effects of Making Messages Consistent and Explaining the Effectiveness of Precautions
replication_journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
effect_name: Precautionary EMF messages raise perceived risk
effect_claim: Messages recommending electromagnetic-field precautions increased recipients' perceived health risk from electromagnetic fields.
effect_claim_quote: precautionary measures may trigger concerns, amplify EMF-related risk perceptions
replication_target_quote: precautionary messages have, however, been shown to unintentionally increase risk perceptions about radiofrequency electromagnetic fields
outcome_quote: The original effect of precautionary messages to amplify risk perceptions could not be replicated.
review_note: Australian message experiment also tested wording amendments; those extension effects are outside this pair.

original_title: Giving Leads to Happiness in Young Children
replication_title: Toddlers Are Happier Giving to Others Than to Themselves
effect_name: Toddlers are happier giving than receiving treats
effect_claim: Toddlers showed greater happiness after giving treats to another person than after receiving treats themselves.
effect_claim_quote: toddlers exhibit greater happiness when giving treats to others than receiving treats themselves.
replication_target_quote: This study examined the emotional benefits of sharing in toddlers
outcome_quote: toddlers displayed greater happiness after giving than receiving.
review_note: The original additional costly-versus-costless comparison is outside this claim.

original_title: An Unintentional, Robust, and Replicable Pro-Black Bias in Social Judgment
replication_title: An unintentional pro‐Black bias in judgement among educators
effect_name: Academic admissions show a pro-Black acceptance-criterion bias
effect_claim: In a hypothetical academic honor-society task, participants used a lower acceptance threshold for Black than White applicants.
effect_claim_quote: participants from undergraduate and online samples had a more relaxed acceptance criterion for Black than White candidates
replication_target_quote: investigate whether a sample of education professionals would favour Black or White applicants to an academic honour society
outcome_quote: adopting a lower acceptance criterion for Black compared to White applicants
review_note: Replicated the task in education professionals; this is specific to a hypothetical honor-society decision, not a general statement about admissions.

original_title: Diet Pill and Laxative Use for Weight Control and Subsequent Incident Eating Disorder in US Young Women: 2001–2016
replication_title: Diet pill and laxative use for weight control predicts first‐time receipt of an eating disorder diagnosis within the next 5 years among female adolescents and young adults
effect_name: Diet-pill or laxative use predicts later eating-disorder diagnosis
effect_claim: Young women using diet pills or laxatives for weight control had higher risk of a first eating-disorder diagnosis later.
effect_claim_quote: women who reported diet pill (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 5.6; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 3.0, 10.5) or laxative (AOR = 6.0; 95% CI = 4.2, 8.7) use for weight control had higher odds
replication_target_quote: To replicate findings from a prior study which identified prospective associations between use of products for weight control
outcome_quote: participants using diet pills (risk ratio [RR] = 3.58, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.96–6.54) and laxatives (RR = 2.77, 95% CI: 1.01–7.64) had greater risk
review_note: Observational prospective associations, not evidence that these products cause eating disorders; follow-up and cohorts differed.

original_title: Recognition Memory is Improved by a Structured Temporal Framework During Encoding
replication_title: Null effects of temporal prediction on recognition memory but evidence for differential neural activity at encoding. A registered report
effect_name: Rhythmic temporal structure boosts later recognition memory
effect_claim: Stimuli encoded within a temporally structured framework were recognized better than stimuli encoded within an unstructured framework.
effect_claim_quote: enhanced recognition memory (d') for stimuli that were explicitly encoded within a temporally structured vs. unstructured framework.
replication_target_quote: aimed at establishing the cognitive and neural mechanisms of the effect of temporal prediction on recognition.
outcome_quote: Our behavioural results did not replicate previous findings that show a difference in recognition memory based on temporal predictability at encoding.
review_note: Registered report found encoding-related EEG effects without a later recognition-memory benefit.

original_title: Pavlovian impatience: The anticipation of immediate rewards increases approach behaviour
replication_title: Intertemporal Pavlovian biases and links with mental health in the general population
effect_name: Immediate reward cues increase go responding
effect_claim: Anticipating immediate rather than matched delayed rewards increased approach or go responses.
effect_claim_quote: Go responding was increased in trials in which an immediate reward was available compared with trials in which a preference-matched delayed reward was available.
replication_target_quote: aimed to replicate this intertemporal Pavlovian bias effect
outcome_quote: We replicated the intertemporal Pavlovian bias effect on the probability of go responding
review_note: Mental-health symptom associations were an extension and did not consistently follow the response bias.

original_title: House-edge information yields lower subjective chances of winning than equivalent return-to-player percentages: New evidence from support forum participants
replication_title: How does the phrasing of house edge information affect gamblers’ perceptions and level of understanding? A Registered Report
effect_name: House-edge wording lowers gamblers' perceived chance of winning
effect_claim: Equivalent gambling-cost information expressed as house edge produced lower perceived chances of winning than return-to-player wording.
effect_claim_quote: house-edge information (e.g., “This game keeps 10% of all money bet on average”) is associated with lower perceived chances of winning, as opposed to equivalent return-to-player information.
replication_target_quote: experimentally tested this original phrasing of the house edge against an alternative phrasing
outcome_quote: Compared to return-to-player information, the original phrasing had both lower perceived chances of winning and higher rates of correct understanding
review_note: Registered report used a larger UK online-gambler sample; the original used support-forum members.

original_title: EXPERIMENTAL ANALYSIS OF PRECURSORS TO SEVERE PROBLEM BEHAVIOR
replication_title: Implementation of interventions informed by precursor functional analyses with young children: A replication
effect_name: Precursor-based intervention reduces severe problem behavior
effect_claim: Function-based treatment aimed at mild precursor behavior reduced precursors while severe problem behavior stayed low.
effect_claim_quote: this treatment strategy was effective for behaviors maintained by positive and negative reinforcement.
replication_target_quote: replicates and extends previous research by examining precursor assessments and interventions with three preschool-aged children.
outcome_quote: reductions in precursor behavior and continued low or zero rates of severe problem behavior.
review_note: The replication used three preschoolers; the original tested treatment analyses for two subjects.

original_title: Do 9-month-old infants expect distinct words to refer to kinds?
replication_title: Bilingualism affects 9‐month‐old infants’ expectations about how words refer to kinds
effect_name: Monolingual infants expect distinct words to name distinct kinds
effect_claim: At nine months, monolingual infants expected two distinct count-noun labels to refer to different object kinds.
effect_claim_quote: infants may expect distinct labels to refer to distinct kinds of objects.
replication_target_quote: comparing monolingual and bilingual 9-10-month-olds' expectations about the relationship between labels and object kinds.
outcome_quote: This replicated previous findings showing that monolinguals expect that distinct words label distinct object kinds
review_note: Bilingual infants in the extension did not show the same expectation; the effect name is restricted to monolingual infants.

original_title: Low mindfulness predicts pain catastrophizing in a fear-avoidance model of chronic pain
replication_title: Mindfulness and Chronic Headache/Migraine
effect_name: Mindfulness inversely predicts pain catastrophizing
effect_claim: Higher mindfulness was associated with lower pain catastrophizing among chronic-pain patients.
effect_claim_quote: mindfulness significantly negatively predicts each of these variables
replication_target_quote: whether level of mindfulness predicts key components in the Fear-Avoidance Model of chronic pain
outcome_quote: Mindfulness significantly predicted negative affect, pain catastrophizing, fear of pain, pain hypervigilance, and headache duration
review_note: Headache-specific sample retained the catastrophizing association; the original pain-intensity moderation did not replicate.

original_title: Performance benefits of depression: Sequential decision making in a healthy sample and a clinically depressed sample.
replication_title: Depression and Sequential Decision-Making Revisited
effect_name: Clinical depression improves sequential decision-task performance
effect_claim: Clinically depressed participants outperformed nondepressed participants on a secretary-problem sequential decision task.
effect_claim_quote: depressed individuals perform better than do nondepressed individuals.
replication_target_quote: von Helversen et al. (2011) were able to document a positive effect of depression on task performance in a sequential decision-making task called the secretary problem.
outcome_quote: We did not find any significant differences between clinically depressed and nondepressed individuals in any indicators of task performance
review_note: Replication tested original and extended conditions; its ambulatory patient sample may differ in depression severity.

original_title: Attachment theory in health care: the influence of relationship style on medical students' specialty choice
replication_title: Bindungsmerkmale und Facharztpräferenz bei Medizinstudierenden
effect_name: Secure attachment predicts primary-care specialty preference
effect_claim: Medical students with secure relationship styles were more likely to prefer primary-care than non-primary-care specialties.
effect_claim_quote: Students with a secure style were more likely to choose primary care (61%) over non-primary care
replication_target_quote: a parallel survey was performed at the medical school of the University of Jena
outcome_quote: Students of the first subgroup (primary care) appeared to be more insecurely attached
review_note: German sample contradicted the secure-primary-care pattern, while non-primary-care preference among avoidant or self-reliant students was similar.

effect_name: Affective word-response compatibility
effect_claim: People respond faster when the emotional meaning of a word matches the emotional meaning of the required response.
effect_claim_quote: reaction times were faster when the affective connotation of the presented word and the correct response was the same than when it differed.
original_title: An Affective Variant of the Simon Paradigm
replication_title: Revisiting the affective Simon effect
replication_target_quote: We replicated the affective Simon effect found by De Houwer and Eelen (1998)
outcome_quote: We replicated the affective Simon effect found by De Houwer and Eelen (1998)
review_note: Replication used the same grammatical-category response task and explored how the proportion of strongly emotional words changes effect size.

effect_name: Single-trial audiovisual timing recalibration
effect_claim: One asynchronous sight-and-sound event shifts the timing at which later sights and sounds seem simultaneous.
effect_claim_quote: exposure to a single, brief asynchrony is sufficient to produce strong recalibration effects.
original_title: Rapid Recalibration to Audiovisual Asynchrony
replication_title: Rapid Audiovisual Temporal Recalibration Generalises Across Spatial Location
replication_target_quote: Van der Burg et al. (2013, J Neurosci, 33, pp. 14633-14637) reported results showing that recalibration to asynchronous audiovisual events can happen extremely rapidly.
outcome_quote: Here we replicate the finding that shifts in perceived timing occur following exposure to a single, asynchronous audiovisual stimulus
review_note: Replication also tested different spatial locations; the named effect is the single-trial timing shift.

effect_name: Tact instruction improves bidirectional vocabulary
effect_claim: Teaching children to say foreign words for pictured objects produces stronger bidirectional vocabulary than teaching them to select matching pictures.
effect_claim_quote: Tact instruction consistently produced higher levels of emergent intraverbal responding compared to listener instruction
original_title: Learning a foreign language: Effects of tact and listener instruction on the emergence of bidirectional intraverbals
replication_title: Teaching a foreign language to students with autism via telehealth in inclusive school settings
replication_target_quote: replicate previous research that examined the effects of tact and listener instruction on the emergence of bidirectional intraverbals
outcome_quote: both forms of instruction led to bidirectional intraverbal relations, with tact instruction being relatively more effective
review_note: Original involved typically developing Brazilian children; replication involved Chinese-speaking students with autism taught by telehealth.

effect_name: Subjective truth relativism and misinformation receptivity
effect_claim: People who believe truth depends on personal intuitions are more receptive to meaningless profound-sounding claims and conspiracy theories.
effect_claim_quote: subjectivism predicted higher receptivity to both forms of misinformation
original_title: Misperceptions in a post-truth world: Effects of subjectivism and cultural relativism on bullshit receptivity and conspiracist ideation
replication_title: The role of truth relativist and realist views in bullshit receptivity, conspiracy ideation and the distribution of science misinformation
replication_target_quote: we replicated findings of positive correlations between belief in (subjectivist) truth relativism and bullshit receptivity and conspiracy ideation
outcome_quote: we replicated findings of positive correlations between belief in (subjectivist) truth relativism and bullshit receptivity and conspiracy ideation
review_note: Association only; replication also examined distribution of science misinformation and attempted, unsuccessfully, to manipulate epistemic beliefs.

effect_name: Positive emotions are easier to maintain
effect_claim: People maintain positive emotional states more accurately than negative emotional states after the eliciting stimulus disappears.
effect_claim_quote: people are generally better at maintaining positive emotional states than they are at maintaining negative emotional states
original_title: People are better at maintaining positive than negative emotional states.
replication_title: Simultaneous maintenance of emotions in affective working memory
replication_target_quote: We aimed to re-examine previous findings, that people are better at maintaining positive than negative emotions
outcome_quote: they replicate previous findings concerning the advantage of maintaining positive compared to negative emotions
review_note: Replication used a modified task requiring simultaneous maintenance of two emotions.

effect_name: Social-support cues resist fear learning
effect_claim: Images of social-support figures are less readily linked to fear than images of strangers.
effect_claim_quote: the threat of shock was not associated with conditional stimuli paired with images of social-support figures, but was associated with stimuli paired with images of strangers.
original_title: Unpacking the buffering effect of social support figures: Social support attenuates fear acquisition
replication_title: Social support and fear-inhibition: an examination of underlying neural mechanisms
replication_target_quote: social-support-figure images have been shown to resist becoming associated with fear
outcome_quote: social-support-figure-images (vs stranger-images) were less readily associated with fear, replicating prior work
review_note: Replication examined neural mechanisms and used a retardation-of-acquisition test; verdict concerns the behavioral support-versus-stranger contrast.

effect_name: Learner control improves multimedia transfer
effect_claim: Controlling the pace of a narrated animation improves performance on later transfer tests.
effect_claim_quote: learners who were allowed to exercise control over the pace of the narrated animation across 2 presentations (part-part presentation) performed better on transfer but not retention tests
original_title: When learning is just a click away: Does simple user interaction foster deeper understanding of multimedia messages?
replication_title: Learner control in animated multimedia instructions
replication_target_quote: We tested this guideline by comparing a learner-paced instruction with a system-paced instruction.
outcome_quote: We successfully replicated the interactivity principle in terms of better transfer.
review_note: Follow-up found learner control increased time on task, so the gain does not establish equal-time efficiency.

effect_name: Hierarchical information is memorized faster
effect_claim: People memorize information arranged as a social hierarchy faster than comparable egalitarian information.
effect_claim_quote: a diagram representing hierarchy was memorized more quickly than a diagram representing equality or a comparison diagram.
original_title: The fluency of social hierarchy: The ease with which hierarchical relationships are seen, remembered, learned, and liked.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Memory bias for social hierarchical information is modulated by perceived social rank
replication_target_quote: previous work showing that hierarchical information is memorised faster relative to the egalitarian control.
outcome_quote: The results replicate previous work showing that hierarchical information is memorised faster relative to the egalitarian control.
review_note: Replication tested participants placed at high or low rank in the hierarchy; the advantage varied with their position.

effect_name: People avoid effortful empathy
effect_claim: People choose to avoid empathizing with others partly because they expect empathy to be mentally effortful.
effect_claim_quote: a robust preference to avoid empathy, which was associated with perceptions of empathy as more effortful and aversive and less efficacious.
original_title: Empathy is hard work: People choose to avoid empathy because of its cognitive costs
replication_title: Are Observers Differentially Motivated to Empathize With Stigmatized Targets? An Investigation Using the Empathy Selection Task
replication_target_quote: people prefer to avoid empathy due to its perceived cognitive costs.
outcome_quote: Results replicate previous findings that people prefer to avoid empathy due to its perceived cognitive costs.
review_note: Follow-up tested stigmatized versus other targets; target group membership did not moderate the avoidance effect.

effect_name: Relationship inventory separates three dimensions
effect_claim: A short relationship inventory distinguishes regard, empathy, and congruence in responses from married couples.
effect_claim_quote: moderate, though tentative, support for the expected dimensionality of the abbreviated inventory.
original_title: The Dimensionality of an Abbreviated Relationship Inventory for Couples
replication_title: Dimensionality of an Abbreviated Version of the Relationship Inventory: An Urban Replication with Married Couples
replication_target_quote: to replicate an earlier study involving a sample of 83 rural married couples.
outcome_quote: the same dimensions were found across four different groups of respondents in the two studies.
review_note: Original tested rural couples; replication tested urban couples. This is a measurement-structure finding rather than a causal effect.

effect_name: Spouses show different body-space changes in pregnancy
effect_claim: Wives and husbands do not show similar patterns of perceived body-space change during and after pregnancy.
effect_claim_quote: The results did not duplicate previous study findings of similarity in spouses' patterns of change in perceived body space.
original_title: Spouses?? Body Image Changes During and After Pregnancy
replication_title: Spouses' Body Image Changes During and After Pregnancy: A Replication in Canada
replication_target_quote: replicated an investigation of the relationship between wives' and husbands' strength of identification and similarities in their patterns of change
outcome_quote: no similarities in wives' and husbands' changes in perceived body space or global body attitude
review_note: The original paper itself revisited an earlier study and reported no similarity. Follow-up was a Canadian sample; other body-attitude outcomes differed.

effect_name: Negative material impairs associative memory
effect_claim: People remember associations between negative items less well than associations between neutral items.
effect_claim_quote: compared to a neutral item, memory for the associate of a negative item (a second item here, context in Experiments 1 and 2) is impaired
original_title:
Negative affect impairs associative memory but not
 
 item memory
replication_title: Reduced associative memory for negative information: impact of confidence and interactive imagery during study
replication_target_quote: memory for associations between items is often impaired for negative, emotionally arousing compared to neutral information.
outcome_quote: we replicated the impairment of associative memory for negative pairs.
review_note: Original also found enhanced memory for negative items themselves; the page concerns memory for associations.

effect_name: Left-prefrontal stimulation reduces mind wandering
effect_claim: High-definition electrical stimulation of the left prefrontal cortex reduces mind wandering compared with sham stimulation.
effect_claim_quote: propensity to mind wander is reduced relative to a group receiving sham stimulation.
original_title: The interplay between executive control, behavioural variability and mind wandering: Insights from a high‐definition transcranial direct‐current stimulation study
replication_title: On the neural substrates of mind wandering and dynamic thought: A drug and brain stimulation study
replication_target_quote: previous HD-tDCS findings
outcome_quote: There was no evidence for our hypothesised effect of left prefrontal cortex HD-tDCS reducing task unrelated thought
review_note: Follow-up also manipulated dopamine availability; verdict concerns the stimulation effect on task-unrelated thought.

effect_name: Women respond better to brief heavy-drinking treatment
effect_claim: Women are more likely than men to achieve moderate drinking after brief interventions for heavy drinking.
effect_claim_quote: At 1-year follow-up, females were more successful than males in all conditions.
original_title: Superior Outcome of Females Over Males After Brief Treatment for the Reduction of Heavy Drinking
replication_title: Superior outcome of females over males after brief treatment for the reduction of heavy drinking: replication and report of therapist effects
replication_target_quote: The procedures and findings of a previous study were replicated.
outcome_quote: Again, at 1-year more women than men were Moderate drinkers in all conditions (69% versus 31% overall).
review_note: Both studies assigned participants to guidelines, manual, or therapist conditions. The sex contrast is observational within randomized treatments.

effect_name: Category labels accentuate line-length differences
effect_claim: People judge line lengths across systematic categories as farther apart than lengths in an uncategorized series.
effect_claim_quote: the stimuli belonging to different classes are judged as farther apart on that scale than in an unclassified series.
original_title: CLASSIFICATION AND QUANTITATIVE JUDGEMENT
replication_title: On the Role of Familiarity with Units of Measurement in Categorical Accentuation: Tajfel and Wilkes (1963) Revisited and Replicated
replication_target_quote: On the Role of Familiarity with Units of Measurement in Categorical Accentuation: Tajfel and Wilkes (1963) Revisited and Replicated
outcome_quote: categorical accentuation was higher when the lines were systematically categorized than when they were not
review_note: Replication also found a stronger effect with unfamiliar units of measurement.

effect_name: Brightness words constrict pupils
effect_claim: Words about bright things cause smaller pupils than words about dark things.
effect_claim_quote: pupils were largest for words conveying darkness, of intermediate size for neutral words, and smallest for words conveying brightness.
original_title: Pupillary Responses to Words That Convey a Sense of Brightness or Darkness
replication_title: Pupil changes to voluntary and involuntary visual imagery: A unified paradigm with implications for aphantasia research
replication_target_quote: processed brightness-related words (involuntary imagery)
outcome_quote: brightness-related stimuli reliably elicited stronger pupil constriction than darkness-related stimuli, replicating prior findings.
review_note: Replication reproduced the group-level pupil difference but reported high individual variability and no correlation with self-reported imagery.

effect_name: Vocabulary and reasoning mutual growth
effect_claim: Higher vocabulary predicts subsequent gains in nonverbal reasoning, and higher reasoning predicts gains in vocabulary.
effect_claim_quote: We found that individuals with higher scores in vocabulary showed greater gains in matrix reasoning and vice versa.
original_title: Mutualistic Coupling Between Vocabulary and Reasoning Supports Cognitive Development During Late Adolescence and Early Adulthood
replication_title: Mutualistic coupling of vocabulary and non‐verbal reasoning in children with and without language disorder
replication_target_quote: The current study tests whether language and non‐verbal reasoning show mutualistic coupling in children with and without language disorder using three waves of data from a longitudinal cohort study that over‐sampled children with poor language at school entry (N = 501, 7–13 years).
outcome_quote: Specifically, children with higher initial language abilities showed greater growth in non‐verbal ability and vice versa.
review_note: Original cohort comprised older adolescents and adults; replication tests reciprocal growth in younger children including language disorders.

effect_name: CW FIT and on task behavior
effect_claim: Class Wide Function related Intervention Teams increases pupils’ on task behavior.
effect_claim_quote: Group on-task data improved during CW-FIT over baseline levels.
original_title: Class-Wide Function-Related Intervention Teams: Effects of Group Contingency Programs in Urban Classrooms
replication_title: Improving Behavior in a Self-Contained Elementary Classroom for Students With Emotional or Behavioral Disorders: A Study of CW-FIT
replication_target_quote: In the present replication study, researchers examined the effects of CW-FIT in a self-contained U.S. elementary EBD classroom.
outcome_quote: Results revealed the teacher was able to implement CW-FIT with fidelity with corresponding increases in student on-task behavior and teacher praise, though there was little effect on teacher reprimands.
review_note: Replication tests CW FIT in a small self contained classroom of five pupils with EBD.

effect_name: Prompt exposure and intraverbal learning
effect_claim: Recent exposure to a prompt type makes that prompt more efficient for teaching new intraverbal responses.
effect_claim_quote: For all participants, the prompt method most recently used to teach intraverbal responses required fewer trials to teach new intraverbal responses compared to a prompt method that had not been used recently.
original_title:
The role of
 
 increased exposure to transfer-of-stimulus control
 
 procedures on the acquisition of intraverbal behavior
replication_title: Exposure to a specific prompt topography predicts its relative efficiency when teaching intraverbal behavior to children with autism spectrum disorder
replication_target_quote: The current study was an attempt to replicate these results with 3 children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.
outcome_quote: For all participants, increased exposure to one prompt topography was sufficient to make it relatively more efficient as measured by number of trials to criterion.
review_note: Original tested typically developing preschool children; replication tests children with autism.

effect_name: Recall direction and subjective distance
effect_claim: Recalling related events backward makes a past target event feel closer than recalling them forward.
effect_claim_quote: people feel closer to a target event when they recall a stream of related events in a backward direction (i.e., a reverse-chronological order ending with the target event) rather than a forward direction (i.e., a chronological order beginning with the target event).
original_title: Trips Down Memory Lane: Recall Direction Affects the Subjective Distance of Past Events
replication_title: The influence of recall direction on judgments of subjective temporal distance from the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns
replication_target_quote: In a conceptual replication of their Study 2, we asked participants how close they felt to the first day that lockdowns were imposed in response to the Covid-19 pandemic in the U.S. (federally mandated on March 13, 2020) following either backward or forward recall of a stream of related events.
outcome_quote: The results of the present study ran directly counter to those of Lam and Buehler: participants rated the first day of lockdowns as feeling closer following forward recall than following backward recall.
review_note: Conceptual replication substitutes pandemic lockdown memory for university acceptance and finds the reverse direction.

effect_name: Failure experience and test anxiety
effect_claim: A single failure experience raises pupils’ test anxiety relative to a success experience.
effect_claim_quote: The failing group scored significantly higher than the successful group in the TASC which was administered immediately after the treatments.
original_title: The effect of a single experience of success or failure on test anxiety
replication_title: The Effect of a Single Success or Failure Experience on Test Anxiety: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Comparison of students' TASC scores indicated that the success group recorded a lower test-anxiety score on the posttest than they had done on the pretest, while the failure group's TASC score had shown an increase.
outcome_quote: Comparison of students' TASC scores indicated that the success group recorded a lower test-anxiety score on the posttest than they had done on the pretest, while the failure group's TASC score had shown an increase.
review_note: The later study assesses pre to post test anxiety changes rather than only post treatment group differences.

effect_name: Subliminal conditioning and implicit self esteem
effect_claim: Pairing self words with positive traits subliminally increases implicit self esteem relative to control pairing.
effect_claim_quote: Relative to control conditions, this procedure enhanced implicit self-esteem.
original_title: I Like Myself but I Don't Know Why: Enhancing Implicit Self-Esteem by Subliminal Evaluative Conditioning.
replication_title: Converging evidence that subliminal evaluative conditioning does not affect self‐esteem or cardiovascular activity
