replication_target_quote: Subliminal evaluative conditioning (SEC), which subliminally couples self-words with positive words, has previously been successfully used to boost self-esteem, but the existing studies are in need of replication.
outcome_quote: Across the 3 experiments, no effects were found of SEC on implicit or explicit self-esteem or affect or on cardiovascular (re)activity compared to a control condition in which the self was coupled with neutral words.
review_note: Original and replication abstracts identify the same measured effect and result.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

effect_name: Head heart pointing and moral choices
effect_claim: Pointing to the heart rather than the head increases emotional responses in moral decision making.
effect_claim_quote: In Study 7, we manipulated attention to the head versus the heart and found that head-pointing facilitated intellectual performance, whereas heart-pointing led to emotional decision making.
original_title: Do you use your head or follow your heart? Self-location predicts personality, emotion, decision making, and performance.
replication_title: No evidence for the influence of head-heart conceptual metaphor on moral decision making and personality
replication_target_quote: This seems so based on the previous findings that (a) simply pointing an index finger to heart (versus head) position caused participants to produce more emotional responses in a moral decision task
outcome_quote: In these high-powered experiments, we failed to replicate the findings of previous work.
review_note: The paired effect is the experimental pointing manipulation on moral decisions, not the separate self location personality correlations.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

effect_name: Pride expression and audience relevance
effect_claim: People express less pride when an achievement matters to the audience than when it does not.
effect_claim_quote: Pride expressions were reported to be less intense when the achievement was relevant to the observer of those expressions, both in hypothetical (Experiments 1a, b, c, 2a, b, and 3) and actual pride experiences (Experiment 4; first four experiments Hedge's g = 0.50).
original_title: Show or hide pride? Selective inhibition of pride expressions as a function of relevance of achievement domain.
replication_title: Who expresses their pride when? The regulation of pride expressions as a function of self-monitoring and social context
replication_target_quote: Specifically, pride expressions are lower when the domain of the achievement is of high relevance to observers. We set out to replicate this effect in a non-Western sample.
outcome_quote: Data from two preregistered studies (N1 = 913; N2 = 1081) replicated the effect that pride expressions are inhibited when the achievement domain is relevant.
review_note: Later preregistered studies use a non Western sample and also test self monitoring as a separate moderator.

effect_name: Evaluative feedback memory advantage
effect_claim: People remember past oriented evaluative feedback better than future oriented directive feedback.
effect_claim_quote: evaluative feedback was in fact recalled consistently better than directive feedback
original_title: A memory advantage for past-oriented over future-oriented performance feedback.
replication_title: Weak memory for future-oriented feedback: investigating the roles of attention and improvement focus
replication_target_quote: Recent research showed that people recall past-oriented, evaluative feedback more fully and accurately than future-oriented, directive feedback.
outcome_quote: We successfully replicated the preferential remembering of evaluative feedback
review_note: Original and replication abstracts identify the same measured effect and result.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition

effect_name: Terrorist news and authority salience
effect_claim: Exposure to terrorist attack news raises the salience of respect for authority.
effect_claim_quote: exposure to terrorist attack news (a) increased the salience of respect for authority
original_title: The Impact of Terrorist Attack News on Moral Intuitions and Outgroup Prejudice
replication_title: The Impact of Terrorist Attack News on Moral Intuitions
replication_target_quote: Previous research demonstrated that exposure to news of the 2015 terrorist attacks in Paris, France increased the salience of moral intuitions associated with respect for authority and purity in a sample of U.S. participants.
outcome_quote: Exposure to news of the Las Vegas terrorist attack increased the salience of respect for authority and purity.
review_note: Original abstract supports authority salience; the later abstract also reports purity, which is not part of this paired claim.

effect_name: Physical education skills and exercise
effect_claim: Behavioral skill training in physical education increases adolescents’ exercise and sport participation.
effect_claim_quote: The intervention also had a positive impact on adolescents’ self-reported sport/exercise behaviour (p < .001).
original_title: Impact of a physical education-based behavioural skill training program on cognitive antecedents and exercise and sport behaviour among adolescents: a cluster-randomized controlled trial
replication_title: Effects of behavioural skill training on cognitive antecedents and exercise and sport behaviour in high school students: a cluster-randomised controlled trial
replication_target_quote: The goal of this paper was to replicate a prior cluster-randomised controlled trial, in which behavioural skill training resulted in significant improvements in adolescents' self-reported exercise/sport behaviour, exercise/sport intention, motivation, coping planning and self-efficacy.
outcome_quote: The results showed that the intervention did neither result in increased self-reported exercise/sport participation, objectively assessed physical activity, nor in improvements in the assessed cognitive antecedents of exercise/sport behaviour compared to the control condition.
review_note: The later trial uses a shorter training program and objective activity measure alongside the same self report outcome.
replication_journal: International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology

effect_name: Culture and spontaneous social inferences
effect_claim: North Americans make more spontaneous trait inferences relative to situation inferences than Japanese people do.
effect_claim_quote: we hypothesized that European Canadians would be more likely to produce STIs than SSIs because of the individualistic/independent social orientation and the analytic thinking style dominant in North America, whereas Japanese would produce both STIs and SSIs equally because of the collectivistic/interdependent social orientation and the holistic thinking style dominant in East Asia. Employing the savings-in-relearning paradigm, we presented information that affords both STIs and SSIs and examined cultural differences in the extent of both inferences. The results supported our hypotheses.
original_title: Cultural Differences in Spontaneous Trait and Situation Inferences
replication_title: Attention allocation is a possible mediator of cultural variations in spontaneous trait and situation inferences: Eye-tracking evidence
replication_target_quote: Two studies sought to replicate previous work on cultural differences in the co-occurrence of spontaneous trait (STI) and situation (SSI) inferences
outcome_quote: Both studies replicated previous findings of cultural differences. European Americans made more STIs relative to SSIs than did Asian American or Japanese participants.
review_note: Original compares European Canadians and Japanese; later tests European Americans, Asian Americans and Japanese.

effect_name: Nostalgia and financial risk taking
effect_claim: Nostalgia increases financial risk taking.
effect_claim_quote: In Study 1, we established the basic effect of nostalgia and increased risk taking.
original_title: Nostalgia Increases Financial Risk Taking
replication_title: A Closer Look on the Relation Between Nostalgia and Risk-Taking
replication_target_quote: we tested in Study 3 if the link between nostalgia and financial risk-taking reported by Zou et al. could be replicated and extended to other domains of risk-taking.
outcome_quote: By and large, the relation between nostalgia and financial risk-taking could not be replicated nor extended to any other domains of risk-taking.
review_note: Later study separately tests functional and dysfunctional risk and directly retests the original finance link in Study 3.

original_title: Uncalculating cooperation is used to signal trustworthiness
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Acting without considering personal costs signals trustworthiness in helpers but not punishers
effect_name: Uncalculating cooperation signals trustworthiness
effect_claim: Helpers who did not inspect the personal cost of cooperating appeared more trustworthy than calculating helpers.
effect_claim_quote: people who engage in uncalculating cooperation are perceived as, and actually are, more trustworthy than people who cooperate in a calculating way.
replication_target_quote: Replicating previous work, we found that refraining from checking the personal cost of helping signals trustworthiness
outcome_quote: evidence for observers trusting uncalculating over calculating helpers was mixed
review_note: Helping result partly recurred; observer trust evidence was mixed, and the finding did not extend to punishment.

original_title: Mere experience of low subjective socioeconomic status stimulates appetite and food intake
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Food Insecurity Moderates the Acute Effect of Subjective Socioeconomic Status on Food Consumption
effect_name: Lower perceived social status increases snack intake
effect_claim: Inducing a lower subjective socioeconomic position increased subsequent food consumption.
effect_claim_quote: the mere feeling of lower socioeconomic status relative to others stimulates appetite and food intake.
replication_target_quote: our experiment served to replicate the effects of SSES and of FI on consumption
outcome_quote: The low-SSES manipulation increased food consumption, but only among participants who were food secure at baseline. Amongst food-insecure participants, the effect was reversed.
review_note: Food insecurity was a moderator discovered in exploratory analysis; the original did not stratify by it.

original_title: Who turned the clock? Effects of Manipulated Zeitgebers, Cognitive Load and Immersion on Time Estimation
original_journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
replication_title: Tick-tock: Revisiting the Influence of Zeitgebers and Cognitive Load on Time Judgments during and after VR Immersion
effect_name: Virtual sun movement changes VR time judgments
effect_claim: Changing the motion of a virtual sun altered participants' judgments of elapsed time in VR.
effect_claim_quote: manipulations of external zeitgebers caused by a natural or unnatural movement of the virtual sun had a significant effect on time judgments.
replication_target_quote: we investigated the influence of virtual sun speed and cognitive workload on time perception in a VR environment.
outcome_quote: Contrary to the original study, virtual sun movements did not affect time judgments in VR.
review_note: The original separate cognitive-load effect recurred; this row targets only the virtual-sun manipulation.

original_title: Read-Out of Emotional Information From Iconic Memory
replication_title: The role of evaluatively conditioned stimuli in iconic memory
effect_name: Threatening stimuli decay more slowly in iconic memory
effect_claim: Threat-relevant information remained available longer than neutral information in iconic memory.
effect_claim_quote: the subsequent decay of the initially stored information was slowed for threatening stimuli
replication_target_quote: attempt was made to replicate results found about the influence of valence on prioritisation and decay in iconic memory.
outcome_quote: slower decay of information in iconic memory for negative targets was not revealed.
review_note: Conceptual replication induced valence through evaluative conditioning rather than using inherently threatening stimuli.

original_title: Cognitive principles of multimedia learning: The role of modality and contiguity.
replication_title: Examining the Effects of Multimodal Presentations on Learning Spatial Layouts
effect_name: Auditory narration improves multimedia learning over on-screen text
effect_claim: Students learned more when verbal material was spoken rather than displayed as on-screen text alongside visual material.
effect_claim_quote: students learned better when verbal input was presented auditorily as speech rather than visually as text.
replication_target_quote: Presenting information appropriately in multiple modalities
outcome_quote: text alone was always the worst performer, and that presentations that capitalized on the auditory channel led to significantly better learning
review_note: Conceptual replication changed the learning target from lightning animation to a navigable spatial layout.

original_title: Action alters object identification: Wielding a gun increases the bias to see guns.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
replication_title: Wielding a gun increases judgments of others as holding guns: a randomized controlled trial
effect_name: Wielding a gun biases judgments that others hold guns
effect_claim: Holding a gun increased the tendency to report that another person also held a gun.
effect_claim_quote: Responding with a gun biased observers to report "gun present" more than did responding with a ball.
replication_target_quote: first step was to conduct a high-powered replication.
outcome_quote: a significant gun embodiment effect in participants' reaction times and in their proportion of correct responses, but not in signal detection measures of bias
review_note: RT and accuracy effects recurred, but the original signal-detection bias measure did not.

original_title: The regulatory effect of choice in Situation Selection reduces experiential, exocrine and respiratory arousal for negative emotional stimulations
replication_title: Situation selection for the regulation of emotion responses: Non-meaningful choice options retain partial physiological regulatory impact
effect_name: Choosing an upcoming negative image reduces negative experience
effect_claim: Being able to choose a forthcoming negative image reduced negative emotional experience relative to having that image imposed.
effect_claim_quote: having the choice in negative contexts decreased negative experience
replication_target_quote: wanted to replicate results on Situation selection efficiency and explore its limits
outcome_quote: The effect of Situation selection for negative experience was replicated.
review_note: The meaningful-choice condition replicated; non-meaningful choice did not reduce negative experience.

original_title: Priming God-Related Concepts Increases Anxiety and Task Persistence
original_journal: Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology
replication_title: God, Can I Give Up?: The Diverging Effects of God-Related Thoughts on Task Persistence in Chinese Buddhists and Taoists
replication_journal: International Journal for the Psychology of Religion
effect_name: God-related primes increase task persistence
effect_claim: Priming God-related concepts increased persistence on a difficult task in the original sample.
effect_claim_quote: God-related primes increased both task persistence and anxiousness
replication_target_quote: we replicated prior findings that exposure to God representations increased task persistence in Chinese Buddhists
outcome_quote: Taoist participants exposed to God-related primes spent less time on tracing a difficult geometric figures
review_note: Buddhist participants showed increased persistence, while Taoist participants showed decreased persistence; original found no religious-affiliation moderation.

original_title: Enhanced recall of disgusting relative to frightening photographs is not due to organisation
replication_title: The effect of discrete emotions on memory: Investigating the replicability and boundary conditions of the mnemonic advantage for disgust
replication_journal: Carolina Digital Repository (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill)
effect_name: Disgusting photos are recalled better than frightening photos
effect_claim: Disgusting photographs were recalled more often than equally unpleasant frightening photographs.
effect_claim_quote: participants recalled more disgusting photographs than frightening photographs.
replication_target_quote: Experiment 1a failed to replicate the mnemonic advantage of disgust
outcome_quote: The disgust advantage was ultimately replicated in an experiment where participants completed a concurrent secondary task at encoding.
review_note: Dissertation/repository replication failed in the initial task but found the advantage under divided attention.

effect_name: Children follow others vegetable-eating norms
effect_claim: Children eat more vegetables when told that other children have eaten a large amount.
effect_claim_quote: Children ate more carrots when they believed that other children had eaten a large amount of carrots, compared to all other conditions.
original_title: Perceived eating norms and vegetable consumption in children
original_journal: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
replication_title: Perceived eating norms and children's eating behaviour: An informational social influence account
replication_target_quote: we aimed to replicate the effect that perceived eating norms have on children's vegetable consumption
outcome_quote: In both studies children were influenced by perceived eating norms, eating more when led to believe others had eaten a large amount compared to when led to believe others had eaten no vegetables.
review_note: Original tested carrot intake; replication examined vegetable consumption in two settings and found the social-norm effect in both.

effect_name: Animal setting alters docility and vigor ratings
effect_claim: Animals shown in less natural settings are judged more docile and less vigorous.
effect_claim_quote: Zoo animals were seen as restricted, tame, and passive while wild animals were characterized as free, wild, and active.
original_title: People's Perceptions of Animals
replication_title: An Animal’s Environment Influences Perceptions of Docility and Vigor But Not Aesthetic Appeal: A Constructive Replication
replication_target_quote: The current study replicated and expanded upon that prior work.
outcome_quote: Perceptions of docility increased and vigor decreased as the naturalness of the environment declined.
review_note: Outcome is for docility and vigor, which matched; replication did not find an environmental effect on aesthetic appeal.

effect_name: Science priming and moral sensitivity
effect_claim: Thinking about science makes people more sensitive to moral norms.
effect_claim_quote: Thinking about science leads individuals to endorse more stringent moral norms and exhibit more morally normative behavior.
original_title: Does “Science” Make You Moral? The Effects of Priming Science on Moral Judgments and Behavior
replication_title: When Science Replaces Religion: Science as a Secular Authority Bolsters Moral Sensitivity
replication_target_quote: The present set of studies sought to replicate this effect
outcome_quote: Study 1 used a sentence unscrambling task for implicitly priming the concept of science but failed to replicate its effect on moral sensitivity, presumably due to a ceiling effect. Study 2 replicated the effect with a new measure of moral sensitivity.
review_note: Study 1 failed with the implicit priming task; Study 2 found the effect with a new moral-sensitivity measure.

effect_name: Girls share more with friends than acquaintances
effect_claim: Preschool girls share more food with friends than acquaintances, while boys do not vary sharing by relationship.
effect_claim_quote: girls sharing more with friends than with acquaintances, and boys not sharing differentially.
original_title: Preschool Children's Food Sharing with Friends and Acquaintances
replication_title: Food sharing with friends and acquaintances: A study in preschool boys and girls
replication_target_quote: we replicated and extended the classical work of Birch and Billman
outcome_quote: Girls gave more non-preferred food to acquaintances than to friends, whereas boys gave more to friends than to acquaintances. No effect of relationship was found for preferred food.
review_note: Dutch follow-up found the opposite pattern for nonpreferred food and no relationship effect for preferred food; active requests by friends did recur.

effect_name: Question choice changes lie-detection accuracy
effect_claim: Diagnostic questioning changes how accurately observers distinguish truthful from deceptive answers.
effect_claim_quote: The different questioning sets produced a 36-point swing in accuracy from 42% to 78% accuracy.
original_title: Strong Diagnostic Questioning Effects on Deception Detection Accuracy With U.S. Customs Agents
replication_title: Deception detection and question effects: testing truth-default theory predictions in South Korea
replication_target_quote: The current experiment (n = 81) tested truth-default theory’s proposition 13 and diagnostic questioning module with a student sample from South Korea.
outcome_quote: questioning was found to significantly enhance (65%) and reduce (30%) deception-detection accuracy
review_note: Original used U.S. Customs agents; replication used South Korean students, and both found large accuracy changes by question set.

effect_name: Implicit criminal identification increases with age
effect_claim: Adults show stronger implicit criminal identification at older ages.
effect_claim_quote: ICI increases with age
original_title: Implicit Criminal Identity and Age: Implications for Criminal Persistence and Desistance
replication_title: Age and Chronic and Temporary Criminality: Associations With Implicit and Explicit Criminal Identities
replication_target_quote: The current study replicates previous research
outcome_quote: Study 1 replicated the results of the original study. Study 2 found that, among those in the control condition, older participants had a stronger ICI than younger participants.
review_note: Study 2 age pattern applied in its control condition; making criminality salient raised implicit criminal identity among younger participants.

effect_name: Ruminative thinking and obsessive-compulsive severity
effect_claim: More ruminative thinking accompanies greater obsessive-compulsive symptom severity.
effect_claim_quote: Tendency to ruminate was positively correlated with the severity of OC symptoms and particularly with obsessive rumination, even after controlling for depression.
original_title: Relations between a ruminative thinking style and obsessive–compulsive symptoms in non-clinical samples
replication_title: Is a Ruminative Thinking Style Related to Obsessive-Compulsive Symptom Severity Beyond Its Associations with Depressive and Anxiety Symptom Severity?
replication_target_quote: We sought to replicate this association in a sample of individuals with OCD
outcome_quote: an RTS continued to predict the questionnaire, but not the interview measure of obsessive-compulsive symptom severity.
review_note: Original used nonclinical student questionnaires; follow-up used clinically diagnosed participants and found the association on a questionnaire but not an interview measure.

effect_name: Independent target enhancement and distractor suppression
effect_claim: Enhancing target features and suppressing distractor features guide visual attention independently.
effect_claim_quote: target-feature enhancement and distractor-feature suppression contribute to attentional guidance independently
original_title: Enhancement and Suppression Flexibly Guide Attention
replication_title: Can enhancement and suppression concurrently guide attention? An assessment at the individual level
replication_target_quote: sought to replicate previous findings and re-establish their independence
outcome_quote: negative correlation between target enhancement and distractor suppression
review_note: Follow-up reproduced a singleton-presence search benefit only with fixed target color, but its probe measures contradicted independence.

effect_name: Psychedelic experiences increase mind attribution
effect_claim: After a psychedelic experience, people attribute more mental awareness to living and nonliving things.
effect_claim_quote: attribution of consciousness to various entities increases.
original_title: A Single Belief-Changing Psychedelic Experience Is Associated With Increased Attribution of Consciousness to Living and Non-living Entities
replication_title: Psychedelic Experiences Increase Mind Perception but do not Change Atheist-Believer Status: A Prospective Longitudinal Study
replication_target_quote: Replicating previous findings, we observed increases in mind perception
outcome_quote: we observed increases in mind perception across a variety of living and non-living targets (e.g. plants, rocks).
review_note: Original retrospective survey asked people with a belief-changing experience; replication prospectively followed people planning psilocybin use.

effect_name: One social threat blunts response to another
effect_claim: Experiencing one social threat reduces the later response to a different social threat.
effect_claim_quote: Both effects were significantly reduced when the exclusion was preceded by preexposure to a loss of control
original_title: From Loss of Control to Social Exclusion: ERP Effects of Preexposure to a Social Threat in the Cyberball Paradigm
replication_title: Preexposure to one social threat alters responses to another social threat: Behavioral and electrophysiological evidence
replication_target_quote: A recent Cyberball study has indicated that the experience of loss of control can affect how people process subsequent social exclusion.
outcome_quote: these effects were significantly reduced by the preexposure to an independent social threat (here: social exclusion).
review_note: Conceptual reverse-order test: original loss of control before exclusion; replication exclusion before loss of control. The P3 and self-report reduction generalized; continuity effects differed.

effect_name: Health outranks economy in Brazilian pandemic perceptions
effect_claim: In Brazilian pandemic perceptions, health and social distancing concerns are more salient than economic concerns.
effect_claim_quote: Brazilian society privileged prophylaxis and health, via social isolation, to the detriment of the country’s economic preservation.
original_title: Universalists or Utilitarianists? The Social Representation of COVID-19 Pandemic in Brazil
replication_title: Sustainability and the Social Representation of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Missing Link
replication_target_quote: our aim is to replicate a previous study carried out in Brazil in mid-2020
outcome_quote: categories such as economy and employment and changes and the new normal were mentioned less.
review_note: A later 2021 Brazilian sample placed politics, distancing, death, and fear centrally while economy remained peripheral; broader representation changed.

effect_name: Sight dominates quick music-performance judgments
effect_claim: Visual cues can outweigh sound in quick judgments of music competition performance.
effect_claim_quote: visual information dominated rapid judgments of group performance.
original_title: The vision heuristic: Judging music ensembles by sight alone
original_journal: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
replication_title: Sight vs. Sound Judgments of Music Performance Depend on Relative Performer Quality: Cross-cultural Evidence From Classical Piano and Tsugaru Shamisen Competitions
replication_target_quote: replicating previous studies of classical piano competitions with Japanese participants
outcome_quote: the second prediction was only supported for the piano stimuli and the third prediction was only supported for the shamisen condition
review_note: Visual dominance appeared for piano but did not generalize to Japanese shamisen; relative performer quality affected modality reliance.

effect_name: Menstrual cycle and speech disfluency
effect_claim: Women produce more speech disfluencies at premenstruation than at ovulation.
effect_claim_quote: The mean total frequency of the women's speech disfluencies produced at premenstruation was significantly greater than the mean total of their speech disfluencies produced at ovulation.
original_title: Speech Fluency Fluctuations during the Menstrual Cycle
replication_title: Replication of “Speech Fluency Fluctuations during the Menstrual Cycle”
replication_target_quote: 20 women read contexual material aloud at ovulation (when the typical woman experiences her greatest feelings of well-being) and at premenstrution (when she experiences a significant increase in anxiety level).
outcome_quote: They were no less fluent at premenstruation than at ovulation.
review_note: The original used extemporaneous speech; the replication used reading aloud, so this is a changed-task conceptual test.
original_journal: Journal of Speech and Hearing Research

effect_name: Mother child mediated learning and resilience
effect_claim: Mother-child mediated learning strategies predict psychological resilience and cognitive modifiability in children with learning disabilities.
effect_claim_quote: The findings showed that mother-child MLE strategies, HOME, and socio-economic level contributed significantly to prediction of psychological resilience (78%) and cognitive modifiability (51%).
original_title: The effects of mother‐child mediated learning strategies on psychological resilience and cognitive modifiability of boys with learning disability
replication_title: The Effects of Mother-Child Mediated Learning Strategies on Cognitive Modifiability and Psychological Resilience of Children With Learning Disabilities: A Replication of Tzuriel and Shomron’s Study (2018) With Nigerian Children
replication_target_quote: This study determined the effects of mother-child mediated learning (MCML) strategies on the psychological resilience (PR) and cognitive modifiability (CM) of children with learning disabilities (LD) using a structural equation modeling (SEM) approach.
outcome_quote: MCML had a significant effect on the PR as well as CM of children with LD.
review_note: Original studied boys; replication includes boys and girls in Nigeria. Neither abstract gives a direction for the separate MLE coefficient.

effect_name: Alternative reinforcement and resistance to extinction
effect_claim: Adding reinforcers independent of the target response increases that response’s resistance to extinction.
effect_claim_quote: Resistance to satiation and extinction, in contrast, was positively related to the overall rate of reinforcement in the component.
original_title: ALTERNATIVE REINFORCEMENT INCREASES RESISTANCE TO CHANGE: PAVLOVIAN OR OPERANT CONTINGENCIES?
replication_title: Additional free reinforcers increase persistence of problem behavior in a clinical context: A partial replication of laboratory findings
replication_target_quote: Results of several investigations have shown that alternative reinforcement can increase the resistance to change of a target response during extinction.
outcome_quote: For 2 out of 3 participants, problem behavior tended to be more resistant to extinction following periods in which additional fixed-time reinforcers were delivered.
review_note: Original was pigeon key pecking; partial clinical replication tests human problem behavior and supports the effect in two of three participants.
original_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
replication_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

effect_name: Equine intervention and substance craving
effect_claim: A session of equine assisted services reduces negative affect and substance craving in veterans receiving substance use treatment.
effect_claim_quote: The State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, Craving Experience Questionnaire, and Positive and Negative Affect Scale revealed preliminary findings of significant preintervention to postintervention decreases in anxiety, negative affect, and craving, as well as increased positive affect.
original_title: A Pilot Observational Study of Implementing an Equine-Assisted Services Program Within a VA Medical Center Residential Substance Use Disorder Treatment Program
replication_title: Examining the Psychological Measures and Feasibility of Recreational Trail Rides in Reducing Cravings for Addictive Substances among Veterans: A Replication Pilot Study
replication_target_quote: This pilot observational study is primarily aimed to investigate safety, feasibility, and acceptability of equine-assisted services for Veterans with substance abuse disorders. It is the second pilot observational study, the first being completed in 2022.
outcome_quote: The results indicated significant reductions in negative affect and substance craving after the first session, with positive effects observed in subsequent sessions.
review_note: The first study used learning and psychotherapy; the later pilot used trail rides. Both measure within-session craving and affect without a control group.

effect_name: Dyadic complex skill training efficiency
effect_claim: Dyadic practice achieves equivalent complex skill performance to individual training with half the training resources.
effect_claim_quote: Trainer time and resources were half for the dyadic group, and performance was equivalent.
original_title: A dyadic protocol for training complex skills
replication_title: A Dyadic Protocol for Training Complex Skills: A Replication Using Female Participants
replication_target_quote: the present study investigated the generalizability of the effectiveness and efficiency gains to women.
outcome_quote: women trained in the AIM-dyad condition performed as well as those trained in the individual condition.
review_note: Original sample was undergraduates; replication explicitly tests women.
original_journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
replication_journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society

effect_name: Teasing and adolescent body disturbance
effect_claim: A history of weight related teasing is associated with body dissatisfaction and eating disturbance in adolescent girls.
effect_claim_quote: teasing history was significantly related to the development of body image and eating disturbance.
original_title: Development of body image, eating disturbance, and general psychological functioning in female adolescents: Covariance structure modeling and longitudinal investigations
replication_title: Development of body image, eating disturbance, and general psychological functioning in adolescent females: a replication using covariance structure modeling in an Australian sample
replication_target_quote: The current study is a follow up to a covariance structure modeling (CSM) investigation of predictors of body image, eating dysfunction, and general psychological functioning in U.S. adolescent females.
outcome_quote: The results support previous research indicating that teasing and body dissatisfaction are risk factors for the development of eating disturbances.
review_note: Replication uses an Australian adolescent sample and covariance structure modeling.

effect_name: Object Assembly and bodily concerns
effect_claim: Adults with low Wechsler Object Assembly scores show more Rorschach responses indicating bodily concerns.
effect_claim_quote: there was a significantly greater percentage of Rorschach responses indicating bodily concern in the group scoring low in OA.
original_title: The Wechsler Object Assembly subtest and bodily concerns.
replication_title: Wechsler Object Assembly subtest and bodily concern: A review and replication.
replication_target_quote: The present paper presents several additional attempts to test the previous observation of a relationship between OA and bodily concerns in adults.
outcome_quote: In three independent samples, adults with a Wechsler profile in which OA was the first or second lowest subtest had a significantly greater number and percentage of Rorschach responses which indicate bodily concern than Ss in which OA was the first or second highest subtest.
review_note: This pairs the original paper’s adult subgroup finding, not its separate child sample result.
replication_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

effect_name: Lure technique and request compliance
effect_claim: Offering an attractive request and then substituting a less attractive one increases compliance with the final request.
effect_claim_quote: The results attest to the effectiveness of this procedure.
original_title: The Lure: A New Compliance Procedure
replication_title: The Lure Technique: Replication and Refinement in a Field Setting
replication_target_quote: Only one formal study has been published on this technique, which failed to control two key methodological factors: the status of the participants and the solicitor, and the delay between the initial decision and the target request.
outcome_quote: Greater compliance with the final request was found in the lure condition (70%) than in the control condition (35%) in which the final request was addressed immediately.
review_note: Replication controls requester status and delay; the original abstract reports effectiveness without numerical comparison.

effect_name: CBT for PTSD in severe mental illness
effect_claim: Individual cognitive behavioral treatment reduces PTSD diagnoses in people with severe mental illness.
effect_claim_quote: Clinical outcomes were good, with reductions in PTSD diagnoses, based on the Clinician Administered PTSD Scale (CAPS), from 100% at baseline to 64% at post-treatment and 50% at three-month follow-up.
original_title: Cognitive-Behavioral Treatmenzt of PTSD in Severe Mental Illness: Results of a Pilot Study
replication_title: Cognitive-Behavioral Treatment of PTSD in Severe Mental Illness: Pilot Study Replication in an Ethnically Diverse Population
replication_target_quote: A parent study conducted in New Hampshire examined the effects of a 12- to 16-week cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) intervention for PTSD among people with SMI.
outcome_quote: Results showed high levels of retention in treatment and improvement at three and six months posttreatment in PTSD.
review_note: Both are small uncontrolled pilots; later sample is ethnically diverse and urban.

effect_name: Social behavior training in deaf children
effect_claim: A multifaceted training program increases appropriate social behavior in children with severe language disabilities.
effect_claim_quote: Results showed a functional relationship between introduction of the training procedure and increases in percentage of appropriate target behaviors for all 9 children.
original_title: EFFECTS OF A MULTIFACETED TRAINING PROCEDURE ON THE ACQUISITION AND GENERALIZATION OF SOCIAL BEHAVIORS IN LANGUAGE‐DISABLED DEAF CHILDREN
replication_title: EFFECTS OF A MULTIFACETED TRAINING PROCEDURE ON THE SOCIAL BEHAVIORS OF HEARING‐IMPAIRED CHILDREN WITH SEVERE LANGUAGE DISABILITIES: A REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: The effectiveness of a training package on the social behaviors of 20 hearing-impaired children with severe language disabilities was assessed.
outcome_quote: Results showed that the training package was effective in increasing greeting, turn waiting, initiating interaction, and giving help and these effects were maintained over several weeks.
review_note: Training package differs in implementation, but target social behaviors and population substantially overlap.

effect_name: Feedback reception skills training
effect_claim: Training employees to receive feedback improves their appropriate feedback receiving behavior.
effect_claim_quote: The results showed that participants were able to acquire and maintain appropriate feedback receiving behavior.
original_title: Teaching Employees How to Receive Feedback: A Preliminary Investigation
replication_title: Teaching Appropriate Feedback Reception Skills Using Computer-based Instruction: A Systematic Replication
replication_target_quote: The current study investigated the efficacy of training individuals to receive feedback in an appropriate manner using computer-based instruction (CBI).
outcome_quote: All three participants demonstrated increases in accuracy of appropriate feedback behaviors following CBI.
review_note: Original used in-person behavioral skills training; later systematic replication used computer instruction.

effect_name: Token reinforcement and disruptive classroom behavior
effect_claim: A classroom token reinforcement program reduces disruptive behavior in children.
effect_claim_quote: With the introduction of the token reinforcement program, an abrupt reduction in deviant behavior occurred.
original_title: Behavior Modification of an Adjustment Class: A Token Reinforcement Program
replication_title: A TOKEN REINFORCEMENT PROGRAM IN A PUBLIC SCHOOL: A REPLICATION AND SYSTEMATIC ANALYSIS1
replication_target_quote: When the Token Reinforcement Program was introduced, the frequency of disruptive behavior declined in five of the six remaining children.
outcome_quote: Withdrawal of the Token Reinforcement Program increased disruptive behavior in these five children, and reinstatement of the Token Reinforcement Program reduced disruptive behavior in four of these five.
review_note: Later classroom study replicates the core decrease and also tests withdrawal; original generalization result did not repeat and is outside this paired claim.

effect_name: Active error correction and word learning
effect_claim: Having students repeat the correct response after an error improves later recall compared with teacher modeling alone.
effect_claim_quote: For all 6 students, the active student response error-correction procedure resulted in more words read correctly during instruction, same-day tests, next-day tests, 2-week maintenance tests, and generality tests (words read in sentences).
original_title: EFFECTS OF ACTIVE STUDENT RESPONSE DURING ERROR CORRECTION ON THE ACQUISITION, MAINTENANCE, AND GENERALIZATION OF SIGHT WORDS BY STUDENTS WITH DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES
replication_title: EFFECTS OF ACTIVE STUDENT RESPONSE DURING ERROR CORRECTION ON THE ACQUISITION, MAINTENANCE, AND GENERALIZATION OF SCIENCE VOCABULARY BY ELEMENTARY STUDENTS: A SYSTEMATIC REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: We compared active student response (ASR) error correction and no-response (NR) error correction while teaching science terms to 5 elementary students.
outcome_quote: ASR error correction was superior on each of the study's seven dependent variables.
review_note: Original taught sight words; replication taught science vocabulary with the same active versus no-response correction.

effect_name: Preschool Life Skills increases learned skills
effect_claim: Teaching the Preschool Life Skills curriculum increases preschoolers' use of classroom social and communication skills.
effect_claim_quote: more than four-fold increase in preschool life skills.
original_title: EVALUATION OF A CLASSWIDE TEACHING PROGRAM FOR DEVELOPING PRESCHOOL LIFE SKILLS
replication_title: Preschool Life Skills: A Systematic Replication with Children with Developmental Disabilities
replication_target_quote: adaptations made to the original preschool life skills curriculum
outcome_quote: skill acquisition with all nine participants
review_note: Original taught typically developing children classwide; follow-up adapted the curriculum for nine children with developmental disabilities.

effect_name: Equalized-cost schedules and reinforcement maximization
effect_claim: When response costs are equalized across concurrent schedules, animals favor the schedule that maximizes reinforcement.
effect_claim_quote: The bias toward the latter component predicted by maximization theory was found.
original_title: MATCHING AND MAXIMIZING WITH CONCURRENT RATIO‐INTERVAL SCHEDULES
original_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
replication_title: MORE ON CONCURRENT INTERVAL‐RATIO SCHEDULES: A REPLICATION AND REVIEW
replication_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
replication_target_quote: To evaluate this hypothesis, pigeons were tested in a procedure in which interval and ratio schedules had equal response costs.
outcome_quote: Pigeons did not maximize rate of reinforcement on this procedure. Instead, their times spent on the alternative schedules matched the relative rates of reinforcement
review_note: Follow-up used a related variable-time versus variable-ratio-time schedule with equalized response costs and found matching rather than the original maximizing bias.

effect_name: Connotatively mismatched colors slow naming
effect_claim: People name ink colors more slowly when a word and its color have conflicting emotional connotations.
effect_claim_quote: color-naming speed is slower for inconsistent than for consistent color-word combinations
original_title: The Color-Word Connotative Incongruity Effect
replication_title: Color-Word Connotative Incongruity: A Replication
replication_target_quote: The previously reported effect of slower color-naming speed for connotatively inconsistent color-word combinatios was investigated.
outcome_quote: As before, the effect was found when connotatively consistent cards were presented for color naming before connotatively inconsistent cards.
review_note: Replication found the effect only when consistent cards came before inconsistent cards; outcome applies to that tested order.

effect_name: Audience laughter improves speaker evaluations
effect_claim: People evaluate a speaker more favorably when an audience laughs at the jokes in the speech.
effect_claim_quote: They preferred the speaker who elicited laughter
original_title: Audience's Response to Jokes in Speeches with and without Recorded Laughs
replication_title: Evaluative Responses to Jokes in Informative Speech with and without Laughter by an Audience: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: Evaluative Responses to Jokes in Informative Speech with and without Laughter by an Audience: A Partial Replication
outcome_quote: Mean responses of 39 students shown a videotaped speech with laughter were higher than those of 33 students viewing the speech without laughter
review_note: Original noted a speaker-order interaction; replication contrasted videotaped speeches with versus without audience laughter.

effect_name: Brief visual attentional blink
effect_claim: Detection of a second visual target temporarily worsens when it follows soon after a first target.
effect_claim_quote: probes are poorly detected when they are presented during a 270-ms interval beginning 180 ms after the target.
original_title: Temporary suppression of visual processing in an RSVP task: An attentional blink?
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
replication_title: An online browser-based attentional blink replication using visual objects
replication_target_quote: The attentional blink is characterised by impaired attention to the second of two target stimuli
outcome_quote: a clear attentional blink effect between 200 to 400ms following the distractor including a Lag 1 sparing effect
review_note: Original used letters in a laboratory; replication used visual objects through a browser, so this is a conceptual timing replication.

effect_name: American and Chinese college dating norms
effect_claim: American college students report more liberal dating attitudes and earlier dating than Chinese college students.
effect_claim_quote: American college students generally entertain a liberal attitude towards dating, tend to date young
original_title: Dating attitudes and behaviors of American and Chinese college students
replication_title: Dating attitudes and behaviors of American and Chinese college students: A partial replication
replication_target_quote: One such study from nearly two decades ago found more liberal attitudes and behavior regarding dating among American college students compared to their relatively conservative Chinese counterparts.
outcome_quote: The American students continue to use a dating script that is far more liberal. They also initiate the dating stage at much younger ages.
review_note: New U.S. and Chinese university samples were assessed roughly two decades later; broader courtship differences persisted.

effect_name: Facial muscle responses distinguish depression
effect_claim: Facial muscle patterns during imagined emotions distinguish depressed from nondepressed people.
effect_claim_quote: facial expression patterns differentiate depressed from nondepressed subjects.
original_title: Facial Muscle Patterning to Affective Imagery in Depressed and Nondepressed Subjects
replication_title: Facial Muscle Electromyography in Depressed and Nondepressed Hospitalized Subjects: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: Previous investigators have observed differences in the facial EMG patterns of depressed and nondepressed subjects who were not hospitalized
outcome_quote: The depressed and nondepressed subjects could not be differentiated on the basis of muscle activity
review_note: Original participants were not hospitalized; follow-up studied hospitalized depressed and nondepressed people, a material population change.

effect_name: Lunar phase does not predict hockey aggression
effect_claim: Lunar cycles do not predict aggressive penalties in ice hockey games.
effect_claim_quote: support for lunar influence was not forthcoming.
original_title: LUNAR INFLUENCES ON HUMAN AGGRESSION
original_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
replication_title: LUNAR CYCLES AND HUMAN AGGRESSION: A REPLICATION
replication_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
replication_target_quote: tests of a lunar-aggression hypothesis using the aggressive penalties awarded in ice hockey over a season of competition.
outcome_quote: Interpersonal aggression was found to be unrelated to either the synodic or anomalistic cycles
review_note: Both papers used a season of hockey penalties; this is replication of an absence, not a claim of equivalent aggression on every lunar phase.

effect_name: Working memory training and parent-rated ADHD symptoms
effect_claim: Working memory training improves parent-rated attention and ADHD symptoms in children with ADHD.
effect_claim_quote: Parent ratings indicated that participants improved on inattention, overall number of ADHD symptoms
original_title: A Controlled Trial of Working Memory Training for Children and Adolescents with ADHD
original_journal: Journal of Clinical Child & Adolescent Psychology
replication_title: A randomized clinical trial of Cogmed Working Memory Training in school‐age children with ADHD : a replication in a diverse sample using a control condition
replication_journal: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry
replication_target_quote: A randomized clinical trial of Cogmed Working Memory Training in school‐age children with ADHD : a replication in a diverse sample using a control condition
outcome_quote: no treatment group differences were observed for any other outcome measures.
review_note: The original reported within-group parent-rating gains; the follow-up used an active placebo and found storage gains but no differential ADHD-symptom improvement.

effect_name: Hyperactivity and time-estimation errors
effect_claim: Hyperactive children make larger errors than other children when estimating short time intervals.
effect_claim_quote: The differences between estimated and elapsed time were larger for hyperactives than for normals
original_title: Time Estimation by Hyperactive and Normal Children
replication_title: Time Estimation and Hyperactivity, Replication
replication_target_quote: Time Estimation and Hyperactivity, Replication
outcome_quote: Time estimation is not clinically useful for identifying hyperactive boys.
review_note: Follow-up tested only six hyperactive boys, versus 100 children in the original main study; its small group limits precision.

effect_name: Fathers rate own mathematical intelligence higher
effect_claim: Fathers estimate their own mathematical and spatial intelligence more highly than mothers do.
effect_claim_quote: males (fathers) rated themselves as more intelligent on mathematical and spatial intelligence than females (mothers)
original_title: Parents’ estimates of their own and their children's multiple intelligences
replication_title: Sex Differences in Parents' Estimations of their Own and their Children's Multiple Intelligences: A Portuguese Replication
replication_target_quote: Sex Differences in Parents' Estimations of their Own and their Children's Multiple Intelligences: A Portuguese Replication
outcome_quote: Men's self-estimates were not significantly higher than women's on any of the 11 estimates.
review_note: The original son-versus-daughter rating pattern partly recurred; verdict concerns only the parent self-rating sex difference.

effect_name: Recorded teacher messages improve school performance
effect_claim: Daily recorded messages from teachers to parents improve students' academic performance.
effect_claim_quote: the inclusion of academic information in the daily message resulted in improved academic performance by every student in the class
original_title: Improving Parent-Teacher Communication through Recorded Telephone Messages1
replication_title: Improving Parent-Teacher Communication through Recorded Telephone Messages: Systematic Replication in a Special Education Classroom
replication_target_quote: daily recorded telephone message as a communications link between parents and the students' teacher.
outcome_quote: three of the six students' spelling performance improved as a function of the message system
review_note: Original regular first-grade class reported gains for all 21 students; follow-up special-education class found spelling gains in three of six.

effect_name: Positive peer reports improve social interactions
effect_claim: Rewarding peers for publicly reporting positive behavior improves interactions with socially isolated youths.
effect_claim_quote: positive peer reports reduced negative social interactions (to near zero) and increased positive interactions (to above 70%).
original_title: FEED THE HUNGRY BEE: USING POSITIVE PEER REPORTS TO IMPROVE THE SOCIAL INTERACTIONS AND ACCEPTANCE OF A SOCIALLY REJECTED GIRL IN RESIDENTIAL CARE
replication_title: USING POSITIVE PEER REPORTING TO IMPROVE THE SOCIAL INTERACTIONS AND ACCEPTANCE OF SOCIALLY ISOLATED ADOLESCENTS IN RESIDENTIAL CARE: A SYSTEMATIC REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: We studied how rewarding youth in residential care for publicly reporting positive social behavior influenced the social interactions and acceptance of their most socially isolated peers.
outcome_quote: substantial improvements in social interactions by the previously isolated peers.
review_note: Outcome concerns social interactions. Acceptance ratings improved for only two target youths in the follow-up.

effect_name: Vicarious reward aids complex imitation
effect_claim: Seeing a model receive a reward improves children's imitation when the task is complex.
effect_claim_quote: vicarious reward had a significant effect only for Ss in the high-complexity condition
original_title: Vicarious Reward and Task Complexity as Determinants of Imitative Learning
replication_title: Vicarious Reward and Task Complexity as Determinants of Imitative Learning: A Modified Replication
replication_target_quote: As in an earlier study with older children
outcome_quote: vicarious reward again favorably influenced imitative learning under high-complexity conditions, the borderline reliability of this effect with younger Ss
review_note: Follow-up used younger preschoolers; benefit was in the same direction but only borderline reliable.

effect_name: Borderline psychotherapy and symptom improvement
effect_claim: Patients with borderline personality disorder improve across symptoms and functioning after a year of structured outpatient psychotherapy.
effect_claim_quote: The subjects showed statistically significant improvement from the initial assessment to the end of the year of follow-up on every measure.
original_title: An outcome study of psychotherapy for patients with borderline personality disorder
replication_title: Borderline personality disorder treated with the conversational model: a replication study
replication_target_quote: original cohort previously reported by Stevenson and Meares
outcome_quote: The rate and degree of improvement in the later cohort are very similar to the original 1992 cohort
review_note: Original study was an uncontrolled treated cohort; follow-up compared another cohort with treatment-as-usual controls.

effect_name: Dyslexia changes phase of speech entrainment
effect_claim: Children with developmental dyslexia show a different phase of low-frequency neural entrainment to rhythmic speech than other children.
effect_claim_quote: significant group difference in the preferred phase of entrainment in the delta band
original_title: Neural entrainment to rhythmic speech in children with developmental dyslexia
replication_title: Neural entrainment to speech and nonspeech in dyslexia: Conceptual replication and extension of previous investigations
replication_target_quote: conceptually replicate previous studies on auditory entrainment in dyslexia
outcome_quote: We failed to observe any of the significant group differences that had previously been reported in delta, theta and gamma frequency bands
review_note: Follow-up found some differences in amplitude cross-correlation for nonspeech noise, but not the original phase-of-speech entrainment contrast.

effect_name: Tailored biofeedback helps psychophysiologic insomnia
effect_claim: Biofeedback matched to the initial tension profile improves sleep in people with psychophysiologic insomnia.
effect_claim_quote: Those treated with the biofeedback that seemed appropriate for their specific deficiencies showed significant sleep improvements
original_title: Treating Psychophysiologic Insomnia With Biofeedback
replication_title: The treatment of psychophysiologic insomnia with biofeedback: A replication study
replication_target_quote: To replicate a previous study, 16 psychophysiological insomniacs
outcome_quote: tense and anxious insomniacs benefited only from Theta feedback but not from SMR feedback, while those who were relaxed at intake but still could not sleep benefited only from SMR but not from Theta feedback.
review_note: Follow-up compared theta with sensorimotor-rhythm feedback and repeated a subgroup-specific benefit; original had additional arms and no universal benefit versus controls.

effect_name: Shifting ability moderates worked-example benefit
effect_claim: Worked examples help learners with lower attention-shifting ability more than learners with higher shifting ability.
effect_claim_quote: The higher the shifting ability and fluid intelligence were, the lower was the benefit of worked examples compared with problem solving.
original_title: Executive functions as moderators of the worked example effect: When shifting is more important than working memory capacity.
replication_title: Does Learners' Shifting Ability Moderate the Worked Example Effect on Statistical Reasoning? A Replication Study
replication_journal: Proceedings of the 2019 AERA Annual Meeting
replication_target_quote: These findings align with the results of the original study (Schwaighofer et al., 2016).
outcome_quote: WEs were more beneficial for learners with low than for learners with high shifting ability.
review_note: Follow-up tested statistical reasoning and added time-pressure conditions; the claim is limited to the shifting interaction.

effect_name: Pornography predicts later extramarital-sex attitudes
effect_claim: Among married adults, earlier pornography use predicts more favorable later attitudes toward extramarital sex.
effect_claim_quote: prior pornography consumption was correlated with more positive subsequent extramarital sex attitudes in both samples
original_title: More than a dalliance? Pornography consumption and extramarital sex attitudes among married U.S. adults.
replication_title: Pornography Consumption and Extramarital Sex Attitudes Among Married U.S. Adults: Longitudinal Replication
replication_target_quote: replicative of the Wright et al.
outcome_quote: the association between baseline pornography consumption and interindividual change in extramarital sex attitudes was not significant.
review_note: Both studies used longitudinal attitudes; the follow-up reports a null adjusted association.

effect_name: Hearing impairment accompanies psychosis
effect_claim: People with psychosis have poorer hearing than people without psychosis.
effect_claim_quote: Experimental subjects were found to have significantly poorer unilateral pure tone averages (PTA) and significantly poorer bilateral speech discrimination ability than control subjects.
original_title: Hearing Impairment and Psychosis
replication_title: Hearing impairment and psychosis: A replication in a cohort of young adults
replication_target_quote: These results replicate previous findings of an association between hearing impairment and psychosis
outcome_quote: These results replicate previous findings of an association between hearing impairment and psychosis
review_note: Original studied hospitalized older adults; follow-up examined a cohort of young adults, so the association extends across age groups.

effect_name: Eye movements reduce later visual-memory accessibility
effect_claim: Eye movements during recall reduce the vividness and later accessibility of visual memories.
effect_claim_quote: Reduction of memory vividness due to recall+EM is also evident from non-self-report data.
original_title: On EMDR: Eye movements during retrieval reduce subjective vividness and objective memory accessibility during future recall
replication_title: Eye movement during recall reduces objective memory performance: An extended replication
replication_target_quote: two objective tests of memory performance
outcome_quote: EM during stimulus recall not only reduces self-reported memory vividness, but also slows down reaction time in a task that requires participants to discriminate the stimulus from perceptually similar stimuli.
review_note: Outcome concerns the discrimination and vividness contrast. A separate conditioned-fear result was not corroborated by startle EMG.

effect_name: Four behavioral syndromes of schizophrenia
effect_claim: Four distinct problem-behavior patterns characterize patients with schizophrenia.
effect_claim_quote: Four behavioural syndromes were identified: 'Thought disturbance', 'Social withdrawal', 'Depressed behaviour' and 'Anti-social behaviour'
original_title: Four Behavioural Syndromes of Schizophrenia
replication_title: Four behavioural syndromes of schizophrenia: a replication in a second inner-London epidemiological sample
replication_target_quote: original Camden study
outcome_quote: The four syndromes extracted from the Feighner positive sample showed relationships to symptoms and social functioning variables similar to those found in the original Camden study.
review_note: Second inner-London epidemiological sample extracted the same four behavioral patterns with similar functional correlates.

effect_name: Practice leadership and positive staff experience
effect_claim: Practice-oriented frontline leadership is linked to more positive work experiences among disability-service staff.
effect_claim_quote: Practice leadership was positively associated with lower stress, greater positive work experiences for staff
original_title: Leadership at the front line: Impact of practice leadership management style on staff experience in services for people with intellectual disability and challenging behaviour
replication_title: Impact of practice leadership management style on staff experience in services for people with intellectual disability and challenging behaviour: A further examination and partial replication
replication_target_quote: partially replicate the findings of (Deveau & McGill, 2014)
outcome_quote: demonstrated an association between PL and greater job satisfaction and positive experiences for staff.
review_note: Verdict concerns positive work experience. Staff turnover results were inconsistent, and neither survey establishes causation.

effect_name: Landolt scanning recruits right parietal cortex
effect_claim: A wordless left-to-right scanning task recruits right superior parietal regions more than reading orthographic material.
effect_claim_quote: additional involvement of the right superior parietal cortex
original_title: Identifying brain systems for gaze orienting during reading: fMRI investigation of the Landolt paradigm
replication_title: Reading without words or target detection? A re-analysis and replication fMRI study of the Landolt paradigm
replication_target_quote: Experiment 2 was a replication study with a new sample and identical procedures.
outcome_quote: In both experiments, the right IPS/SPL were recruited in the Landolt condition as compared to orthographic stimuli
review_note: Follow-up used an identical-procedure second sample and examined whether target detection itself explained the parietal activation.

effect_name: Stimulus-set size and tact-training efficiency
effect_claim: Training larger sets of words can increase tact-learning efficiency for autistic learners.
effect_claim_quote: larger (i.e., 6 and 12) stimulus set sizes was more efficient than training with smaller (i.e., 3 and 4) stimulus set sizes.
original_title: A comparison of stimulus set size on tact training for children with autism spectrum disorder
replication_title: Comparing Skill Acquisition Under Different Stimulus Set Sizes With Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Replication
replication_target_quote: The current study replicated and extended Kodak et al.
outcome_quote: The set sizes of 3 and 6 stimuli were associated with the most efficient acquisition, whereas the set size of 12 stimuli was not.
review_note: Original found both 6- and 12-item sets efficient; follow-up supported six but not twelve, in adolescents rather than younger children.

effect_name: Therapist orientation affects client recommendations
effect_claim: Psychotherapists' theoretical orientation shapes methods they recommend for clients more than methods they use for themselves.
effect_claim_quote: change processes used for treating clients varied in frequency as a function of the S's orientation. In contrast, there were no discernable differences on any of the change processes for self-change
original_title: Psychotherapists' perspectives on treating themselves and their clients for psychic distress.
replication_title: Treating ourselves vs. Treating our clients: A replication with alcohol abuse
replication_target_quote: In an attempt to replicate previous findings
outcome_quote: employment of particular change processes varied as a function of theoretical orientation for psychologists' client change but not for psychologists' self-change.
review_note: Follow-up focused specifically on alcohol-abuse treatment choices instead of general psychic distress.

effect_name: Defensive pressure and three-point shooting
effect_claim: Basketball players make a higher proportion of three-point shots under defensive pressure than when left open.
effect_claim_quote: shooting success was higher when the players shot under defensive pressure.
original_title: “Don't think, just shoot” – The paradox of shooting three-point shots in basketball
original_journal: International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology
replication_title: The “three-point shooting paradox”: An artifact or a real phenomenon? Replication with large-scale National Basketball Association (NBA) data
replication_target_quote: replicate a finding by Lidor et al.
outcome_quote: failed to support the idea of the three-point shooting paradox but instead strongly supports the commonsense hypothesis that tight defense hinders shooting performance.
review_note: Original analyzed 382 Division I shots; follow-up analyzed 781,663 NBA shots, a population and scale change.

effect_name: Preferred activities increase happiness indices
effect_claim: Preferred activities increase observable happiness behaviors in people with profound multiple disabilities.
effect_claim_quote: increases in happiness indices were observed when individuals were presented with most preferred stimuli relative to least preferred stimuli
original_title: DEFINING, VALIDATING, AND INCREASING INDICES OF HAPPINESS AMONG PEOPLE WITH PROFOUND MULTIPLE DISABILITIES
replication_title: A replication to increase happiness indices among some people with profound multiple disabilities
replication_target_quote: A replication of Green and Reid was made for four people with profound multiple disabilities
outcome_quote: 3 of the 4 participants replicated the demonstration of the happiness indices, while the fourth individual showed reduced unhappiness indices
review_note: Three participants showed increased happiness; one showed less unhappiness instead. Follow-up used a Fun Time preferred-stimulus activity.

original_title: Suppression-induced forgetting: a pre-registered replication of the think/no-think paradigm
replication_title: Two replications of Wiechert et al.’s (2023) online Think/No-Think study in undergraduate students
effect_name: Online think/no-think tasks show little suppression-induced forgetting
effect_claim: The original online think/no-think procedure did not produce lower recall for suppression items than baseline items.
effect_claim_quote: Overall, we did not replicate the suppression-induced forgetting effect
replication_target_quote: Wiechert et al.’s [(2023). Suppression-induced forgetting: A pre-registered replication of the think/no-think paradigm.
outcome_quote: The results suggested evidence for SIF in the in-lab setting, yet no evidence was observed in the online setting.
review_note: Online null repeated in undergraduate participants, while in-lab adaptations showed suppression-induced forgetting; a non-significant setting interaction means this is a suggestive boundary, not a proven one.

original_title: Most people do not ignore salient invalid cues in memory-based decisions
replication_title: Salience effects in memory-based decisions: an improved replication
effect_name: Salient invalid cues increase compensatory memory-based decisions
effect_claim: Visually salient but low-validity cues made participants more likely to use compensatory decision strategies.
effect_claim_quote: Only the latter condition increased compensatory decision making
replication_target_quote: salient attributes are often not ignored even if they are less valid than other cues.
outcome_quote: The main experiment clearly replicated the salience effect at the strategy selection level
review_note: New stimuli and larger sample reproduced the decision-strategy result; a secondary response-time interaction did not.

original_title: Increasing the efficiency of paired‐stimulus preference assessments by identifying categories of preference
replication_title: Further evaluation of the use of preference categories to identify novel reinforcers: A systematic replication
effect_name: Preference categories identify novel effective reinforcers
effect_claim: Categories containing highly preferred edible items predicted which novel items would act as reinforcers for people with developmental disabilities.
effect_claim_quote: items from the highest ranked preference category, some of which were included in the preference assessments and some of which were not, functioned as reinforcers.
replication_target_quote: little research has been conducted on identifying categories of preferred items.
outcome_quote: Novel items (i.e., items not included in the preference assessments) identified by the researchers as belonging to the high‐preference category functioned as effective reinforcers
review_note: Systematic replication used four people with autism spectrum disorder; original assessment involved six people with developmental disabilities.

effect_name: Four smoking-cessation contemplation subtypes
effect_claim: Smokers in the contemplation stage form four distinct motivational subtypes.
effect_claim_quote: Four distinct subtypes were found in Precontemplation and Contemplation, and five subtypes were found in Preparation.
original_title: Cluster subtypes within stage of change in a representative sample of smokers
replication_title: Replication of subtypes for smoking cessation within the contemplation stage of change
replication_target_quote: This study attempts to replicate cluster subtypes within the Contemplation stage of change in a secondary analysis of data from a sample of current smokers (N=3967).
outcome_quote: Four distinct cluster subtypes (Classic Contemplators, Progressing, Early Contemplators, and Disengaged) were found and replicated across samples.
review_note: The later paper explicitly identifies Norman et al. (2000) as its target in its introduction; only the Contemplation-stage finding is assessed.

effect_name: Positive conditioning and body satisfaction
effect_claim: Pairing body pictures with positive social cues increases body satisfaction in women with high body concern.
effect_claim_quote: Women with high body concern demonstrated an increase in body satisfaction and global self-esteem when pictorial representations of their own bodies were associated with positive stimuli that signaled social acceptance.
original_title: Increasing body satisfaction of body concerned women through evaluative conditioning using social stimuli.
replication_title: Reducing body dissatisfaction by means of an evaluative conditioning procedure in undergraduate women: A replication study
replication_target_quote: Therefore, our main goal was to replicate the original finding of Martijn et al.
outcome_quote: However, this effect of the EC procedure did not transfer to the self-report indices of body satisfaction.
review_note: The replication found more positive ratings of trained pictures, but not improved self-reported body satisfaction; it used a larger unselected student sample.

effect_name: Challenging behavior as a depressive equivalent
effect_claim: Aggression and self-injury are not reliable indicators of depression in people with intellectual disability.
effect_claim_quote: Challenging behaviours such as self-injury or aggression were not closely associated with depression.
original_title: Challenging behaviours should not be considered as depressive equivalents in individuals with intellectual disability
replication_title: Challenging behaviors should not be considered depressive equivalents in individuals with intellectual disabilities. II. A replication study
replication_target_quote: The relationship between a measure of depression and several proposed behavioral equivalents of depression was assessed in 693 adults living in a large residential setting.
outcome_quote: No support was found for behavioral equivalents of depression.
review_note: The later paper explicitly says it replicated Tsiouris et al. (2003), including the weak association between challenging behavior and depression.

effect_name: Bipolar screening and later improvement
effect_claim: Among people screening positive on the Mood Swings Questionnaire, those taking action and receiving clinical confirmation show the largest later improvement.
effect_claim_quote: those who took assertive action and had the diagnosis confirmed had the most superior outcome.
original_title: The ‘real world’ utility of a web‐based bipolar disorder screening measure
replication_title: The ‘real world’ utility of a web-based bipolar disorder screening measure: A replication study
replication_target_quote: We previously reported high acceptance of the Mood Swings Questionnaire (MSQ) bipolar disorder screening measure, as well as improved outcomes for those completing the test, leading to this independent replication study.
outcome_quote: All three sample sub-sets improved on key study measures--with those receiving a confirmed bipolar diagnosis (and thus most likely to have management plans modified) reporting the greatest improvement.
review_note: Observational follow-up in both studies; the papers do not establish that screening or diagnosis caused improvement.

effect_name: Resilience and life satisfaction in wheelchair athletes
effect_claim: Greater resilience predicts higher life satisfaction among wheelchair athletes.
effect_claim_quote: athletes with high levels of hardiness and resilience reported the highest quality of life.
original_title: Gritty, Hardy, and Resilient: Predictors of Sport Engagement and Life Satisfaction in Wheelchair Basketball Players
replication_title: Gritty, hardy, resilient, and socially supported: A replication study
replication_target_quote: In the current study we replicated previous findings by predicting life quality and sport engagement using measures of grit, hardiness, and resilience.
outcome_quote: Athletes reporting high levels of resilience reported the highest quality of life.
review_note: Replication used wheelchair rugby rather than basketball. The broader original predictor pattern was only partially replicated; this narrower resilience-life-satisfaction result did replicate.

effect_name: Domain-general interference in serial memory
effect_claim: Spatial tapping and articulatory suppression impair verbal and spatial serial memory to comparable extents.
effect_claim_quote: Effects were comparable to those found with a serial verbal task that was generally similar in demand characteristics to the spatial task.
original_title: Functional equivalence of verbal and spatial information in serial short-term memory.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
replication_title: A Replication of "Functional Equivalence of Verbal and Spatial Information in Serial Short-Term Memory (1995; Experiments 2 and 3)".
replication_target_quote: In the present study, we replicated the second and third experiments of Jones et al.
outcome_quote: This interaction reflects the larger detrimental effect of the interference task when it is in the same domain as the memory task
review_note: Direct replication of Experiments 2 and 3. This result quote is verbatim in the cached published PDF extract at https://www.tqmp.org/ReplicationStudies/vol11-2/r004/r004.pdf (p. 5, Results); full sentence contrasts within-domain with cross-domain interference.

effect_name: Accuracy gain from averaging two guesses
effect_claim: The average of two guesses from one person is more accurate than either guess alone.
