effect_claim_quote: The average of two guesses from one individual (within-person average) was more accurate (lower mean squared error) than either guess alone
original_title: Measuring the Crowd Within
replication_title: Replication of Vul & Pashler (Psych Science, 2008)
replication_target_quote: We attempted to replicate the crowd within effect, which is the effect that the average of two guesses within one person provides a more accurate answer than either guess alone.
outcome_quote: Our results successfully replicated the original finding by Vul and Pashler (2008) that averaging two guesses within one person provides a more accurate answer than either guess alone.
review_note: Original result quote verified in the original article PDF at https://perception.jhu.edu/chaz/teaching/courses/tp/files/readings/9/Vul_Pashler_2008_Psychological_Science_Measuring_the_Crowd_Within_Probabilistic_Representations_Within_Individuals.pdf (p. 645, Results). OSF project reports the completed published replication (Steegen et al., 2014).

effect_name: Slower learning from negative outcomes in substance use disorder
effect_claim: People with substance use disorder learn more slowly from losses than healthy controls.
effect_claim_quote: significantly slower learning rates for losses in SUDs than HCs when only comparing groups at follow-up
original_title: Slower Learning Rates from Negative Outcomes in Substance Use Disorder over a 1-Year Period and Their Potential Predictive Utility
replication_title: Attenuated learning rates for negative outcomes in substance use disorders: A replication and extension of prior longitudinal computational modeling results
replication_target_quote: Learning rates for losses were consistently lower in individuals with SUDs than HCs (posterior probability > 0.99), replicating prior findings.
outcome_quote: Learning rates for losses were consistently lower in individuals with SUDs than HCs (posterior probability > 0.99), replicating prior findings.
review_note: Original result quote verified in published original full text at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11104312/ (Results paragraph after Table 5). The later paper used an independent confirmatory sample and did not reproduce the exploratory symptom-prediction result.

effect_name: Bilingualism and dementia symptom onset
effect_claim: Bilingual patients show dementia symptoms several years later than comparable monolingual patients.
effect_claim_quote: The bilinguals showed symptoms of dementia 4 years later than monolinguals
original_title: Bilingualism as a protection against the onset of symptoms of dementia
replication_title: Effects of bilingualism on the age of onset and progression of MCI and AD: Evidence from executive function tests.
replication_target_quote: Previous articles have reported that bilingualism is associated with a substantial delay in the onset
outcome_quote: Results replicated the finding that bilingual patients are several years older than comparable monolinguals at both age of symptom onset and date of first clinic visit.
review_note: The original included dementia patients; the later sample included MCI and Alzheimer's disease.

effect_name: Vagus nerve stimulation and fear extinction
effect_claim: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation accelerates explicit conditioned-fear extinction.
effect_claim_quote: tVNS accelerated explicit fear extinction learning (US expectancy ratings)
original_title: The effects of transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation on conditioned fear extinction in humans
replication_title: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation and extinction of prepared fear: A conceptual non-replication
replication_target_quote: Here, we aimed to investigate this hypothesis in healthy young participants in a prepared learning paradigm
outcome_quote: the expected accelerated extinction due to tVNS was not observed
review_note: Conceptual replication used spider pictures and a prepared-fear paradigm; the original's 24-hour retention effect was already null.

effect_name: Meal recall reduces later snacking
effect_claim: Recalling a recent lunch reduces later snack consumption relative to recalling an earlier meal.
effect_claim_quote: Participants who recalled the lunch they had eaten that day consumed less of all types of popcorn than participants who recalled lunch eaten the previous day
original_title: Recall of recent lunch and its effect on subsequent snack intake
replication_title: The role of memory ability, depth and mode of recall in the impact of memory on later consumption
replication_target_quote: This study attempted to replicate this effect, by assessing participants'
outcome_quote: only the written group demonstrated the meal-recall effect, whereas the verbal group did not
review_note: Written unguided recall showed lower biscuit intake; verbal recall did not and written guided recall reversed the pattern.

effect_name: Acute stress shifts action toward habits
effect_claim: Acute stress after instrumental learning reduces sensitivity to outcome devaluation and favors habitual responding.
effect_claim_quote: Controls but not stressed participants reduced responding to the action associated with the devalued outcome.
original_title: Socially evaluated cold pressor stress after instrumental learning favors habits over goal-directed action
replication_title: Stress-induced reliance on habitual behavior is moderated by cortisol reactivity
replication_target_quote: The aim of the current studies was to replicate and extend findings on stress-induced prompting of habitual responding
outcome_quote: Both studies failed to replicate that stress overall, i.e., independent of cortisol reactivity, shifted behavior from goal-directed to habitual control. However, both studies found that relative to stress-exposed cortisol non-responders and no-stress controls, participants displaying stress-induced cortisol reactivity displayed prominent habitual responding.
review_note: Overall stress effect failed, but a cortisol-reactive subgroup showed habitual responding, matching the original moderator.

effect_name: Graduated exposure increases skin-product tolerance in autism
effect_claim: Graduated exposure, modeling, and social attention increase children's tolerance of skin-care products.
effect_claim_quote: The results suggest that the package was successful in teaching tolerance of skin products for both children.
original_title: The effects of graduated exposure, modeling, and contingent social attention on tolerance to skin care products with two children with autism
replication_title: Using a Behavioral Treatment Package to Teach Tolerance to Skin Care Products to a Child with Autism: A Systematic Replication
replication_target_quote: The current study uses graduated exposure, modeling and contingent social attention to teach the child to accept the application of skin care products previously avoided.
outcome_quote: Results of the study showed that the participant tolerated criterion amounts of all target stimuli with both experimenter and parent. Follow-up probes revealed maintenance of the behaviors with only two out of the three target skin care products.
review_note: Systematic replication in one child achieved initial tolerance for all products, with maintenance for two of three.

effect_name: Fishy smells reduce cooperation
effect_claim: Incidental fishy odor elicits social suspicion and lowers cooperation in a public-goods game.
effect_claim_quote: Incidental exposure to fishy smells induced suspicion and undermined cooperation in trust-based economic exchanges in a trust game (Study 1) and a public goods game (Study 2).
original_title: Bidirectionality, mediation, and moderation of metaphorical effects: The embodiment of social suspicion and fishy smells.
replication_title: Exploring the boundaries of embodied cognition and conceptual metaphor theory
replication_target_quote: two empirical studies designed to replicate and extend research on the embodied fishiness-suspicion conceptual metaphor.
outcome_quote: Consistent with the original experiments, exposure to a fishy smell undermined cooperation (i.e., Public Goods game; Lee & Schwarz, 2012)
review_note: This row concerns the olfactory public-goods test; the thesis's separate visual-cue extension failed.

effect_name: Intuition increases cooperation
effect_claim: Inducing intuitive rather than reflective thinking increases cooperation in social dilemmas.
effect_claim_quote: an induction that primes subjects to trust their intuitions increases contributions compared with an induction that promotes greater reflection.
original_title: Spontaneous giving and calculated greed
replication_title: Spontaneous Giving under Structural Inequality: Intuition Promotes Cooperation in Asymmetric Social Dilemmas
replication_target_quote: The present research investigates the role of intuitive mental processing on cooperation in experimental games involving structural inequality.
outcome_quote: cooperation is promoted by intuition in an asymmetric context
review_note: Conceptual replication used an asymmetric game and conceptual priming.

effect_name: Diet composition and anorexia outcome
effect_claim: Lower dietary energy density and variety predict poorer outcomes after weight restoration for anorexia nervosa.
effect_claim_quote: lower DEDS and DVS but not caloric intake were associated with poor outcome.
original_title: Dietary energy density and diet variety as predictors of outcome in anorexia nervosa
replication_title: Dietary energy density and diet variety as risk factors for relapse in anorexia nervosa: A replication
replication_target_quote: To replicate our previous findings of an association between energy density and diet variety
outcome_quote: a lower DEDS, but not DVS, is associated with poor clinical outcome after inpatient treatment.
review_note: Energy density replicated; diet variety did not reach significance in the small later sample.

effect_name: Preemption and entrenchment in verb generalization
effect_claim: Higher bare-verb and alternative-form frequencies each reduce acceptance of ungrammatical un-forms.
effect_claim_quote: Across verbs, a negative correlation was observed between the acceptability of ungrammatical un‐ prefixed forms (e.g., *unclose ) and the frequency of (a) the bare form and (b) alternative forms (e.g., open ), supporting the entrenchment and pre‐emption hypotheses, respectively.
original_title: How Do Children Restrict Their Linguistic Generalizations? An (Un-)Grammaticality Judgment Study
replication_title: Effects of Both Preemption and Entrenchment in the Retreat from Verb Overgeneralization Errors: Four Reanalyses, an Extended Replication, and a Meta-Analytic Synthesis
replication_target_quote: Across a reanalysis of two previous studies of un- prefixation, and a new extended replication with adults
outcome_quote: we find dissociable effects of both preemption and entrenchment.
review_note: The later paper reanalyzed previous child data and added an adult replication; it uses improved measures.

effect_name: Right hemisphericity and self-esteem
effect_claim: Greater self-reported right hemisphericity is associated with lower self-esteem.
effect_claim_quote: People who reported the greatest numbers of right hemispheric indicators displayed the lowest self-esteem
original_title: Greater Right Hemisphericity is Associated with Lower Self-Esteem in Adults
replication_title: Right Hemisphericity and Low Self-Esteem in High School Students: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Greater right hemisphericity was associated with lower self-esteem.
outcome_quote: Greater right hemisphericity was associated with lower self-esteem.
review_note: The replication used high-school students and a different self-esteem questionnaire; both used Vingiano's hemisphericity questionnaire.

effect_name: Prepositional-object priming exceeds double-object priming
effect_claim: Cumulative structural priming is stronger for prepositional-object than double-object constructions.
effect_claim_quote: biasing participants toward the prepositional object construction produced stronger cumulative priming effects than did biasing participants toward the double object construction.
original_title: Structural priming as implicit learning: Cumulative priming effects and individual differences
replication_title: Implicit and Explicit Memory Factors in Cumulative Structural Priming
replication_target_quote: In the first two experiments, we replicate the finding that stronger cumulative structural priming
outcome_quote: stronger cumulative structural priming is observed for the prepositional object (PO) construction than for the double object (DO) construction.
review_note: The later paper directly tested this contrast in its first two experiments.

effect_name: Smiling increases estimated facial age
effect_claim: Smiling faces are estimated as older than neutral faces.
effect_claim_quote: smiling faces were perceived as older than neutral faces.
original_title: The effects of smiling on perceived age defy belief
replication_title: The effect of emotional expression on age estimates is modulated by face age and participant age
replication_target_quote: The results replicated previous findings that happy faces were perceived as older than neutral faces when faces were young.
outcome_quote: When faces were older, smiling did not age the faces
review_note: The effect repeated for young faces but was absent for older faces; the later study also varied face race and observer age.

effect_name: Contingently faded biofeedback lowers heart rate
effect_claim: Contingently faded heart-rate biofeedback produces a larger heart-rate decrease than control feedback.
effect_claim_quote: The group receiving contingently faded feedback training showed a significantly greater heart rate decrease in the training sessions and also the test session.
original_title: The production and generalization of large-magnitude heart rate deceleration by contingently faded biofeedback
replication_title: Contingently faded heart rate biofeedback: Attempted replication of large-magnitude decreases
replication_target_quote: The present study compared decreases in HR in 20 male subjects receiving the contingently faded biofeedback procedure
outcome_quote: The former group showed significantly greater decreases in HR that could not be attributed to elevated baseline levels. However, the decreases in HR were not as large as those reported by McKinney et al. (1980).
review_note: Direction replicated, but original large magnitude did not.

effect_name: Three meanings of sex and commitment
effect_claim: Emerging adults' descriptions of sex and commitment commonly fall into commitment, flexibility, and recreation themes.
effect_claim_quote: Our largest group was the Committers (sex is indicative of love and trust and occurs after commitment is developed in a relationship), followed by Flexibles (sex can hold deep personal meaning, but can also be purely for pleasure and isn't always connected with commitment), and then Recreationers (sex is a basic need or purely for pleasure and is not associated with commitment).
original_title: Meanings for Sex and Commitment Among First Semester College Men and Women: A Mixed-Methods Analysis
replication_title: Meanings Ascribed to Sex and Commitment Among College-Attending and Non-College Emerging Adults: A Replication and Extension
replication_target_quote: Findings from our content analysis replicated previous research by identifying meanings focused on commitment
outcome_quote: Findings from our content analysis replicated previous research by identifying meanings focused on commitment (47.8%), flexibility (22.7%), and recreation (17.8%).
review_note: The later sample also identified two additional, smaller themes.

effect_name: Response-option order shifts self-rated health
effect_claim: Starting self-rated health response options with 'poor' yields worse average self-ratings than starting with 'excellent'.
effect_claim_quote: Mean SRH is higher (better health) and proportion in "fair" or "poor" health lower when response options are ordered from "excellent" to "poor"
original_title: The effects of response option order and question order on self-rated health
replication_title: The effect of response option order on self-rated health: a replication study
replication_target_quote: experimentally examine the impact of response option order on self-rated health (SRH).
outcome_quote: mean SRH is lower (worse) when the response options start with "poor" rather than "excellent."
review_note: The original factorial design also tested question order; this effect focuses only on response-option order.

effect_name: Oxytocin and mind-reading performance
effect_claim: Intranasal oxytocin improves Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test performance relative to placebo.
effect_claim_quote: Oxytocin improved performance on the RMET compared with placebo.
original_title: Oxytocin Improves “Mind-Reading” in Humans
replication_title: Does oxytocin affect mind-reading? A replication study
replication_target_quote: Following the original design of Domes et al. (2007), the aim of the current study was to replicate and extend previous findings
outcome_quote: Oxytocin did not affect mind-reading, neither in general nor when considering specific item characteristics.
review_note: The later study found an exploratory emotional-empathy moderator, but no overall or item-difficulty effect.

effect_name: Self-compassion buffers body-image threats
effect_claim: Higher self-compassion weakens the negative relationship of body comparison and appearance-contingent self-worth with body appreciation.
effect_claim_quote: when self-compassion was very high, body comparison and appearance contingent self-worth were unrelated to body appreciation.
original_title: Self-compassion moderates body comparison and appearance self-worth’s inverse relationships with body appreciation
replication_title: The protective role of self-compassion for women’s positive body image: an open replication and extension
replication_target_quote: This research, an independent direct replication of the original study, supported the original findings.
outcome_quote: those who endorsed higher levels of self-compassion reported a more positive body image, even in the presence of these potential threats.
review_note: Direct independent replication with a larger sample; the abstract reports the matching moderation pattern.

effect_name: Four child-maltreatment exposure classes
effect_claim: Child maltreatment exposure falls into four classes: none, episodic neglect, episodic abuse, and chronic multiple types.
effect_claim_quote: our analyses identified four classes of children, with three distinct classes based on maltreatment subtypes and chronicity, and one group of children who did not experience maltreatment.
original_title: Identifying maltreatment subgroups with patterns of maltreatment subtype and chronicity: A latent class analysis approach
replication_title: Common patterns of maltreatment exposure: A replication study using confirmatory latent class analysis
replication_target_quote: The current study addresses this gap by replicating a previous LCA of CM exposure using Confirmatory LCA
outcome_quote: Results provide evidence for the replication of four unique latent classes of CM exposure: a) nonmaltreated, b) Episodic, Single-Type (Neglect), c) Episodic, Single-Type (Abuse), d) Chronic, Multi-Type.
review_note: Later confirmatory latent-class analysis used a new low-income child cohort.

effect_name: Mental toughness and physical perseverance
effect_claim: Higher self-reported mental toughness predicts greater behavioral perseverance in an aerobic task.
effect_claim_quote: the association between mental toughness and behavioural perseverance lies between .14 and .34
original_title: When the going gets tough: Mental toughness and its relationship with behavioural perseverance
original_journal: Journal of science and medicine in sport
replication_title: Mental toughness and behavioural perseverance: A conceptual replication and extension
replication_journal: Journal of science and medicine in sport
replication_target_quote: The purpose of this study was to conduct a conceptual replication of the proposition that mental toughness is associated positively with behavioural perseverance.
outcome_quote: the positive association between mental toughness and behavioural perseverance did not generalise to a performance context in which participants were fatigued.
review_note: Typical-condition association repeated only when prior evidence was incorporated; the effect did not generalize after induced fatigue.

effect_name: Family psychosis history in high-risk youth
effect_claim: Among clinically high-risk youth, family psychosis history is linked to greater trauma exposure without a higher psychosis transition rate.
effect_claim_quote: There were no major differences between the groups in symptoms, functioning, IQ, cannabis use or in the rate of conversion between the groups. The CHR + FH group reported increased amounts of early trauma.
original_title: The role of a family history of psychosis for youth at clinical high risk of psychosis
replication_title: Family history of psychosis in youth at clinical high risk: A replication study
replication_target_quote: This paper aims to confirm these results in a new CHR sample, NAPLS-3.
outcome_quote: There were no differences in transition rates between the two groups. This study supports some of the already reported differences in trauma, physical and psychological abuse
review_note: Trauma and unchanged transition replicated, but the later group also differed in symptoms and IQ, unlike the original.

effect_name: Four adolescent smoking-risk subtypes
effect_claim: Adolescents in smoking-acquisition precontemplation fall into four risk-attitude subtypes.
effect_claim_quote: Four distinct subtypes were identified in each subsample: High Risk, Protected, Ambivalent, and Risk Denial.
original_title: Identifying cluster subtypes for the prevention of adolescent smoking acquisition
replication_title: Replicating cluster subtypes for the prevention of adolescent smoking and alcohol use
replication_target_quote: Cluster analysis was performed within each subsample based on three variables: Pros and Cons
outcome_quote: Across all subsamples for both smoking and alcohol, the following four clusters were identified: (1) Most Protected (MP; low Pros, high Cons, low Temptations); (2) Ambivalent (AM; high Pros, average Cons and Temptations); (3) Risk Denial (RD; average Pros, low Cons, average Temptations); and (4) High Risk (HR; high Pros, low Cons, and very high Temptations).
review_note: The later paper extends the four smoking clusters to alcohol and uses five subsamples.

effect_name: BDNF, 5-HTTLPR, and adversity interaction
effect_claim: BDNF genotype, 5-HTTLPR genotype, and childhood maltreatment interact in predicting depressive symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: There was a significant three-way interaction between BDNF genotype, 5-HTTLPR, and maltreatment history in predicting depression.
original_title: Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor–5-HTTLPR Gene Interactions and Environmental Modifiers of Depression in Children
replication_title: The BDNF Val66Met × 5‐HTTLPR × child adversity interaction and depressive symptoms: An attempt at replication
replication_journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part B Neuropsychiatric Genetics
replication_target_quote: Kaufman et al. [2006] reported a higher order interaction effect
outcome_quote: this BDNF Met x childhood adversity interaction in turn was moderated by 5-HTTLPR genotype (three-way interaction)
review_note: Replication used female twins and noted possible gene-environment correlation confounding.

effect_name: Turning-point memory detail predicts adolescent depression
effect_claim: Greater episodic detail in adolescents’ turning-point narratives predicts later increases in depressive symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: uniquely predicted increases in depressive symptoms across the year.
original_title: Delving into the detail: Greater episodic detail in narratives of a critical life event predicts an increase in adolescent depressive symptoms across one year
replication_title: My Turning Point Tells the Story: A Longitudinal Examination of Greater Episodic Detail and Youth Depressive Symptoms
replication_journal: Research on Child and Adolescent Psychopathology
replication_target_quote: we aimed to replicate and extend this finding.
outcome_quote: greater detail did not predict increased depressive symptoms longitudinally.
review_note: Concurrent association recurred, but the longitudinal prediction did not in a six-month follow-up.

effect_name: Need moderates risky-choice framing
effect_claim: Need thresholds reduce or eliminate the framing effect in risky choices.
effect_claim_quote: Both explicit and self-determined need requirements eliminated framing effects
original_title: Beyond gains and losses: The effect of need on risky choice in framed decisions.
replication_title: Replication: Beyond gains and losses by Mishra and Fiddick (2012)
replication_target_quote: close preregistered replication of their Experiment 3
outcome_quote: we observed a framing effect among participants with low need, but not among participants with high need.
review_note: Close preregistered replication found the standard framing effect and need relationship, with a remaining effect in low-need participants.

effect_name: Misinformation weakens concealed-information testing
effect_claim: Misleading post-event information weakens the physiological discrimination used by the Concealed Information Test.
effect_claim_quote: no physiological response differences between crime‐relevant and crime‐irrelevant information were found.
original_title: The Concealed Information Test is Susceptible to Misleading Information
replication_title: Is the CIT susceptible to misleading information? A constructive replication
replication_target_quote: constructive replication of Volz et al.
outcome_quote: physiological responses to the critical CIT items were only partially attenuated.
review_note: Explicit memory declined, but physiological detection remained partly possible.

effect_name: Emotional well-being in children with sickle cell disease
effect_claim: Children with sickle cell disease show broadly similar emotional well-being to classroom comparison peers.
effect_claim_quote: no other differences were identified on numerous measures of emotional well-being.
original_title: Peer Relationships and Emotional Well-Being of Youngsters with Sickle Cell Disease
replication_title: Peer Relationships and Emotional Well-Being of Children with Sickle Cell Disease: A Controlled Replication
replication_target_quote: replication study examining the social and emotional functioning
outcome_quote: No group differences were identified for emotional well-being.
review_note: Replication also found differences in some peer and teacher ratings; this claim concerns emotional well-being only.

effect_name: Hypothetical trolley judgments predict real choices
effect_claim: Hypothetical sacrificial-dilemma choices do not predict behavior in a corresponding real-life dilemma.
effect_claim_quote: responses to hypothetical dilemmas are not predictive of real-life dilemma behavior
original_title: Of Mice, Men, and Trolleys: Hypothetical Judgment Versus Real-Life Behavior in Trolley-Style Moral Dilemmas
replication_title: Hypothetical Judgment and Real-Life Decision-Making in Sacrificial Dilemmas: A Replication of “of Mice, Men and Trolleys”
replication_target_quote: aimed at replicating and extending this earlier work.
outcome_quote: responses to hypothetical dilemma batteries significantly predict real-life dilemma decisions.
review_note: Replication still found context-dependent switching; its prediction result differs from the original.

effect_name: Memory capacity and cognitive offloading
effect_claim: Use of external memory storage varies with memory load and a person’s actual or perceived memory capacity.
effect_claim_quote: external storage was related both to the number of items to be remembered and an individual's actual and perceived short-term-memory capacity.
original_title: Storing information in-the-world: Metacognition and cognitive offloading in a short-term memory task
replication_title: Offloading items from memory: individual differences in cognitive offloading in a short-term memory task
replication_target_quote: replication and extension of a previous study conducted by Risko and Dunn
outcome_quote: we fail to observe that those with poorer memory abilities have a greater propensity for offloading
review_note: Replication found an offloading performance benefit at higher loads, but not a greater propensity among people with poorer memory.

effect_name: Neuroticism and bulimic symptoms
effect_claim: Higher neuroticism is associated with more bulimic symptoms in a nonclinical sample of young women.
effect_claim_quote: A relationship was obtained between Neuroticism, Addictiveness, and scores on the BULIT-R.
original_title: Personality and bulimic symptomatology
replication_title: Bulimic Symptomatology and Personality Factors in a Nonclinical Sample: A Replication
replication_target_quote: replicated the 1993 findings of Janzen, Saklofske, and Kelly
outcome_quote: the strongest relationship with bulimic symptomatology was for Neuroticism.
review_note: The replication differed on Psychoticism; the named claim concerns Neuroticism.

effect_name: Instructive feedback and play skills in autism
effect_claim: Embedding instructive feedback in discrete-trial teaching can produce new play behavior in children with autism.
effect_claim_quote: Instructive feedback resulted in the emergence of play behaviors
original_title: An Evaluation of Instructive Feedback to Teach Play Behavior to a Child with Autism Spectrum Disorder
replication_title: A Systematic Replication: Instructive Feedback to Produce Emerging Play Responses
replication_target_quote: we replicated and extended Grow et al. (2016)
outcome_quote: two participants demonstrated some acquisition and generalization of the secondary toy play responses.
review_note: Systematic replication of three children: two showed some secondary play-response acquisition and generalization.

effect_name: Gratton effect after confound control
effect_claim: Removing contingency biases and stimulus repetitions eliminates the response-time Gratton effect.
effect_claim_quote: This eliminated the Gratton effect in the response times in both experiments
original_title: Now you see it, now you don't: Controlling for contingencies and stimulus repetitions eliminates the Gratton effect
replication_title: The Gratton effect remains after controlling for contingencies and stimulus repetitions
replication_target_quote: attempts to replicate and extend this important finding
outcome_quote: we observe reliable conflict adaptation after controlling for feature binding.
review_note: Replication used a vocal four-choice Stroop task rather than the original button-press and flanker tasks.

effect_name: Preference for nanotechnology packaging over foods
effect_claim: Consumers perceive nanotechnology food packaging more favorably than nanotechnology inside foods.
effect_claim_quote: nanotechnology packaging is perceived as being more beneficial than nanotechnology foods.
original_title: Public acceptance of nanotechnology foods and food packaging: The influence of affect and trust
replication_title: COMPARISON OF NANOTECHNOLOGY ACCEPTANCE IN TURKEY AND SWITZERLAND
replication_journal: International Journal of Innovation and Technology Management
replication_target_quote: aim of this paper is to replicate the study of Siegrist et al.
outcome_quote: Results did not support any evidence suggesting that the nanoinside applications are perceived as less acceptable than nanooutside application
review_note: Conceptual cross-country comparison used Turkish participants and different applications; outcome is limited to the inside/outside preference.

effect_name: Direct eye gaze increases Stroop interference
effect_claim: Eye contact increases interference during a concurrent Stroop task.
effect_claim_quote: participants showed stronger Stroop interference under concomitant eye contact
original_title: The cost of being watched: Stroop interference increases under concomitant eye contact
replication_title: The interference effect of direct eye gaze in the Stroop paradigm
replication_target_quote: first was to replicate the increased Stroop effect under direct eye gaze.
outcome_quote: we could not replicate previous findings of direct eye gaze increasing the Stroop effect.
review_note: Three experiments, including a direct replication, found no increase.

effect_name: Cross-language regularities in reading eye movements
effect_claim: Eye-movement models reveal common aspects of reading in Chinese, English, and Finnish.
effect_claim_quote: statistical models of reading behaviour were strikingly similar in a number of respects
original_title: Universality in eye movements and reading: A trilingual investigation
replication_title: Universality in eye movements and reading: A replication with increased power
replication_target_quote: Liversedge, Drieghe, Li, Yan, Bai and Hyönä (2016)
outcome_quote: Unlike the original findings, the new analyses showed shorter total sentence reading times for Chinese relative to Finnish and English readers. The other main findings reported in the original study were consistent.
review_note: Larger samples supported most cross-language patterns but changed the sentence-time comparison.

effect_name: Basic psychological needs in first-episode psychosis
effect_claim: People with first-episode psychosis report less autonomy, competence, and relatedness than peers without psychosis.
effect_claim_quote: individuals with first-episode psychosis experience less satisfaction of basic psychological needs
original_title: Self-determination and first-episode psychosis: Associations with symptomatology, social and vocational functioning, and quality of life
replication_title: Self-Determination Theory and First-Episode Psychosis: A Replication
replication_target_quote: goal of this project was to replicate Breitborde et al.’s (2012)
outcome_quote: Our results supported the conclusion that individuals with first-episode psychosis report lower autonomy, competence, and relatedness
review_note: Replication also reported similar associations with symptoms, social functioning, and quality of life.

effect_name: Age and general benevolence
effect_claim: General Benevolence scores increase across adulthood.
effect_claim_quote: General Benevolence exhibited a robust increase across the adult life span
original_title: A general benevolence dimension that links neural, psychological, economic, and life-span data on altruistic tendencies.
replication_title: Beyond money: Nonmonetary prosociality across adulthood.
replication_target_quote: Conceptually replicating findings from Hubbard, Harbaugh, Srivastava, Degras, and Mayr (2016)
outcome_quote: older adults are not consistently more likely to behave prosocially than younger or middle-aged adults in nonmonetary domains.
review_note: A first hypothetical nonmonetary measure rose with age, but two behavioral time-donation studies did not generalize the result.

effect_name: Infant expectations about simple arithmetic
effect_claim: Infants expect the outcomes of simple addition and subtraction events.
effect_claim_quote: 5-month-old infants can calculate the results of simple arithmetical operations
original_title: Addition and subtraction by human infants
replication_title: Do you believe in magic? Infants? social looking during violations of expectations
replication_target_quote: Two experiments replicated the results of well-known physical knowledge experiments on addition/subtraction
outcome_quote: infants at both ages looked longer at unexpected than at expected events.
review_note: Replication included addition/subtraction and occlusion tasks with 6- and 9-month-old infants; the named claim is the numerical expectation.

effect_name: Reconsolidation-window extinction prevents fear return
effect_claim: Extinction training shortly after fear-memory reactivation can prevent later return of fear.
effect_claim_quote: fear responses are no longer expressed, an effect that lasted at least a year
original_title: Preventing the return of fear in humans using reconsolidation update mechanisms
replication_title: Updating Fearful Memories with Extinction Training during Reconsolidation: A Human Study Using Auditory Aversive Stimuli
replication_target_quote: We sought out to reproduce Schiller et al., (2010) findings
outcome_quote: only the conditioned stimulus that was reminded 10 minutes before extinction training did not reinstate a fear response
review_note: Replication used auditory aversive stimuli rather than electric shock; abstract does not establish the original one-year duration.

effect_name: Communicative cues shift infant object memory
effect_claim: Infants in communicative contexts favor remembering an object’s identity over its location.
effect_claim_quote: infants devoted their limited memory resources to encoding the identity of novel objects at the expense of encoding their location
original_title: Communication-induced memory biases in preverbal infants
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Evaluating the replicability and specificity of evidence for natural pedagogy theory
replication_target_quote: attempted two replications of the study with the highest theoretical value for NP (Yoon et al., 2008)
outcome_quote: we were unable to replicate the original findings.
review_note: Replication source is a Lancaster University doctoral thesis; two attempted replications are summarized in its abstract.

effect_name: Pathogen cues increase facial-symmetry preference
effect_claim: Exposure to pathogen cues increases preference for symmetric opposite-sex faces.
effect_claim_quote: Change in preferences was seen mainly for opposite-sex faces
original_title: Exposure to visual cues of pathogen contagion changes preferences for masculinity and symmetry in opposite-sex faces
replication_title: Pathogen avoidance mechanisms affect women’s preference for symmetrical male faces.
replication_target_quote: conceptual replication of research reported by Little, DeBruine, and Jones (2011)
outcome_quote: exposure to disease cues increased preference for symmetrical opposite sex targets
review_note: Conceptual replication reproduced symmetry preference; relative strength differed by sex.

effect_name: False-belief word-learning advantage
effect_claim: Young children track another person’s false belief better in a word-learning task than in a standard action-prediction task.
effect_claim_quote: Children were significantly better at tracking the puppet’s false belief
original_title: ‘Theory of Mind’ and Tracking Speakers’ Intentions
replication_title: Tracking speakers’ false beliefs: is theory of mind available earlier for word learning?
replication_target_quote: Happé and Loth (2002) describe word learning as a 'privileged domain'
outcome_quote: performance discrepancy disappeared when tasks were equated in their 'referential pull'
review_note: Experiment 1 reproduced the advantage; Experiments 2–3 removed it when task demands were matched.

effect_name: Metaphor-incongruent location memory advantage
effect_claim: Positive and negative words are better remembered when learned in locations incongruent with the GOOD is UP metaphor.
effect_claim_quote: memory advantage for words that had been studied in metaphor incongruent locations
original_title: "Good Is Up” Is Not Always Better: A Memory Advantage for Words in Metaphor-Incompatible Locations
replication_title: The “good is up” metaphoric effects on recognition: True for source guessing but false for item memory
replication_target_quote: conceptual replication and extension of Experiment 2 by Crawford et al., (2014)
outcome_quote: no metaphor-(in)congruent effects in memory
review_note: Conceptual replication found a guessing bias for source location but no item or source-memory advantage.

effect_name: Native-language advantage in face recognition
effect_claim: Faces paired with a listener’s native language are recognized more accurately than faces paired with a foreign language.
effect_claim_quote: participants were more accurate at remembering faces previously paired with their native as opposed to their FL.
original_title: Speak My Language and I Will Remember Your Face Better: An ERP Study
replication_title: Social Categorization Based on Language and Facial Recognition
replication_journal: Journal of Language and Social Psychology
replication_target_quote: replicate the effect found by Baus et al.
outcome_quote: Faces presented along with Swedish utterances were not recognized better than faces presented along with English utterances. In Study 2, we used another language pair and presented faces along with utterances in Swedish and in Spanish to native Swedish speakers. Faces presented along with Swedish utterances were recognized better than faces presented along with Spanish utterances.
review_note: Swedish-versus-English comparison failed; Swedish-versus-Spanish comparison succeeded.

original_title: The influence of retrieval processes in verbal overshadowing
replication_title: The development of a computer system to collect descriptions of culprits
effect_name: Forced detailed eyewitness descriptions impair face identification
effect_claim: Forcing witnesses to describe uncertain facial details reduces their later identification accuracy.
effect_claim_quote: variation in response criterion significantly influenced not only the quality of the description generated but also accuracy on a subsequent identification task
replication_target_quote: The present study attempts to replicate this effect
outcome_quote: lower identification performance for participants forced to provide descriptive details
review_note: Computerized feature checklists did not show verbal overshadowing; the forced-description effect did.

original_title: Social contagion of memory
replication_title: The influence of schematic knowledge on contradictory versus additive misinformation: false memory for typical and atypical items
effect_name: Scene-consistent misinformation spreads false memories
effect_claim: Misleading scene items consistent with the scene schema produce more false memories than inconsistent items.
effect_claim_quote: this social contagion effect was greater when the scenes were presented for less time (15 sec) and when the intruded item was more schema consistent
replication_target_quote: The findings failed to replicate Roediger, Meade, and Bergman (2001)
outcome_quote: Participants reported greater false memory for schema‐inconsistent items than schema‐consistent items
review_note: Conceptual test used written narratives rather than confederate suggestions; the schema-direction finding reversed.

original_title: Semantic similarity and immediate serial recall: Is there an effect on all trials
replication_title: The effect of semantic relatedness on immediate serial recall and serial recognition
effect_name: Semantic relatedness aids immediate serial recall
effect_claim: Words from the same semantic category are recalled better in an immediate serial recall task.
effect_claim_quote: items from similar lists were better recalled on all the trials, including the first one
replication_target_quote: Replicating the findings of previous studies (e.g., Saint-Aubin, Ouellette, & Poirier, 2005)
outcome_quote: semantic relatedness boosted percentage serial recall
review_note: The later study also found increased order errors; it did not directly test the original all-trials claim.

original_title: Multiple-object tracking and visually guided touch
replication_title: Visually guided computer-mouse clicking interferes with multiple-object tracking (MOT)
effect_name: Touching tracked targets interferes less with multiple-object tracking
effect_claim: Actions toward tracked targets disrupt multiple-object tracking less than actions toward distractors.
effect_claim_quote: Touching distractors always reduced MOT performance more than touching targets
replication_target_quote: we attempted to replicate the finding using a different coordinated action: computer-mouse clicks
outcome_quote: Mouse-clicking also interfered differentially with MOT
review_note: Conceptual replication used computer-mouse clicks rather than direct touch.

original_title: Chinese subject-relative clauses are more difficult to process than the object-relative clauses
replication_title: Processing Chinese Relative Clauses: Evidence for the Subject-Relative Advantage
effect_name: Chinese object-relative clauses are easier to process
effect_claim: Chinese object-relative clauses are easier to comprehend than subject-relative clauses.
effect_claim_quote: the object-relative structure was easier to understand than the subject-relative structure
replication_target_quote: three self-paced reading experiments that attempted to replicate these results
outcome_quote: Two of our three studies found a subject-relative preference, and the third study found an object-relative advantage
review_note: One of three experiments reproduced the original direction; two found the opposite.

original_title: RCT of a Manualized Social Treatment for High-Functioning Autism Spectrum Disorders
original_journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
replication_title: Randomized Clinical Trial Replication of a Psychosocial Treatment for Children with High‐Functioning Autism Spectrum Disorders
effect_name: Manualized social treatment improves outcomes for children with HFASD
effect_claim: The manualized social treatment improves primary social outcomes for children with high-functioning autism spectrum disorders.
effect_claim_quote: Significant treatment effects were found for five of seven primary outcome measures
replication_target_quote: This replication randomized clinical trial examined the efficacy of a comprehensive psychosocial intervention
outcome_quote: Significant treatment effects were found for five of seven primary outcome measures
review_note: The later randomized trial used the same intervention components and replicated the five-of-seven primary-outcome result.

original_title: Emotion-based learning on a simplified card game: The Iowa and Bangor Gambling Tasks
replication_title: The Bangor Gambling Task: Computerized replication and reappraisal of an emotion-based decision task
effect_name: Bangor Gambling Task participants learn to avoid losing bets
effect_claim: In the Bangor Gambling Task, participants learn over time to reduce gambling as the chance of winning declines.
effect_claim_quote: participants showing a comparable pattern of incremental learning on both tasks
replication_target_quote: We explore BGT's replicability and analyze its probabilistic structure
outcome_quote: participants diminished their gambling probability throughout the task, learning to inhibit the initially rewarded gambling behavior
review_note: Computerized version replicated within-task learning; it did not retest the original correlation with Iowa Gambling Task scores.

original_title: Peer status and classroom seating arrangements: A social relations analysis
replication_title: The social implications of classroom seats: replicating and extending previous findings on seating arrangements and peer status
effect_name: Classroom seat proximity tracks peer liking and popularity
effect_claim: Classmates seated closer together rate one another as more likable and popular.
effect_claim_quote: classmates who sat closer together liked each other more and perceived each other as more popular
replication_target_quote: We aimed to replicate and extend the study by van den Berg and Cillessen (2015)
outcome_quote: classmates seated closer together concurrently rated each other as more popular and likeable
review_note: Preregistered replication; longitudinal proximity predicted mutual liking but not perceived popularity.

original_title: Neural correlates of attentional deployment within unpleasant pictures
replication_title: Behavioral and neuropsychological correlates of emotion regulation via attentional deployment: An expanded replication
effect_name: Non-arousing image focus reduces negative affect
effect_claim: Directing attention to non-arousing portions of unpleasant images reduces negative affect.
effect_claim_quote: participants felt significantly less negative affect after viewing unpleasant images with a non-arousing focus compared to unpleasant images with an arousing focus
replication_target_quote: we replicated and extended a previously introduced AD task
outcome_quote: We replicated the original AD effect in a new population sample, although we found a lower effect size
review_note: Replication moved the task from scanner to a regular laboratory and found a smaller effect.

original_title: I. Factor Analysis of Ufo-Related Attitudes
replication_title: Systematic Replication of Saunders' (1968) Attitude Factors
effect_name: UFO attitude survey yields a Philosophy of Science factor
effect_claim: Factor analysis of UFO-related attitude items identifies a Philosophy of Science factor.
effect_claim_quote: VI, Philosophy of Science
replication_target_quote: A replication of a factor analyzed questionnaire on science and UFOs was carried out
outcome_quote: the Philosophy of Science factor from the original study did not replicate
review_note: Later survey found ten factors, only two similar to original; this row concerns the explicitly named Philosophy of Science factor.

original_title: Carving personality description at its joints: Confirmation of three replicable personality prototypes for both children and adults
replication_title: The replicability and utility of three personality types
effect_name: Three personality prototypes recur across samples
effect_claim: The resilient, overcontrolled, and undercontrolled personality prototypes recur across adult samples.
effect_claim_quote: The results confirmed the hypothesis in all studies
replication_target_quote: The present research attempts to replicate these types in four large and diverse adult samples
outcome_quote: The failure of the three personality types to replicate in three of the four samples leads to the conclusion that they are not robust empirical entities
review_note: One of four adult samples met the stated standard; dimensions predicted outcomes better.

original_title: Infants rapidly learn word-referent mappings via cross-situational statistics
replication_title: Sequential Bayes Factor designs in developmental research: Studies on early word learning
effect_name: Infants learn word-object mappings across ambiguous scenes
effect_claim: Infants can learn novel word-object associations by aggregating cross-situational statistics.
effect_claim_quote: 12- and 14-month-old infants can resolve the uncertainty problem
replication_target_quote: their learning of novel word-object associations from cross-situational learning paradigms
outcome_quote: We did not replicate the findings of the cross-situational learning study
review_note: The sequential Bayes factor study found evidence favoring the null for the trained word-object associations.

original_title: Altered vision near the hands
replication_title: Situational Determinants of Hand-Proximity Effects
effect_name: Hand proximity slows shifts of visual attention
effect_claim: Holding hands near a visual display slows shifts of visual attention relative to hands held away.
effect_claim_quote: people shifted their attention between items more slowly when their hands were near the display
replication_target_quote: In our attempt to deconstruct the factors giving rise to the Hand-Proximity Effects (HPEs)
outcome_quote: In two experiments, we observed the absence of HPE
review_note: Visual search layouts were modified, so this is a boundary test rather than a literal repeat of the original three-task procedure.

original_title: The relationship between baseline pupil size and intelligence
replication_title: An examination of relations between baseline pupil measures and cognitive abilities
effect_name: Larger baseline pupils predict higher cognitive ability
effect_claim: People with higher fluid intelligence tend to have larger resting baseline pupils.
effect_claim_quote: it is fluid intelligence, more so than working memory capacity, which is related to baseline pupil size
replication_target_quote: The present study attempted to replicate such relations
outcome_quote: At the factor level, cognitive ability and pupil size correlated near zero
review_note: Three studies with N=845 failed to show the original positive association.

original_title: Mindfulness reduces habitual responding based on implicit knowledge: Evidence from artificial grammar learning

replication_title: Collective responsibility framing also leads to mitigation behavior in East Asia: a replication study in Taiwan
replication_target_quote: A recent study in Climatic Change by Obradovich and Guenther
outcome_quote: Participants in the collective and personal conditions donated significantly more than those in the control condition
review_note: Taiwan replication found both framing conditions raised donations versus control; personal framing lowered stated mitigation intent relative to collective/control.

effect_name: Two dimensions of perceived technological risk
effect_claim: Judgments of technological risk cluster into two dimensions that predict acceptable-risk tradeoffs.
effect_claim_quote: These nine attributes seemed to tap two basic dimensions of risk.
original_title: How safe is safe enough? A psychometric study of attitudes towards technological risks and benefits
replication_title: What makes risk acceptable? Revisiting the 1978 psychological dimensions of perceptions of technological risks
replication_target_quote: minimally modified replication of their 1978 study
outcome_quote: still explained by two factors: dread and uncertainty.
review_note: Risk ranking remained stable, while dread had a stronger influence in the newer US sample.

effect_name: Simple discrimination training produces equivalence classes
effect_claim: Simple discrimination training can produce emergent relations consistent with stimulus equivalence classes.
effect_claim_quote: In Experiment 2, all 4 participants showed patterns that are consistent with functional and equivalence class formation.
original_title: Transfer-of-Function and Novel Emergent Relations Using Simple Discrimination Training Procedures
replication_title: A Simpler Route to Stimulus Equivalence? A Replication and Further Exploration of a “Simple Discrimination Training Procedure” (Canovas, Debert and Pilgrim 2014)
replication_target_quote: Canovas, Debert and Pilgrim
outcome_quote: The present study starts with a successful replication of this seemingly new way of establishing stimulus equivalence classes
review_note: Replication directly targeted Experiment 2, then extended the procedure with nonword stimuli.

effect_name: Quantal step function in duration discrimination
effect_claim: With extensive practice, duration-discrimination thresholds form discrete steps rather than a smooth time function.
effect_claim_quote: steps unfold from the linear function, and these steps are clearly evident after 17 consecutive sessions
original_title: A quantal step function in duration discrimination
replication_title: On the replication of Kristofferson’s (1980) quantal timing for duration discrimination: some learning but no quanta and not much of a Weber constant
replication_target_quote: Kristofferson’s (Perception & Psychophysics 27:300–306, 1980)
outcome_quote: The data do not replicate Kristofferson’s (Perception & Psychophysics 27:300–306, 1980) quantal finding
review_note: Two new participants completed 260 sessions; modest learning occurred without the reported quantal steps.

effect_name: Self-compartmentalization in mood disorder
effect_claim: Remitted bipolar and recovered depressed patients organize positive and negative self-aspects more separately than healthy controls.
effect_claim_quote: The remitted bipolar and recovered depressed groups demonstrated greater compartmentalization than healthy controls
original_title: Self-Organization in Bipolar Disorder: Compartmentalization and Self-Complexity
replication_title: Self-Organization in Bipolar Disorder: Replication of Compartmentalization and Self-Complexity
replication_target_quote: Similar to the findings of Taylor et al.
outcome_quote: the bipolar and unipolar groups showed higher levels of self compartmentalization than healthy controls.
review_note: The specific compartmentalization result recurred; the original self-complexity difference did not.

effect_name: Implicit memory for unattended speech
effect_claim: Words heard in an unattended speech channel can leave an implicit memory trace without explicit recognition.
effect_claim_quote: recognition and spelling of previously unattended homophones, suggest an affirmative answer
original_title: Memory for unattended events: Remembering with and without awareness
replication_title: Is there implicit memory without attention? A reexamination of task demands in Eich’s (1984) procedure
replication_target_quote: Eich (1984) made an important discovery of implicit but not explicit memory
outcome_quote: With a direct replication of Eich's timing parameters, we reproduced his results, but when the attended channel was presented twice as fast as Eich's, implicit memory for the to-be-ignored words vanished.
review_note: Outcome quote is in the exact-DOI Europe PMC abstract, although discovery cached it under fulltext; the effect was sensitive to shadowing rate.

effect_name: Type A behavior and shorter sleep
effect_claim: Shorter habitual sleep is associated with higher self-reported Type A behavior among college students.
effect_claim_quote: an inverse relationship between normal habitual sleep duration and level of Type A behavior.
original_title: Type A behavior and normal habitual sleep duration
replication_title: Sleep Duration and Self-Reported Type A Behavior: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Replicating a previous report (Hicks et al., 1979)
outcome_quote: subjects who slept fewer hours scored higher on Type A behavior questions than those who slept more hours. However, for subjects with a less stable sleeping pattern, Type A scores for the two groups (ns = 72, 23) did not differ.
review_note: The association appeared among regular sleepers and disappeared among less stable sleepers.

effect_name: Family members most impress gifted youth
effect_claim: Gifted youth most often name family members as the people who impress them most.
effect_claim_quote: The most frequently chosen category of individuals was family members (44.8%)
original_title: Persons Who Most Impress Gifted Youth
replication_title: Persons Who Most Impress Gifted Youth: A Replication
replication_target_quote: A replication of a study of the persons who most impressed gifted youth was conducted with 95 students
outcome_quote: Consistent with the 1982 study by Karnes and Lee, most impressive to these students were family members and least impressive moral and religious personalities.
review_note: The 1994 study repeats the 1982 question and explicitly reports the same most frequent category.

effect_name: Partial phonological marking facilitates noun-class learning
effect_claim: Shared phonological endings facilitate learning otherwise arbitrary noun classes.
effect_claim_quote: Many adult subjects learning the experimental language acquired the word classes while no one learning the control language did.
original_title: Acquisition of Gender-like Noun Subclasses in an Artificial Language: The Contribution of Phonological Markers to Learning
replication_title: PARTIAL PHONOLOGICAL MARKING FACILITATES THE ACQUISITION OF NOUN SUBCLASSES: A REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: This is a partial replication of Brooks, Braine, Catalano, Brody, and Sudhalter (1993).
outcome_quote: The experimental group was markedly superior to the control.
review_note: The later study names the 1993 study, uses marked versus unmarked noun classes, and reports the same direction.

effect_name: A smile increases pedestrians’ responsiveness
effect_claim: A confederate looking and smiling elicits more pedestrians’ responsive glances and social gestures than looking alone or avoiding.
effect_claim_quote: the look and smile condition produced higher levels of smiling, nodding, and greetings than did the other two conditions.
original_title: Passing Encounters: Patterns of Recognition and Avoidance in Pedestrians
replication_title: Through a Glass Darkly: Effects of Smiling and Visibility on Recognition and Avoidance in Passing Encounters
replication_target_quote: The first purpose of the study was to replicate the results of an earlier experiment (Patterson, Webb, & Schwartz, 2002
outcome_quote: more glances, smiles, and nods in the look and smile condition than in the avoid and look‐only conditions.
review_note: The later paper names the original 2002 pedestrian study and repeats its smile condition and response measures.

effect_name: Marital distress and MMPI Mf score difference
effect_claim: Couples with husbands scoring at least 20 MMPI Mf T-score points above their wives enter group psychotherapy with more distress.
effect_claim_quote: couples in whom the husband scores 20 or more T-score points higher than his wife on the Mf scale of the MMPI come into group psychotherapy with significantly more distress
original_title: An MMPI Index of Disturbed Marital Interaction
replication_title: The Mf Scale as an Index of Disturbed Marital Interaction: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Osborne (1971) found that couples in group psychotherapy in whom the husband scored 20 or more T score points higher than his wife
outcome_quote: there does not appear to be any evidence to support Osborne's assumption that couples with a high Mf index were experiencing more distress
review_note: The later paper explicitly remeasured Osborne's Mf index and rejects the original distress finding.

effect_name: Anxiety and negative future events
effect_claim: Anxiety is associated with generating more negative future experiences.
effect_claim_quote: Anxiety was associated with generating more negative experiences but not fewer positive experiences
original_title: Retrospective and Prospective Cognitions in Anxiety and Depression
replication_title: Prospective cognitions in anxiety and depression: Replication and methodological extension
replication_target_quote: replication and methodological extension of MacLeod, Tata, Kentish, and Jacobsen (1997)
outcome_quote: only anxiety (but not depression) was related to enhanced imagery for future negative events
review_note: The replication names MacLeod et al. and tests the anxiety-negative future cognition result.

effect_name: Power priming reduces temporal discounting
effect_claim: Priming a sense of power reduces temporal discounting.
effect_claim_quote: priming power reduced temporal discounting in monetary and nonmonetary tasks
original_title: Power and Reduced Temporal Discounting
replication_title: Does Power Increase Self-Control? Episodic Priming May Not Provide the Answer
replication_target_quote: pre-registered direct replication of the only experiment testing the effects of power on self-control (Joshi & Fast, 2013, Study 3)
outcome_quote: social power, operationalized by episodic priming, did not affect temporal discounting
review_note: Study 3 is specifically named and its priming-discounting result is tested.

effect_name: Conditional-only receptive labeling instruction
effect_claim: Conditional-only instruction teaches receptive labeling more efficiently than simple-conditional instruction for children with autism.
effect_claim_quote: the conditional-only method was a more reliable and efficient teaching procedure
original_title: A COMPARISON OF METHODS FOR TEACHING RECEPTIVE LABELING TO CHILDREN WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDERS
replication_title: A comparison of methods for teaching receptive labeling to children with autism spectrum disorders: A systematic replication
replication_target_quote: The current study systematically replicated the earlier study by comparing the 2 approaches
outcome_quote: the conditional-only method was a more efficient and reliable teaching procedure than the simple-conditional method
review_note: Both studies contrast the same two receptive-labeling methods in children with autism.

effect_name: Suboptimal affective priming
effect_claim: Brief affective primes shift judgments of later neutral stimuli even without conscious recognition.
effect_claim_quote: At suboptimal exposures only affective primes produced significant shifts in Ss' judgments of novel stimuli.
original_title: Affect, cognition, and awareness: Affective priming with optimal and suboptimal stimulus exposures.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Is Affective Priming Possible?
replication_target_quote: This study is a replication of Murphy and Zajonc (1993)
outcome_quote: No affective priming effect was found either when there was no recognition of the affective prime above chance or when recognition was significantly above chance.
review_note: The later study names Murphy and Zajonc and tests masked affective faces on liking judgments.

effect_name: Nearby hands improve change detection
effect_claim: Placing both hands near the display improves change detection accuracy.
effect_claim_quote: When their hands were near the display, change detection performance was more accurate
original_title: Improved change detection with nearby hands
replication_title: Hand proximity effects are fragile: a useful null result
replication_target_quote: A third experiment attempted to replicate the near-hands advantage in a change detection paradigm featuring simple stimuli (Tseng and Bridgeman
outcome_quote: Still, no near-hands advantage was observed.
review_note: The later paper explicitly names Tseng and Bridgeman and reports null results for near-hands change detection.

effect_name: Older and male patients receive higher pain ratings and more help
effect_claim: Observers rate older and male patients as in greater pain and offer them more help than younger and female patients.
effect_claim_quote: older and male patients were offered more help and were perceived as being in more intense pain than younger and female patients
original_title: Pain evaluation and prosocial behaviour are affected by age and sex
replication_title: Reproducing age and sex biases in perceived pain intensity and prosocial behaviors using digital characters
replication_target_quote: One study by Gingras et al. (2021) investigated how these characteristics affect the first (perception) and last (help) stages
outcome_quote: The findings replicated those of Gingras et al. (2021) with the addition of an age by sex interaction
review_note: The later study names Gingras et al. and tests the same patient age and sex bias with digital stimuli.

effect_name: Overinvolved parents and male self-defeating traits
effect_claim: Among men, recalled parental overinvolvement is positively associated with self-defeating personality traits.
effect_claim_quote: The latter scores correlated positively with memories of both overinvolved mother and father for men
original_title: Self-Defeating Personality and Memories of Parents' Child-Rearing Behaviour
replication_title: Self-Defeating Personality and Memories of Parents' Child-Rearing Behaviour: A Replication
replication_target_quote: A recent study of correlations of self-defeating personality and memories of parents' child-rearing behaviour has been replicated
outcome_quote: Memories of an overinvolved parent were significantly correlated with self-defeating personality scores only among men
review_note: The same parental overinvolvement and men-only association recurs in a larger sample.

effect_name: Psychotherapy approaches have equivalent outcomes
effect_claim: CBT, person-centred and psychodynamic therapies in NHS routine practice show broadly equivalent outcomes.
effect_claim_quote: theoretically different approaches tend to have equivalent outcomes
original_title: Effectiveness of cognitive-behavioural, person-centred and psychodynamic therapies as practised in UK National Health Service settings
replication_title: Effectiveness of cognitive-behavioural, person-centred, and psychodynamic therapies in UK primary-care routine practice: replication in a larger sample
replication_target_quote: We replicated an earlier comparison of treatment approaches in a sample four times larger
outcome_quote: Replicating the earlier results, the theoretically different approaches tended to have equivalent outcomes.
review_note: The later NHS study repeats the same three therapy approaches and outcome comparison in a larger sample.

effect_name: Irrelevance can cause color blindness under low load
effect_claim: An irrelevant color is often forgotten even when perceptual resources are available.
effect_claim_quote: up to a quarter of the participants could not name the color of the irrelevant stimulus
original_title: Blinded by irrelevance: Pure irrelevance induced “blindness”.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
replication_title: A Novel Test of Pure Irrelevance-Induced Blindness
replication_target_quote: a recent one-trial study showed that under low load, with only two colors in the display - a ring and a disk -
outcome_quote: the results only partly replicated prior findings. In particular, there was no evidence of irrelevance-induced blindness under conditions in which a ring was designated as relevant
review_note: The ring-relevant condition failed; the authors’ cumulative analysis retained some irrelevance effect across studies.

effect_name: Untrustworthy faces are remembered better
effect_claim: Faces judged untrustworthy are recognized more accurately than trustworthy faces after a delay.
effect_claim_quote: after one week untrustworthy faces were better recognized than trustworthy faces
original_title: Behavioral and neural evidence of enhanced long-term memory for untrustworthy faces
replication_title: Memory advantage for untrustworthy faces: Replication across lab- and web-based studies
replication_target_quote: This study tested the validity of a web-based episodic memory paradigm by comparing participants' memory performance for trustworthy and untrustworthy facial stimuli
outcome_quote: Consistent with previous results, we observed enhanced episodic memory for untrustworthy compared to trustworthy faces.
review_note: The later study reproduced the behavioral memory advantage in both web and laboratory settings; no neural claim is coded.

effect_name: Unexpected local events boost lottery gambling
effect_claim: Unexpectedly sunny days or positive local sports outcomes are followed by increased lottery gambling.
effect_claim_quote: When local sports teams performed better than expected, or a sunny day followed a streak of cloudy days, residents gambled more.
original_title: Unexpected but Incidental Positive Outcomes Predict Real-World Gambling
replication_title: The Relationship Between Unexpected Outcomes and Lottery Gambling Rates in a Large Canadian Metropolitan Area
replication_target_quote: we examined whether city residents gamble more when local outcomes are better than expected
outcome_quote: We found that unexpectedly sunny days predict increased rates of fixed-prize lottery gambling. The number of local sports team wins also predicted increased purchase rates of fixed-prize lottery, but unexpected positive outcomes in sports did not.
review_note: Toronto data reproduced the unexpected-sunshine association, but not the unexpected-sports-outcome component of the New York result.

effect_name: Defensive responding masks distress–memory correlation
effect_claim: A defensive MMPI response style attenuates the negative association between self-reported distress and cognitive performance.
effect_claim_quote: increased emotional distress was reliably associated with decreased cognitive functioning ( rs = −.22 to −.27) among the nondefensive group, but was unrelated in the defensive group
original_title: The Impact of a Defensive Response Set on the Relationship Between MMPI and Cognitive Tests Among Heart Transplant Candidates
replication_title: A Defensive Response Set and the Relation between Cognitive and Emotional Functioning: A Replication
replication_target_quote: This study was designed to examine the hypothesis that a defensive self-report response set tends to attenuate the strength of the relationship
outcome_quote: increases on Scales 2 and 7 were significantly associated with decreased functioning of verbal memory (r = -.35 and -.34, respectively) among the nondefensive group but were unrelated in the defensive group.
review_note: Replication in lung transplant candidates extends the original cardiac transplant sample.

effect_name: Credible messages raise self-esteem
effect_claim: A credible counter-attitudinal message raises self-esteem in college students with low initial self-esteem.
effect_claim_quote: demonstrated significant positive changes in esteem for Ss exposed to the high credibility communication
original_title: An experimental study of the effectiveness of attitude change techniques for enhancing self-esteem
replication_title: Modification of Self-Esteem with Techniques of Attitude Change: A Replication
replication_target_quote: The present study was intended to replicate and extend that initial effort.
outcome_quote: Results supported the earlier findings that levels of esteem could be raised by exposing subjects to appropriate messages under conditions of high credibility.
review_note: Same authors replicated the high-credibility message intervention in a larger college sample.

effect_name: High IQ protects against delinquency
effect_claim: Among people at high risk of criminal behavior, high IQ is associated with avoiding serious offending.
effect_claim_quote: the first group evidenced a mean IQ score that was significantly higher than that of the other risk groups
original_title: IQ as a protective factor for subjects at high risk for antisocial behavior.
original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_title: A prospective replication of the protective effects of IQ in subjects at high risk for juvenile delinquency.
replication_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_target_quote: The purpose of the study was to test the replicability of a protective effect of high IQ against criminality.
outcome_quote: a very high IQ may help boys, even those at risk, to stay free of delinquency altogether.
review_note: Prospective New Zealand cohort supports a protective pattern specifically in boys; age, outcome and cohort differ from original.

effect_name: Pairs training effect in face matching
effect_claim: Low-accuracy viewers improve subsequent individual unfamiliar-face matching after working in a pair.
effect_claim_quote: working in a pair can lead to subsequent improvements in individual performance, specifically for viewers whose accuracy is initially low
original_title: Unfamiliar face matching: Pairs out‐perform individuals and provide a route to training
replication_title: The pairs training effect in unfamiliar face matching
replication_target_quote: Here, we sought to replicate the original finding
outcome_quote: In two experiments, we replicated the pairs training effect
review_note: Replicates the training benefit specifically, rather than the separate simultaneous pairs advantage.

effect_name: Social-label transfer in resource allocation
effect_claim: Giving one member of an equivalence class a positive or negative social label changes resource allocations across the class.
effect_claim_quote: marked differences occurred in the distribution depending on whether YIM was described as a “Good” or a “Bad” person.
original_title: The Effects of Social Labels on the Allocation of Resources to Equivalent Stimuli: Does One Rotten Apple Spoil the Whole Barrel?
replication_title: The Effects of Social Labels on the Allocation of Resources among Equivalent Stimuli: An Extended Replication
replication_target_quote: Two experiments measured the effects of adding a social label to one of the stimuli in an equivalence class
outcome_quote: Results showed that the label that was assigned influenced the distribution of tokens.
review_note: Extended replication uses the same social-label and equivalent-stimulus token allocation design.

effect_name: Sferics and ESP correlation
effect_claim: Higher natural atmospheric sferics activity correlates with lower scores on a forced-choice ESP task.
effect_claim_quote: a negative correlation between ESP performance and sferics activity around the time of the session
original_title: Geophysical Variables and Behavior: LXXXVIII. Atmospheric Electromagnetism: The Possible Disturbing Influence of Natural Sferics on ESP
replication_title: Atmospheric Electromagnetism: Attempted Replication of the Correlation between Natural Sferics and ESP
replication_target_quote: In a previous study a negative correlation was found between the natural sferics activity and scores on an ESP task.
outcome_quote: In these studies ESP scores and the level of sferics activity were not significantly correlated.
review_note: Three attempted replications individually found no significant correlation; combined estimate was significant but small.

effect_name: Leisure-item preference in dementia
effect_claim: Adults with dementia preferentially select leisure items over edible items in preference assessments.
effect_claim_quote: all participants showed a noticeable preference for leisure items over edible items
original_title: ASSESSMENT OF PREFERENCE FOR EDIBLE AND LEISURE ITEMS IN INDIVIDUALS WITH DEMENTIA
replication_title: Preference for leisure items over edible items in individuals with dementia: A replication
replication_target_quote: We replicated previous research in which adults with dementia tended to show a preference for leisure items over edible items
outcome_quote: The most highly preferred stimulus for 6 out of 7 participants was a leisure item
review_note: Both studies test leisure versus edible preferences in adults with dementia.

effect_name: Self-help bestseller words rated more relevant
effect_claim: Words from bestselling self-help psychology books receive higher self-help relevance ratings than words from nonbestselling books.
effect_claim_quote: the ratings for relevance of words from the two bestselling books were higher than the ratings for the words from the two nonbestselling books.
original_title: Rated Relevance of Words in Self-Help Psychology Books
replication_title: A Replication of Rated Relevance of Self-Help Words from Psychology Books
replication_target_quote: 44 men and 47 women rated 128 high frequency words from self-help psychology books similarly for relevance to self-help behaviour.
outcome_quote: words from best-selling books generally were rated higher.
