review_note: The same author replicates the same word-rating task and bestseller contrast.

effect_name: Honest interview statements are longer and more detailed
effect_claim: Honest witnesses give longer and more detailed statements than deceptive witnesses in the ACID interview procedure.
effect_claim_quote: Honest responses were longer, more detailed, and contained more admissions of potential mistakes.
original_title: Assessment Criteria Indicative of Deception (ACID): an integrated system of investigative interviewing and detecting deception
original_journal: Journal of Investigative Psychology and Offender Profiling
replication_title: Assessment Criteria Indicative of Deception (ACID): Replication and Gender Differences
replication_target_quote: The first goal was to replicate ACID with a population of incarcerated witnesses.
outcome_quote: this study demonstrated honest statements were longer and more detailed than deceptive statements
review_note: The later ACID study repeats the honest-versus-deceptive statement comparison with incarcerated witnesses.

effect_name: Loss incentives improve high-load working memory
effect_claim: Loss incentives improve working-memory task performance relative to gain incentives at the highest task load.
effect_claim_quote: In Experiment 3, losses did enhance working memory performance, but only at the highest load level.
original_title: Losses Motivate Cognitive Effort More Than Gains in Effort-Based Decision Making and Performance
replication_title: Limited evidence for enhanced working memory performance and effort allocation in the face of loss versus gain incentives: A preregistered (non) replication
replication_target_quote: In a recent study, we found evidence that losses motivated better working memory performance than gains.
outcome_quote: losses did not enhance working memory performance, relative to gains, at any N-Back level.
review_note: Preregistered higher-powered N-back study failed to reproduce the high-load performance advantage; participants still reported more effort under losses.

effect_name: Nemours BrightStart improves emergent literacy
effect_claim: The Nemours BrightStart small-group program improves early literacy skills among at-risk preschoolers.
effect_claim_quote: Significantly accelerated growth in print knowledge, elision, rhyming, and the screener was observed during intervention.
original_title: Efficacy of the Nemours BrightStart! Early Literacy Program: Treatment Outcomes From a Randomized Trial With At-Risk Prekindergartners
replication_title: Small-Group, Emergent Literacy Intervention Under Two Implementation Models: Intent-to-Treat and Dosage Effects for Preschoolers at Risk for Reading Difficulties
replication_target_quote: we examined the effects of the Nemours BrightStart! (NBS!) intervention
outcome_quote: Intent-to-treat analyses showed no significant impacts of NBS! on any outcome
review_note: Routine teacher/community-aide implementation did not reproduce effects from the controlled efficacy trial; one letter-writing effect appeared only in as-treated analysis.

effect_name: Emotion understanding and peer action coordination
effect_claim: Children with higher emotion understanding coordinate actions with peers more successfully in a cooperative sensorimotor task.
effect_claim_quote: higher levels of emotion understanding significantly explained greater peer action coordination
original_title: Emotions in motion: impact of emotion understanding on children’s peer action coordination
replication_title: Peer Action Coordination in Middle Childhood: A Replication Null Finding on Emotion Understanding and Inhibitory Control
replication_target_quote: This study replicates and extends a previous study by examining whether emotion understanding and inhibitory control correlate with children’s peer action coordination
outcome_quote: there was no direct association between emotion understanding or inhibitory control and children’s peer action coordination
review_note: Same Test of Emotion Comprehension and cooperative sensorimotor task; no direct association after matching controls.

effect_name: Temporal-lobe signs and paranormal reports
effect_claim: People who report more types of paranormal experiences also report more temporal-lobe signs.
effect_claim_quote: people who reported greater numbers of different types of paranormal experiences also reported greater numbers of temporal lobe signs
original_title: Propensity to Report Paranormal Experiences is Correlated with Temporal Lobe Signs
replication_title: Temporal Lobe Signs and Reports of Subjective Paranormal Experiences in a Normal Population: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Correlations (r = 0.50) were found between the numbers of different psi (paranormal) experiences
outcome_quote: Correlations (r = 0.50) were found between the numbers of different psi (paranormal) experiences and the numbers of temporal lobe signs
review_note: Same author and survey association in an independent university sample; claim is about self-reports, not evidence of paranormal events or the proposed neural mechanism.

effect_name: Early number-conservation performance
effect_claim: Very young children can discriminate the relative number of objects in aligned arrays, with a nonmonotonic age pattern when arrays differ in length.
effect_claim_quote: between 3 years, 2 months and 4 years, 6 months they indicate a longer row with fewer objects to have "more"
original_title: Cognitive Capacity of Very Young Children
replication_title: Cognitive Capacities of Young Children: A Replication
replication_target_quote: The Mehler and Bever assertion that very young children conserve the concept of number
outcome_quote: with a decline and rise in performance, is not confirmed.
review_note: Science replication explicitly names the original authors and rejects the proposed decline-and-rise age pattern.

effect_name: Individual versus shared puzzle choice
effect_claim: When given the choice, most participants work on their own puzzle rather than a peer’s puzzle under social exchange conditions.
effect_claim_quote: most subjects chose to solve the puzzle individually
original_title: A Comparison of Choice Between Individual and Shared Social Contingencies in Children and Young Adults
replication_title: Choice between individual and shared social contingencies in children: An experimental replication in a natural setting
replication_target_quote: preference for individual versus social contingencies under different social exchange conditions
outcome_quote: most subjects chose to solve the puzzle individually, even when they obtained less earnings.
review_note: Same authors and puzzle choice task, replicated in a natural setting with children.

effect_name: Rape salience, rape myths, and self-esteem
effect_claim: Making rape salient lowers self-esteem among women with low rape myth acceptance, while high acceptance moderates that response.
effect_claim_quote: When rape was salient, low-RMA women showed a decrease in that aspect of SE
original_title: Salience of Rape Affects Self-Esteem: Individual versus Collective Self-Aspects
replication_title: Expecting to Meet a Rape Victim Affects Women’s Self-Esteem: The Moderating Role of Rape Myth Acceptance
replication_target_quote: Conceptually replicating previous studies where rape salience was operationalized by presenting newspaper articles
outcome_quote: low-RMA women reported lower self-esteem in the rape condition than in the studying condition, whereas high-RMA participants showed an opposite effect.
review_note: Same authors and rape-myth-acceptance moderator; replication changed salience induction to an expected meeting with a victim.

effect_name: Trauma history moderates estradiol–PTSD association
effect_claim: Sexual trauma history moderates the association between estradiol and trauma-related symptom severity.
effect_claim_quote: Estradiol at the time of the interview was inversely associated with symptoms in women with sexual but not nonsexual trauma
original_title: Trauma Characteristics Moderate the Relation Between Estradiol and Trauma‐Related Symptoms
replication_title: Trauma-related moderators of associations between sex hormones and PTSD symptoms: a replication-extension
replication_target_quote: a prior study that identified trauma characteristics (sexual trauma and age at trauma) as moderators of associations between estradiol and PTSD symptoms
outcome_quote: no moderation effects by sexual trauma or age at trauma for estradiol.
review_note: Replication explicitly identifies the original moderator pattern and finds no estradiol interaction.

effect_name: ASL activation during English word recognition
effect_claim: ASL phonological forms are activated when deaf ASL–English bilinguals judge English word pairs.
effect_claim_quote: ASL signs are engaged during English print word recognition
original_title: Bilingual word recognition in deaf and hearing signers: Effects of proficiency and language dominance on cross-language activation
replication_title: The time course of cross-language activation in deaf ASL–English bilinguals
replication_target_quote: We replicated prior findings of cross-language activation
outcome_quote: We replicated prior findings of cross-language activation despite the introduction of a much faster rate of presentation.
review_note: Same lead author, English-word-pair task, ASL translation manipulation, and deaf bilingual group.

effect_name: Delayed substance initiation mediates prevention effects
effect_claim: Middle-school family prevention programs lower young-adult substance misuse partly by delaying initiation during adolescence.
effect_claim_quote: long-term effects were primarily indirect
original_title: Universal intervention effects on substance use among young adults mediated by delayed adolescent substance initiation.
original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_title: Replication RCT of early universal prevention effects on young adult substance misuse.
replication_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_target_quote: We replicated and extended an earlier study examining whether delayed substance initiation during adolescence
outcome_quote: significant indirect intervention effects on the average levels of all young adult outcomes
review_note: Same lead author and Iowa school prevention program; later trial replicated the indirect pathway across four young-adult substance outcomes.

effect_name: CBD expectancy increases sedation
effect_claim: Being told that CBD-free oil contains CBD increases subjective sedation after ingestion.
effect_claim_quote: The CBD expectancy condition was associated with increased sedation
original_title: Evaluating cannabidiol (CBD) expectancy effects on acute stress and anxiety in healthy adults: a randomized crossover study
replication_title: The impact of cannabidiol placebo on responses to an acute stressor: A replication and proof of concept study
replication_target_quote: Our group has previously reported that cannabidiol (CBD) expectancy alone blunts markers of stress
outcome_quote: CBD expectancy was associated with increased subjective sedation
review_note: The later primary full text explicitly cites Spinella et al. (2021); it repeats CBD-free oil expectancy and subjective sedation.

effect_name: Jewish cultural group and psychological differentiation
effect_claim: In the original sample, Jewish boys scored as less psychologically differentiated than matched Anglo-Saxon Protestant boys.
effect_claim_quote: les enfants juifs (garçons) montrent proportionnellement moins de différenciation que les enfants anglo‐saxons
original_title: JEWISH SUBCULTURAL PATTERNS AND PSYCHOLOGICAL DIFFERENTIATION1
replication_title: Jewish Culture and Psychological Differentiation—Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: Traditional-Jewish Ss, in comparison with Anglo-Saxon Protestant Ss, matched for age and verbal ability, will be more global
outcome_quote: The first hypothesis was confirmed with regard to Embedded Figures (p less than .05), but not with regard to the other two criterion measures.
review_note: The same author retested the same group contrast and three differentiation measures; only one measure supported it.

effect_name: Human figures reduce occlusion effect in women
effect_claim: For women, occlusion had a smaller effect during mental rotation of human figures than during rotation of block figures.
effect_claim_quote: for women, the effect of occlusion was decreased when mentally rotating human figures.
original_title: Bodies and occlusion: Item types, cognitive processes, and gender differences in mental rotation
replication_title: Photographs of real human figures: Item types and persistent sex differences in mental rotation
replication_target_quote: the human figures MRT used in Doyle and Voyer's 2013 study
outcome_quote: The three-way interaction between test, sex, and occlusion reported in Doyle and Voyer's 2013 study was not replicated
review_note: Same authors and tests; the original DOI has 2013 publication year in Crossref despite candidate cache year 2012.

effect_name: Crossover in stuttering attitude scores
effect_claim: In POSHA-S retests, respondents with the least positive initial stuttering attitudes improve most while those with the most positive initial attitudes worsen.
effect_claim_quote: Respondents with the least positive pre attitudes improved greatly, and respondents with the most positive attitudes worsened greatly.
original_title: Profiles of public attitude change regarding stuttering
replication_title: Intervention to Improve Attitudes Toward Stuttering: A Multi-Site International Replication and Expansion
replication_target_quote: replicate an extreme case of regression to the mean (i.e., “crossover” effect) reported earlier in larger combined samples
outcome_quote: The “crossover” effect was replicated
review_note: The later primary MDPI article references the matched St. Louis et al. 2024 aggregate study and tests its same POSHA-S crossover effect in fresh samples.

effect_name: Bedtime pass reduces bedtime resistance
effect_claim: A bedtime pass reduces crying and leaving the bedroom after bedtime in young children.
effect_claim_quote: Crying and coming out from the bedroom reduced to zero rates in both children.
original_title: The Bedtime Pass
original_journal: Archives of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine
replication_title: TREATING BEDTIME RESISTANCE WITH THE BEDTIME PASS: A SYSTEMATIC REPLICATION AND COMPONENT ANALYSIS WITH 3‐YEAR‐OLDS
replication_target_quote: treated with the bedtime pass (i.e., provision of a small notecard exchangeable for one trip out of the bedroom after bedtime) plus extinction
outcome_quote: Bedtime resistance was eliminated for all participants.
review_note: The later primary full text explicitly says it systematically replicated Friman et al. (1999) and used the same bedtime-pass intervention.

effect_name: Ostracism increases desire for solitude
effect_claim: Ostracized people show increased desire to be alone after social exclusion.
effect_claim_quote: three experiments (Studies 2–4) demonstrated that manipulated ostracism experience increases the desire to be alone in a subsequent activity
original_title: Evidence for Another Response to Ostracism
replication_title: Seeking Solitude After Being Ostracized: A Replication and Beyond
replication_target_quote: we conceptually replicated the original paper in three studies
outcome_quote: being ostracized increased participants’ desires for solitude (Studies 2 and 3)
review_note: Exact original citation Ren et al. 2016 appears in the replication full text at PMC7897794. The main solitude-seeking effect replicated; extraversion moderation did not.

effect_name: Minority dissenter causes delayed behavioral conversion
effect_claim: Seeing an accomplice break an initial compliance commitment reduces willingness to make a later commitment, without immediate imitation.
effect_claim_quote: simply observing someone (an accomplice) break his or her own initial agreement to abstain from smoking for 18 hours was enough to bring about a substantial reduction
original_title: When a compliance without pressure strategy fails due to a minority dissenter: A case of “behavioral conversion”
replication_title: Behavioural conversion in a compliance paradigm: A replication and a refinement
replication_target_quote: simply observing an accomplice break his commitment to forego lunch was enough to produce a significant reduction
outcome_quote: This pattern of influence, similar to a ‘behavioural conversion’, appeared if the accomplice had first agreed to the initial request and only later refused to continue
review_note: Same original and replication authors Joule and Mugny; same uncommon delayed minority-dissenter compliance paradigm, with smoking abstinence changed to meal abstinence.

effect_name: Reading program generalizes to untrained words
effect_claim: A matching and word-construction program teaches reading of trained words and enables reading of new, generalized words.
effect_claim_quote: Five children also read generalization words and showed progress in spelling.
original_title: TEACHING READING AND SPELLING: EXCLUSION AND STIMULUS EQUIVALENCE
replication_title: READING, EQUIVALENCE, AND RECOMBINATION OF UNITS: A REPLICATION WITH STUDENTS WITH DIFFERENT LEARNING HISTORIES
replication_target_quote: First graders, preschoolers, special education students, and adults received a reading program in which they learned to match printed to dictated words and to construct (copy) printed words.
outcome_quote: most of the students learned to read new words that involved recombinations of the syllables of the training words.
review_note: The later primary PMC record explicitly cites DOI 10.1901/jaba.1996.29-451. It repeats printed-to-dictated matching plus word construction and reports generalization to new recombined words.

effect_name: Age-related positivity in picture memory
effect_claim: With older age, negative pictures are recalled less often relative to positive and neutral pictures.
effect_claim_quote: The relative number of negative images compared with positive and neutral images recalled decreased with each successively older age group.
original_title: Aging and emotional memory: The forgettable nature of negative images for older adults.
replication_title: Replicating the positivity effect in picture memory in Koreans: Evidence for cross-cultural generalizability.
replication_target_quote: This study examined whether a relative preference for positive over negative material is also observed in older Koreans.
outcome_quote: the relative preference for positive over negative material in memory observed in older Koreans was indistinguishable from that observed previously in older Americans.
review_note: The later primary PMC full text directly compares its Korean IAPS picture-memory data with the matched Charles et al. (2003) American sample and cites that original study.

effect_name: Word-level uncertainty during reading
effect_claim: Readers can retain uncertainty about a previously seen word and use later sentence context to revise its identity.
effect_claim_quote: readers maintain uncertain beliefs about previously read word identities
original_title: Eye movement evidence that readers maintain and act on uncertainty about past linguistic input
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: No evidence of word-level uncertainty in younger and older adults in self-paced reading
replication_target_quote: This design replicated that of an earlier study conducted by Levy et al. (2009)
outcome_quote: there was no evidence that either younger or older adults maintained uncertainty about the identity of the perceptually confusable preposition
review_note: Exact Levy et al. 2009 design and confusable-preposition effect, tested with self-paced reading rather than eye movements; absence may reflect paradigm change.

effect_name: Consonant-vowel recall difference across languages
effect_claim: English speakers recall vowel-varying syllable sequences better than consonant-varying sequences, whereas Arabic speakers do not show this vowel advantage.
effect_claim_quote: Native speakers of English recalled the vowel series better than consonant series in English and in Arabic, which was not true of native Arabic speakers.
original_title: Cross-linguistic differences in the immediate serial recall of consonants versus vowels
replication_title: Templaticity Effects on Differential Processing of Consonants and Vowels
replication_journal: Laboratory Phonology Journal of the Association for Laboratory Phonology
replication_target_quote: replicating findings from Kissling (2012).
outcome_quote: Arabic speakers remembered both types of sequences equally well
review_note: Replication names Kissling (2012), the 2012 print issue of the original article (published online in 2011), and reproduces the English-Arabic immediate-serial-recall contrast.

effect_name: Aerobic fitness and heart-rate recovery
effect_claim: Greater aerobic fitness predicts faster tonic heart-rate recovery after psychosocial stressors.
effect_claim_quote: Aerobic power was found to be significantly (p < .001) related to how quickly subjects recovered from stress.
original_title: Aerobic Power and Tonic Heart Rate Responses to Psychosocial Stressors
replication_title: Aerobic Fitness and Emotional Arousal: A Critical Attempt at Replication
replication_target_quote: This study was an attempt to replicate the findings of earlier research in which conclusions were based on a questionable interpretation of statistical results.
outcome_quote: did not confirm, as had been previously reported, greater heart-rate recovery for 20 aerobically fit subjects as opposed to 20 unfit subjects following psychosocial stress.
review_note: A published 1982 reply by Zimmerman and Fulton explicitly identifies their 1981 paper as an attempt to replicate Cox, Evans and Jamieson (1979) and cites the matched original title/DOI.

effect_name: TOMM resistance to genuine memory impairment
effect_claim: The Test of Memory Malingering can distinguish suboptimal effort while most patients with genuine cognitive impairment score above its Trial 2 cutoff.
effect_claim_quote: The results from all 4 experiments show that the TOMM is relatively insensitive to genuine memory impairment
original_title: The Test of Memory Malingering (TOMM): Normative data from cognitively intact and cognitively impaired individuals.
replication_title: Replication of the Test of Memory Malingering (TOMM) in a Traumatic Brain Injury and Head Trauma Sample
replication_target_quote: The purpose of the current study was to replicate the clinical validation study of the Test of Memory Malingering
outcome_quote: Results replicated and expanded those found by Tombaugh
review_note: Replication explicitly cites Tombaugh (1997) title and validates the same TOMM Trial 2 cutoff in traumatic brain injury. Original full abstract recovered from the original article publisher preview mirrored by ResearchGate/EBSCO; cached discovery abstract was truncated.

effect_name: 40-second interval overestimation
effect_claim: Women of childbearing age tend to verbally overestimate a 40-second interval.
effect_claim_quote: All age groups overestimated the 40-sec. time interval.
original_title: Norm Setting for the Verbal Estimation of a 40-Second Interval by Women of Childbearing Age
replication_title: Women's Verbal Estimation of a 40-Second Interval during the First Week Postpartum : a Replication
replication_target_quote: In this replication research 49 mothers verbally estimated a 40-sec. interval
outcome_quote: Throughout this postpartum period mothers overestimated the time interval.
review_note: Same lead author and exact 40-second verbal estimation protocol; replication paper references the original norm-setting article in its publisher preview. The reported 1987 research date appears to precede the original 1988 publication.

effect_name: Herd-immunity explanation increases vaccination intentions
effect_claim: Explaining herd immunity increases willingness to vaccinate.
effect_claim_quote: Communicating the concept of herd immunity improved willingness to vaccinate, especially in cultures lacking this prosocial cultural background.
original_title: On the benefits of explaining herd immunity in vaccine advocacy
replication_title: Social nudges for vaccination: How communicating herd behaviour influences vaccination intentions
replication_target_quote: This Registered Report attempted to conceptually replicate the finding that communicating herd immunity increases vaccination intentions (Betsch, et al., 2017, Nat. Hum. Behav., 0056).
outcome_quote: Compared to the control, communicating social benefits of herd immunity was effective in increasing vaccination intentions (F(1,541) = 6.97, p = .009, Partial Eta-Squared = 0.013).
review_note: Conceptual UK replication used a fictitious disease and self-reported intentions, not observed vaccination.

effect_name: Age pattern in moral-story judgments
effect_claim: Moral judgments of cartoon action sequences change with age, with motive criteria becoming more prominent in older children.
effect_claim_quote: the motive criterion becoming more dominant and differentiated with age.
original_title: ON THE ONTOGENETIC DEVELOPMENT OF MORAL CRITERIA
replication_title: Rating scale vs. pair comparison in moral judgment: A replication of the study by von Wright & Niemelä (1966) with a different method
replication_target_quote: The eight moral story‐cartoons used by von Wright & Niemelä (1966)
outcome_quote: closer to the order of 13‐year‐olds than to that of the seven‐year‐olds.
review_note: Exact von Wright and Niemelä (1966) story cartoons and explicit citation; 4–6-year-olds using a rating scale resembled the original older age groups, suggesting method-dependent age pattern.

effect_name: Reading racetracks improve sight-word fluency
effect_claim: Reading racetrack practice increases correct sight-word reading and reduces errors in elementary students.
effect_claim_quote: The results indicated that during the reading racetrack intervention all of the participants more than doubled their correct rate in oral reading.
original_title: The Effects of Reading Racetracks on the Sight Word Acquisition and Fluency of Elementary Students
replication_title: The Effects of Reading Racetracks on the Sight Word Fluency and Acquisition for Two Elementary Students with Disabilities: A Further Replication and Analysis
replication_target_quote: The purpose of this research was to determine the effectiveness of reading racetracks on the sight word acquisition and fluency of two elementary students who qualified for special education services.
outcome_quote: The overall outcomes indicated an increase in the acquisition and fluency of sight words and a decrease in errors.
review_note: The 2009 primary full text explicitly says it replicates and extends Rinaldi et al. [12], with exact 1997 title in references; outcome is from the article abstract.

effect_name: Immediate self-correction improves spelling
effect_claim: Correcting each attempted word immediately improves spelling acquisition and retention compared with correcting after a ten-word list.
effect_claim_quote: An alternating treatments design showed self-correction after each word to be more effective for acquisition of new spelling words
original_title: When to Self-Correct?: A Comparison of Two Procedures on Spelling Performance
replication_title: When to Self-Correct Spelling Words: A Systematic Replication
replication_target_quote: This investigation examined the comparative effects of self-correction after attempting each word and self-correction after attempting a list of 10 words
outcome_quote: An alternating treatments design showed self-correction after each word to be more effective for (a) acquisition of new spelling words as measured by weekly spelling tests for five of the six students
review_note: The Springer replication page cites Morton, Heward, and Alber (1998) with the same title and paradigm; Alber is a shared author. Five of six students showed acquisition gain and all six retention gain.

effect_name: Educational gains are specific rather than general
effect_claim: Education is associated with improvements in specific cognitive test skills rather than a general increase in cognitive ability.
effect_claim_quote: the association of education with improved cognitive test scores is not mediated by g, but consists of direct effects on specific cognitive skills.
original_title: Is education associated with improvements in general cognitive ability, or in specific skills?
replication_title: The Generality of Educational Effects on Cognitive Ability: A Replication
replication_target_quote: We used the structural equation models from Ritchie, Bates & Deary (2015)
outcome_quote: Our results were consistent with theirs in that we found that the effect of education on intelligence test scores was not an improvement to intelligence itself, but instead was relegated to improvements to specific skills.
review_note: Preprint. The later study explicitly names Ritchie, Bates and Deary (2015), reuses their structural equation models on a new longitudinal sample, and reports the same specific-skills rather than general-ability result.

effect_name: Physical warmth increases judged interpersonal warmth
effect_claim: Briefly holding a warm rather than cold beverage led people to judge another person as having a warmer personality.
effect_claim_quote: participants who briefly held a cup of hot (versus iced) coffee judged a target person as having a "warmer" personality
original_title: Experiencing Physical Warmth Promotes Interpersonal Warmth
replication_title: Physical and social warmth
replication_target_quote: Williams and Bargh (2008; Study 1) found that individuals holding a cup of warm beverage perceived the individuals they faced as psychologically warmer
outcome_quote: We found no main effect of physical warmth
review_note: The replication names Williams and Bargh 2008 Study 1 and reports no main effect.

effect_name: Infant algebraic rule learning
effect_claim: Seven-month-old infants generalize abstract rules across novel syllable sequences.
effect_claim_quote: 7-month-old infants attend longer to sentences with unfamiliar structures than to sentences with familiar structures
original_title: Rule Learning by Seven-Month-Old Infants
replication_title: ManyBabies 3: A Multi‐Lab Study of Infant Algebraic Rule Learning
replication_target_quote: Marcus et al. (1999) reported that 7-month-old infants learned abstract rules over syllable sequences
outcome_quote: The current study therefore finds no evidence for rule-learning
review_note: Registered multi-lab conceptual replication with 650 analyzed infants; the original is explicitly named.

effect_name: Power posing changes hormones and risk taking
effect_claim: Holding an expansive power pose increases testosterone and risk tolerance while reducing cortisol.
effect_claim_quote: High-power posers experienced elevations in testosterone, decreases in cortisol, and increased feelings of power and tolerance for risk
original_title: Power Posing
replication_title: The effects of power posing on neuroendocrine levels and risk-taking
replication_target_quote: attempted to replicate the original findings regarding the effects of power posing on testosterone and cortisol levels, risk-taking behavior, and perceived power
outcome_quote: Power posing was not found to replicate the original results regarding effects on testosterone levels or feelings of power; however, our findings partially supported the original results regarding effects on cortisol levels and risk-taking.
review_note: The original multicomponent claim is tested directly; rep results are mixed across its components.

effect_name: American flag priming of Republican attitudes
effect_claim: Brief exposure to the American flag shifts political attitudes toward Republicanism.
effect_claim_quote: a brief exposure to the American flag led to a shift toward Republican beliefs, attitudes, and voting behavior
original_title: A Single Exposure to the American Flag Shifts Support Toward Republicanism up to 8 Months Later
replication_title: Has the Effect of the American Flag on Political Attitudes Declined Over Time? A Case Study of the Historical Context of American Flag Priming
replication_target_quote: consistent with the studies we originally published in 2011 (T. J. Carter et al., 2011b)
outcome_quote: American flag primes did create politically conservative shifts in attitudes and beliefs during the initial time period when data were collected (even excluding the published studies), but this effect has since declined over time to be roughly zero
review_note: Later report is a meta-analysis of additional published and unpublished direct and conceptual replications from the original labs; initial effect appeared but later estimates approached zero.

effect_name: Attention-shift account of the Simon effect
effect_claim: A horizontal attention shift creates a spatial code underlying the Simon effect.
effect_claim_quote: a spatial compatibility effect will be observed if the last step in attentional focussing of the stimulus attribute specifying the response is a horizontal or a vertical attention shift
original_title: Attentional focussing and spatial stimulus-response compatibility
replication_title: Attention shifts and the Simon effect: a failure to replicate Stoffer (1991)
replication_target_quote: Three experiments were performed to examine further the attention-shift hypothesis forwarded by Stoffer
outcome_quote: Experiment 1 was an attempt to replicate Stoffer (1991), but failed to do so.
review_note: Rep explicitly identifies Stoffer 1991 and reports three failed tests of the attention-shift account.

effect_name: Mere exposure increases liking
effect_claim: Repeated exposure to nonsense words increases positive meaning ratings.
effect_claim_quote: the effect of experimentally manipulated frequency of exposure upon the affective connotation of nonsense words and symbols
original_title: Attitudinal effects of mere exposure
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Attitudinal effects of mere exposure: A replication and extension
replication_target_quote: Zajonc’s (1968) study that demonstrated that rated “goodness”-of-meaning of nonsense words is a positive function of exposure frequency
outcome_quote: both a replication condition and an experimental condition that deleted one of the aural sources of input yielded the same function (p<.025)
review_note: Rep explicitly names Zajonc 1968 and reports the same exposure-frequency function in both conditions.

effect_name: Achievement-goal priming improves performance
effect_claim: Priming achievement words without awareness improves later task performance.
effect_claim_quote: priming of the goal to perform well caused participants to perform comparatively better on an intellectual task.
original_title: The automated will: Nonconscious activation and pursuit of behavioral goals.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Nonconscious Activation of Behavioral Goals, a Methodologically Refined Replication
replication_target_quote: In four of the five experiments presented by Bargh and colleagues
outcome_quote: findings that the achievement content is responsible for the priming effect were confirmed.
review_note: Word-class confound controlled in online replication.

effect_name: Glucose drink improves later self-control
effect_claim: A glucose drink can improve performance after a self-control demand.
effect_claim_quote: consuming a glucose drink eliminated these impairments.
original_title: Self-control relies on glucose as a limited energy source: Willpower is more than a metaphor
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: A successful test of parallel replication teams in teaching research methods
replication_target_quote: Four teams, of five undergraduates each, independently attempted exact replications of Study 8 by Gailliot et al. (2007)
outcome_quote: its main result was replicated, since self–control overall was raised by the lucose drink.
review_note: Glucose main effect was female-only; depletion writing had no effect.

effect_name: Gain versus loss framing changes risk choice
effect_claim: Equivalent disease outcomes framed as lives saved or lost produce different risky choices.
effect_claim_quote: Reversals of preference are demonstrated in choices regarding monetary outcomes, both hypothetical and real, and in questions pertaining to the loss of human lives.
original_title: The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice
replication_title: Replicating the Disease framing problem during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic: A study of stress, worry, trust, and choice under risk
replication_target_quote: we investigated how stress, concerns, and trust moderated the effect in the Disease problem
outcome_quote: risk aversion and the framing effect in our study were larger than under typical circumstances.
review_note: Original disease problem tested during COVID-19.

effect_name: Facial feedback changes cartoon humor ratings
effect_claim: Facilitating a smile increases rated cartoon humor compared with inhibiting a smile.
effect_claim_quote: Subjects reported more intense humor responses when cartoons were presented under facilitating conditions than under inhibiting conditions
original_title: Inhibiting and facilitating conditions of the human smile: A nonobtrusive test of the facial feedback hypothesis.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Attention to Emotion and Non-Western Faces: Revisiting the Facial Feedback Hypothesis
replication_target_quote: In a modified replication of Strack, Martin, and Stepper's demonstration of the Facial Feedback Hypothesis (1988)
outcome_quote: the effect was not present in individuals with high Attention to Emotion.
review_note: Ghana sample shows facial feedback only at low attention to emotion.

effect_name: Practice amount separates violinist skill levels
effect_claim: Accumulated deliberate practice differs by violinist skill level.
effect_claim_quote: Individual differences, even among elite performers, are closely related to assessed amounts of deliberate practice.
original_title: The role of deliberate practice in the acquisition of expert performance
replication_title: The role of deliberate practice in expert performance: revisiting Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Römer (1993)
replication_target_quote: We sought to replicate Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Römer's (Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Römer 1993 Psychol. Rev. 100 , 363–406) seminal study on deliberate practice.
outcome_quote: We did not replicate the core finding that accumulated amounts of deliberate practice corresponded to each skill level.
review_note: Methodological replication reports smaller overall practice-performance association.

effect_name: Retroactive affective priming
effect_claim: A future affective prime influences response speed to a previously seen target.
effect_claim_quote: retroactive priming; retroactive habituation
original_title: Feeling the future: Experimental evidence for anomalous retroactive influences on cognition and affect.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Behavioural and EEG correlates of forward and backward priming—An exploratory study
replication_target_quote: Bem introduced a backward priming paradigm in 2011
outcome_quote: We did not replicate Bem's backward priming results.
review_note: Conventional forward priming reproduced, backward priming absent.

effect_name: Own name breaks through selective listening
effect_claim: People sometimes detect their own name in an ignored speech stream during selective listening.
effect_claim_quote: The only stimulus so far found that will break through this barrier is the subject's own name.
original_title: Attention in Dichotic Listening: Affective Cues and the Influence of Instructions
replication_title: Equivalent Processing of Self-Relevant Information in Autism: Evidence from the Cocktail Party Phenomenon
replication_target_quote: Here we present a preregistered replication of the cocktail party phenomenon in autism.
outcome_quote: 13 of 48 participants in the autistic group (27%) and 18 of 50 participants in the neurotypical group (36%) reported hearing their own name in the to-be-ignored message
review_note: Replication article explicitly names Moray (1959); same dichotic-listening effect.

effect_name: Stress and 5-HTTLPR interact in depression
effect_claim: The 5-HTTLPR variant moderates the association between stressful events and depression symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: A functional polymorphism in the promoter region of the serotonin transporter (5-HT T) gene was found to moderate the influence of stressful life events on depression.
original_title: Influence of life stress on depression: moderation by a polymorphism in the 5-HTT gene
replication_title: Interaction between serotonin transporter polymorphism (5-HTTLPR) and stressful life events in adolescents' trajectories of anxious/depressed symptoms.
replication_target_quote: Caspi et al. (2003) found an interaction between the serotonin transporter polymorphism gene (5-HTTLPR) and stressful life events on depression.
outcome_quote: Analyses demonstrated a G × E interaction in predicting the development of anxious/depressed symptoms.
review_note: Adolescent longitudinal study modifies genotype coding with rs25531.

effect_name: IKEA effect in children's vegetable snacks
effect_claim: Children should like self-crafted vegetable snacks more than similar snacks they did not craft.
effect_claim_quote: the increase in valuation of self‐made products
original_title: The IKEA effect: When labor leads to love
replication_title: Self-crafting vegetable snacks: testing the IKEA-effect in children
replication_target_quote: 86 children aged four to six either crafted a peacock with vegetables or with non-food objects
outcome_quote: No significant main effect of the vegetable snack creation on consumption and liking was observed.
review_note: Publisher article names Norton et al. 2012; child study tests the same self-creation valuation effect with edible products.

effect_name: Red cue impairs achievement performance
effect_claim: Brief exposure to red before an achievement task lowers task performance.
effect_claim_quote: the brief perception of red prior to an important test (e.g., an IQ test) impairs performance
original_title: Color and psychological functioning: The effect of red on performance attainment.
replication_title: Functional Equivalence of the Color Red and Enacted Avoidance Behavior?
replication_target_quote: The purpose of the present research was to both replicate and empirically integrate prior work on red and enacted avoidance behavior.
outcome_quote: Both experiments replicated prior research in each literature, with red and enacted avoidance behavior producing comparable effects across both experiments.
review_note: Replication full text explicitly names Elliot et al. (2007) as the red-in-achievement original; anagram performance and local processing were tested.

effect_name: Disfluent fonts improve analytic problem solving
effect_claim: Hard-to-read font increases correct responses on counterintuitive reasoning problems.
effect_claim_quote: receiving information in a degraded font (Experiments 1 and 4)
original_title: Overcoming intuition: Metacognitive difficulty activates analytic reasoning.
replication_title: Disfluent fonts don’t help people solve math problems.
replication_target_quote: The most famous demonstration showed that participants were more likely to solve counterintuitive math problems when they were printed in hard-to-read font.
outcome_quote: we find no effect on solution rates.
review_note: Replication manuscript explicitly names Alter et al. (2007) and pools 16 attempts on the original font/Cognitive Reflection Test claim.

effect_name: Vulnerable narcissism predicts hostile attribution
effect_claim: Vulnerable, but not grandiose, narcissism is linked to hostile interpretations of ambiguous actions.
effect_claim_quote: we found a consistent link between vulnerable narcissism and hostile attribution bias.
original_title: Assuming the worst: Hostile attribution bias in vulnerable narcissists
replication_title: Hostile Attribution Biases in Vulnerable Narcissists Depends on the Socio-Relational Context
replication_target_quote: we replicated and extended previous work linking vulnerable, but not grandiose, narcissism to hostile attributions
outcome_quote: We replicated previous research indicating a relationship between vulnerable narcissism and hostile attribution bias, but shed new light on the phenomenon of this bias in that it appears to depend on the socio-relational context and the level of ambiguity of the situation.
review_note: Replication full text cites Hansen-Brown & Freis (2021), the exact offered original; association is context-dependent.

effect_name: Erotic cues increase men's temporal discounting
effect_claim: Men exposed to attractive women or erotic cues choose more immediate rewards.
effect_claim_quote: discounting increased significantly in men who viewed attractive women
original_title: Do pretty women inspire men to discount the future?
original_journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
replication_title: Erotic cue exposure increases physiological arousal, biases choices toward immediate rewards, and attenuates model‐based reinforcement learning
replication_target_quote: Erotic cue exposure increased discounting as reflected by more impatient choices.
outcome_quote: Our findings replicate previous work on cue-reactivity effects in temporal discounting
review_note: Replication full text uses Wilson & Daly (2004) findings for power analysis and tests same heterosexual-male cue/discounting effect.

effect_name: Red increases perceived male attractiveness
effect_claim: A red background or red clothing increases women’s ratings of men’s attractiveness.
effect_claim_quote: women perceive men to be more attractive and sexually desirable when seen on a red background and in red clothing
original_title: Red, rank, and romance in women viewing men.
replication_title: Men in red: A reexamination of the red-attractiveness effect
replication_target_quote: Elliot, Kayser, Greitemeyer, Lichtenfeld, Gramzow, Maier, and Liu (Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 139(3), 399-417, 2010)
outcome_quote: We did not find any significant impact of red in either of the studies.
review_note: Close replication used the same photograph and red/white background as the first original experiment; a second study varied clothing.

effect_name: Expected talker variability slows speech recognition
effect_claim: Expecting two talkers creates a speech processing cost even with acoustically similar stimuli.
effect_claim_quote: Listeners expecting to hear 2 different talkers differing only slightly in average pitch showed performance costs typical of adjusting to talker variability
original_title: Acoustic differences, listener expectations, and the perceptual accommodation of talker variability.
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
replication_title: Listener expectations and the perceptual accommodation of talker variability: A pre-registered replication
replication_target_quote: Magnuson & Nusbaum, 2007
outcome_quote: we did not observe multitalker processing costs in either of our groups
review_note: Registered report explicitly identifies Magnuson and Nusbaum 2007 and tests the expectation manipulation; no processing cost was observed.

effect_name: Random VVIQ format lowers reported imagery vividness
effect_claim: The random VVIQ item order produced higher scores, indicating less vivid reported imagery, than the blocked order.
effect_claim_quote: Mean scores were significantly higher (less vivid imagery was reported) and split‐half reliability significantly lower with the random (0–692) than blocked (0–893) grouping
original_title: Effects of format of the Vividness of Visual Imagery Questionnaire on content validity, split‐half reliability, and the role of memory in test‐retest reliability
replication_title: Effects of format on the distribution of scores on the Vividness of Visual Imagery Questionnaire: A replication and extension
replication_target_quote: These results replicate McKelvie's (1986) finding that imagery was reported to be less vivid with the random (M = 2.35) than with the blocked (M = 2.14) VVIQ
outcome_quote: These results replicate McKelvie's (1986) finding that imagery was reported to be less vivid with the random (M = 2.35) than with the blocked (M = 2.14) VVIQ

effect_name: Articulation ease correlates with phoneme acquisition
effect_claim: Adult ratings of consonant articulation ease were positively associated with how early children mastered those phonemes.
effect_claim_quote: Ease ratings were positively correlated with Templin’s data (1957) on three-year-old children’s degree of mastery of these same phonemes.
original_title: Ease of Articulation
original_journal: Journal of Speech and Hearing Research
replication_title: Ease of articulation: A replication
replication_target_quote: the results of a direct replication of a study by Locke (1972) regarding ease of articulation.
outcome_quote: We obtained a very high positive correlation between our phoneme rankings and rankings obtained in the original study for the second method.

effect_name: Life event stress reduces working memory capacity
effect_claim: Greater negative life event stress was associated with poorer working memory capacity.
effect_claim_quote: Participants with more life event stress performed more poorly on Turner and Engle's ( 1989 ) operation‐word span WM task
original_title: The relationship of life event stress and working memory capacity
replication_title: An individual differences investigation of the relations among life event stress, working memory capacity, and mind wandering: A preregistered replication-extension study
replication_target_quote: Klein and Boals (2001a, Applied Cognitive Psychology, 15[5], 565-579, Experiments 1 and 2) found that working memory capacity correlated negatively with perceived negative life event stress
outcome_quote: we found no evidence suggesting that perceived negative life stress is associated with working memory capacity.

effect_name: Face encoding ERP speed relates to face cognition accuracy
effect_claim: Faster N170 face encoding and ERE/N250 access to face representations were associated with more accurate face cognition.
effect_claim_quote: The ability of face cognition accuracy was moderately related to neurocognitive indicators of structural face encoding (latency of the N170) and of activating representations of both faces and person-related knowledge (latencies and amplitudes of the early and late repetition effects, ERE/N250 and LRE/N400, respectively).
original_title: Individual Differences in Face Cognition: Brain–Behavior Relationships
replication_title: Neurocognitive mechanisms of individual differences in face cognition: A replication and extension
replication_target_quote: Herzmann, Kunina, Sommer, & Wilhelm, 2010
outcome_quote: We replicated the links of the ERP components indicating the speed of structural face encoding (N170 latency) and access to structural representations in memory (early repetition effect [ERE]/N250r) with the accuracy and speed of face cognition

effect_name: Family expressed emotion and schizophrenia relapse
effect_claim: A relative’s high expressed emotion predicts relapse after psychiatric discharge.
effect_claim_quote: The expressed emotion of the relative again seems to be associated with relapse independently of all other social and clinical factors investigated.
original_title: The Influence of Family and Social Factors on the Course of Psychiatric Illness
replication_title: The relationship between relative's Expressed Emotion and schizophrenic relapse: an Australian replication
replication_target_quote: investigating the association between the Expressed Emotion (EE) status of the household to which the patient is discharged and schizophrenic relapse.
outcome_quote: There was a significant association between returning to a high EE household and both re-hospitalisation and relapse.
review_note: Publisher page cites Vaughn and Leff 1976 by title; Sydney cohort reproduced the expressed-emotion/relapse association, especially in specified subgroups.

effect_name: Individual mastery criteria speed tact acquisition
effect_claim: Applying mastery criteria to individual targets speeds tact acquisition compared with set-level criteria.
effect_claim_quote: the target mastery criterion required fewer sessions of tact training for 3 of 5 participants
original_title: Comparison of mastery criteria applied to individual targets and stimulus sets on acquisition of tacts, intraverbals, and listener responses
replication_title: Applying “Mastery” Criteria to Sets and Individual Operants: A Replication with Preschoolers with Disabilities
replication_target_quote: applying acquisition "mastery" criteria to individual operants speeds a child’s acquisition of listener responses, tacts, intraverbals, and textual responses.
outcome_quote: Overall, most participants learned faster in the OA condition and maintenance was comparable between conditions.
review_note: Publisher reference list cites Cordeiro et al. 2022 DOI 10.1002/jaba.946; replicated individual-versus-set mastery comparison in preschoolers.

effect_name: Individual mastery criteria speed tact acquisition
effect_claim: Applying mastery criteria to individual targets speeds tact acquisition compared with set-level criteria.
effect_claim_quote: the target mastery criterion required fewer sessions of tact training for 3 of 5 participants
original_title: Comparison of mastery criteria applied to individual targets and stimulus sets on acquisition of tacts, intraverbals, and listener responses
replication_title: Comparison of Acquisition Criteria Applied to Individual and Sets of Tacts: A Systematic Replication
replication_target_quote: two different levels of acquisition criteria—Set and Operant Analysis—to assess acquisition and response maintenance of tact operants
outcome_quote: All participants required fewer instructional trials to acquire tacts under the Operant Analysis condition.
review_note: Publisher reference list cites Cordeiro et al. 2022 DOI 10.1002/jaba.946; systematic replication of individual-versus-set mastery comparison.

effect_name: Gender difference in interest in mixed-gender threesomes
effect_claim: Men report greater interest in mixed-gender threesomes than women.
effect_claim_quote: Compared to the women, the men reported significantly more positive attitudes and greater interest
original_title: Heterosexual Young Adults’ Interest, Attitudes, and Experiences Related to Mixed-Gender, Multi-Person Sex
replication_title: Exploring Variations in North American Adults’ Attitudes, Interest, Experience, and Outcomes Related to Mixed-Gender Threesomes: A Replication and Extension
replication_target_quote: The present study investigated attitudes toward, interest in, experiences with, and outcomes of MGTs in two samples
outcome_quote: Men, sexual minority individuals, and participants from the online sample reported more favorable attitudes toward and greater interest in MGTs as compared to women
review_note: Same lead author; publisher reference list cites Thompson and Byers original DOI 10.1007/s10508-016-0699-1 (online 2016, print 2017); rep uses larger college and online samples.

effect_name: Effectiveness of embedded discrete trial teaching
effect_claim: Both traditional and activity-embedded discrete trial teaching improve receptive skills in autistic learners.
effect_claim_quote: traditional and embedded DTT were equally effective and efficient
original_title: Teaching Receptive Discriminations to Children With Autism: A Comparison of Traditional and Embedded Discrete Trial Teaching
replication_title: Comparison of Traditional and Embedded Discrete Trial Teaching on the Acquisition of Receptive Identification Skills: A Systematic Replication in Adults with Autism
replication_target_quote: These results replicated and extended the results of Geiger et al. (Behav Anal Pract 5(2):49–59, 2012. 10.1007/bf03391823)
outcome_quote: The percentage of correct responses improved with the introduction of both types of DTT
review_note: Rep explicitly cites Geiger et al. 2012 and its exact DOI. Both formats improved correct responses; relative efficiency differed from the child sample because embedded teaching reached criterion faster but required longer sessions in adults.

effect_name: It's Your Game delays sexual initiation
effect_claim: The It's Your Game middle-school curriculum reduces sexual initiation by ninth grade.
effect_claim_quote: students in the comparison condition were 1.29 times more likely to initiate sex by the ninth grade
original_title: It's Your Game: Keep It Real: Delaying Sexual Behavior with an Effective Middle School Program
replication_title: Replication of It’s Your Game…Keep It Real! in Southeast Texas
replication_target_quote: To test the effectiveness of It’s Your Game…Keep It Real! (IYG)
outcome_quote: There were no significant differences in initiation of vaginal or oral sex between study conditions at follow-up.
review_note: Same named IYG program and ninth-grade behavioral endpoint; effectiveness trial in 20 new schools did not reproduce the original efficacy trial's behavioral result.

effect_name: Teaching interaction outperforms social stories
effect_claim: The teaching interaction procedure teaches social skills to autistic children more effectively than social stories.
effect_claim_quote: The teaching interaction procedure resulted in mastery of all 18 skills across the 6 participants.
original_title: COMPARING THE TEACHING INTERACTION PROCEDURE TO SOCIAL STORIES FOR PEOPLE WITH AUTISM
replication_title: Comparing the Teaching Interaction Procedure to Social Stories: A Replication Study
replication_journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
replication_target_quote: This study compared the teaching interaction procedure to social stories implemented in a group setting
outcome_quote: The results indicated that the teaching interaction procedure was more efficacious than the social story procedure across all three participants.
review_note: Same named procedures and outcome, independent participants; replication has Leaf author overlap with original.

effect_name: Binge eating disorder predicts greater psychopathology than overeating
effect_claim: Obese women meeting binge eating disorder criteria show greater eating-related and general psychopathology than overeaters without loss of control.
effect_claim_quote: The results support the idea that binge eaters might be a distinct subgroup among the obese population
original_title: Eating related and general psychopathology in obese females with binge eating disorder
replication_title: Binge eating disorder versus overeating: A failure to replicate and common factors in severely obese treatment seeking women
replication_journal: Eating and Weight Disorders - Studies on Anorexia Bulimia and Obesity
replication_target_quote: obese women diagnosed with Binge Eating Disorder (BED) and obese women who overeat (OE) are examined.
outcome_quote: MANOVAs revealed very few significant differences between the groups.
review_note: The 2003 replication cites the exact 1994 original in PubMed references (PMID 8124326); sample is severely obese treatment seekers, a narrower clinical population.

effect_name: Distinct depression and alcohol-misuse trajectories in emerging adults
effect_claim: Emerging adults follow distinct joint depression and alcohol-misuse trajectories, including a high-risk comorbid subgroup.
effect_claim_quote: Our findings show that the co-development of depression and alcohol misuse after university is not uniform.
original_title: Examining co-patterns of depression and alcohol misuse in emerging adults following university graduation
replication_title: Examining Subgroups of Depression and Alcohol Misuse in Emerging Adults During University: a Replication and Extension Study
replication_journal: International Journal of Mental Health and Addiction
replication_target_quote: We aimed to replicate and extend this study with emerging adults during university
outcome_quote: Class 1, the “high-risk comorbid” group, had high stable depression and high stable alcohol misuse (n = 28).
review_note: Replica explicitly identifies Frohlich et al. 2018 and exact DOI in its paper, and says it replicated three of four classes. Same latent-class trajectory claim; different stage (during vs after university) and 3 vs 4 classes, so claim is restricted to subgroup heterogeneity and high-risk comorbid group.

effect_name: Color-based inhibition of return
effect_claim: A neutral distractor between color cue and target enables inhibition of return to a repeated color.
effect_claim_quote: the inhibition only occurs if a neutral, nontarget distractor color is presented
original_title: Color-based inhibition of return
replication_title: Inhibition of return to color: A replication and nonextension of Law, Pratt, and Abrams (1995)
replication_target_quote: Law, Pratt, and Abrams (1995) reported slower reaction times (RTs) when cue and target were the same color
outcome_quote: the inhibitory effect observed by Law et al. at the 900-msec ISI was present at—and did not vary in magnitude across—the range of ISIs tested
review_note: Rep reproduced the original 900-ms color inhibition, but contradicted its predicted time course and proposed mechanism.

effect_name: Multiple auditory responses in autistic children
effect_claim: Children with autism show multiple motor responses to a single sound.
effect_claim_quote: All of these children appeared to respond to sound more than once
original_title: Multiple response to sound in dysfunctional children
original_journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
replication_title: Condon's multiple-response phenomenon in severely dysfunctional children: An attempt at replication
replication_journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
replication_target_quote: attempt to replicate the findings of William Condon on multiple entrainment and dyssynchronous behavioral organization in autistic children
outcome_quote: No firm evidence of multiple-responding to single sound was found for the autistic or normal children.
review_note: Rep names William Condon and tests double-response and dyssynchrony; double-response failed, while some dyssynchrony remained.

effect_name: Operant responding despite free reward
effect_claim: Animals will perform operant responses for a reward even when the same reward is freely available.
effect_claim_quote: Pigeons pecked a response disk to gain access to grain rewards while identical grain was freely available
original_title: Animals Respond for Food in the Presence of Free Food
replication_title: Operant responding with free access to the reinforcer: A replication and extension
replication_target_quote: maintenance of operant responding in the presence of free access to the reinforcer
outcome_quote: The results replicated earlier research using food reinforcement and demonstrated that the same general results could be obtained with water reinforcement.
review_note: Publisher reference list cites Neuringer 1969 original by exact title; rep extended the free-reward operant effect to water.

effect_name: Fixed-ratio workload increases self-imposed time-outs
effect_claim: Self-imposed time-outs from fixed-ratio reinforcement increase as the response requirement rises.
effect_claim_quote: the duration of the extinction period is a function of the number of responses required for reinforcement
original_title: Time-out from Positive Reinforcement
replication_title: Time-out from fixed-ratio reinforcement: A systematic replication
replication_target_quote: systematic replication of the “FR-TO effect”
outcome_quote: escapes from a fixed-ratio increase as the work requirement is made more demanding
review_note: Publisher reference list cites Azrin 1961 original by exact title; same fixed-ratio time-out effect replicated under two session formats.

effect_name: Perceived rather than reported parental behavior differences
effect_claim: In these survey samples, group differences centered on perceptions of parents more than reported parental behavior.
effect_claim_quote: The results also suggest that the subjects' reactions to his parents behaviour may be more important than the parent behaviour considered alone.
original_title: Parental Background of Homosexual and Heterosexual Women
replication_title: Parental backgrounds of homosexual and heterosexual women: A cross-national replication
replication_target_quote: The parental backgrounds of British homosexual and heterosexual women were evaluated on the same questionnaires used with two similar United States samples.
outcome_quote: The consistent United States and British findings dealt with how the subjects perceived their parents rather than with how their parents acted toward them.
review_note: Same investigator and questionnaires in U.S. and British women; publisher reference list explicitly cites Siegelman 1974a original by exact title. Descriptive group comparison only; no causal inference about orientation.

effect_name: Lateral eye movements raise misinformation false memories
effect_claim: Lateral eye movements after witnessing an event increase susceptibility to misleading postevent information.
effect_claim_quote: eye movement participants were less accurate and were more susceptible to the misinformation effect than controls.
original_title: Lateral Eye Movements Increase False Memory Rates
replication_title: Do lateral eye movements increase susceptibility to misinformation? A registered replication
replication_target_quote: The primary findings of Houben et al. (2018) were that participants who completed the eye-movement exercise were less accurate on the recognition test than control participants
outcome_quote: number of misinformation responses,t(118) = 0.10, p = .920,d = 0.02, or number of robust false memories,t(118) = 0.11, p = .911, d = 0.02, between participants in the two conditions.
review_note: Registered direct replication with original materials; target named in Springer full text. N=120 vs original 82; no misinformation or false-memory difference.

effect_name: Cross-modal aesthetic sensitivity to complexity
effect_claim: Individual preferences for complexity in music and visual designs are uncorrelated.
effect_claim_quote: We found no significant correlation for any of the four attributes across sensory modalities, except for contour.
original_title: Evaluative judgment across domains: Liking balance, contour, symmetry and complexity in melodies and visual designs
replication_title: Reexamining the Association between Aesthetic Sensitivity to Musical and Visual Complexity
replication_target_quote: In a provocative recent study, Clemente et al. (2021) found that individual differences in aesthetic sensitivity to stimulus complexity in the musical domain were uncorrelated with those in the visual domain.
outcome_quote: With these modifications, reliable positive correlations indeed emerged between aesthetic sensitivities to complexity across domains
review_note: Conceptual replication changed timing and complexity operationalization; positive cross-modal correlation contradicts original null, not an exact-material replication.

effect_name: Plausibility shapes memory for truth and falsity
effect_claim: Plausibility changes how people classify previously presented statements as true or false.
effect_claim_quote: Our results show that Gilbert's 'truth bias' does not hold for implausible statements
original_title: Plausibility matters: A challenge to Gilbert's Spinozan account of belief formation
replication_title: Revisiting the Plausibility Effect in Remembering Truth and Falsity: An Analysis of Underlying Memory and Guessing Processes
replication_target_quote: In a study by Vorms and colleagues (2022), an interaction pattern between statement plausibility and veracity feedback on memory performance appeared
outcome_quote: We replicated the plausibility effect as an interaction between statement plausibility and veracity feedback on correct true/false attributions.
review_note: Observed plausibility-by-veracity pattern reproduced; model attributes it largely to expectation-consistent guessing and statement memory rather than a simple initial-encoding mechanism.

effect_name: Typicality adds little to category-verification speed
effect_claim: Category typicality has no unique effect on category-verification response time beyond category dominance.
effect_claim_quote: Typicality had no effect beyond its shared effect with the dominance measures except as a possible suppressor variable.
original_title: The roles of typicality, instance dominance, and category dominance in verifying category membership
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
replication_title: A reexamination of the roles of typicality and category dominance in verifying category membership.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
replication_target_quote: Four partiaI replications of Chumbley's (1986) speeded category verification experiments were performed
outcome_quote: contrary to Chumbley's findings, typicality produced significant effects in the 12 conditions used over the 4 experiments
review_note: Four partial replications explicitly identify Chumbley 1986. Significant independent typicality effects conflict with original null; category dominance also became order-dependent.

effect_name: Endogenous attention and the line-motion illusion
effect_claim: The line-motion illusion under the original cueing method reflects impletion rather than an endogenous attention gradient.
effect_claim_quote: Evidence in the present study favors, instead, an account in which the illusion is the result of an impletion process
original_title: The line-motion illusion: Attention or impletion?
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
replication_title: Endogenous attention and illusory line motion reexamined.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
replication_target_quote: P. Downing and A. Treisman's (1997) failure to replicate an effect of endogenous attention on the direction of illusory line motion (ILM) was reexamined.
outcome_quote: The endogenous effect disappeared when participants moved their eyes to the attended item, when there was no motivation to endogenously attend, and when the presentation methods of P. Downing and A. Treisman (1997) were used.
review_note: Same authors and original paradigm explicitly named. Original no-attention result recurred when original presentation was used, but endogenous attention affected line motion under modified methods; hence mixed mechanism result.

effect_name: Direct self-surveillance–sexual satisfaction link
effect_claim: Self-surveillance directly predicts sexual satisfaction in college women.
effect_claim_quote: body surveillance and body shame directly predicted sexual satisfaction
original_title: Potential implications of the objectification of women's bodies for women's sexual satisfaction
replication_title: Self-objectification and sexual satisfaction: A preregistered test of the replicability and robustness of Calogero & Thompson (2009) in a sample of U.S. women
replication_target_quote: replication of Calogero and Thompson (2009a), which reported a direct relationship between self-surveillance and sexual satisfaction
outcome_quote: failed to replicate the direct pathway between self-surveillance and sexual satisfaction
review_note: Preregistered replication explicitly identifies Calogero and Thompson 2009a and tests the same direct path in full and matched restricted samples. Original authors and title verified against Crossref DOI metadata. Replication supports an indirect route through body shame and sexual self-esteem but not the direct path.
